Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 1–4:

The explanation of the words of Allah, exalted is He and sanctified are His names: ﴿Ta, Sin, Mim.﴾ ﴿These are the verses of the Clear Book.﴾ ﴿We recite to you some of the news of Moses and Pharaoh in truth, for a people who believe.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: We have already explained earlier the interpretation of Allah's words ﴿Ta, Sin, Mim﴾, and we mentioned the disagreement of the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) regarding its meaning. As for His words ﴿These are the verses of the Clear Book﴾, He means: these are the verses of the Book which We have sent down to you, O Muhammad, which makes clear that it is from Allah, and that you did not invent it or fabricate it.

Qatadah, as is related from him, said regarding this:

Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to me, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Ta, Sin, Mim. These are the verses of the Clear Book﴾: it means "clear," by Allah's blessing, its guidance and its right direction.

* *

As for His words ﴿We recite to you﴾:

He says: We read to you, and We relate in this Qur'an the account of ﴿Moses and Pharaoh in truth﴾.

As:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿We recite to you some of the news of Moses and Pharaoh in truth, for a people who believe﴾: he says: in this Qur'an is their news.

* *

As for His words ﴿for a people who believe﴾:

He says: for a people who affirm this Book, so that they may know that what We recite to you of their news contains their news, and so that their souls may be reassured that Our way with those among the polytheists who oppose you and act hostilely toward you is the same as Our way with those who were hostile to Moses and those among the Children of Israel who believed in him, from Pharaoh and his people: that We destroy them as We destroyed them, and deliver them from them as We delivered them.

* *

The explanation of the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and made its people into factions, oppressing a group among them, slaughtering their sons and keeping their women alive. Indeed, he was among the corrupters.﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: Indeed Pharaoh acted arrogantly in the land of Egypt and was haughty, and he exalted himself over its people and subdued them, until they acknowledged servitude to him.

As:

Muhammad ibn Harun narrated to us, he said: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land﴾: he says: he acted arrogantly in the land.

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land﴾: that is, he transgressed in the land.

* *

As for His words ﴿and made its people into factions﴾:

By "shi'a" he means the sects: he says, and made its people into divided groups.

As Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿and made its people into factions﴾: that is, into groups; he slaughters one group of them, keeps another alive, tortures another, and enslaves another. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿slaughtering their sons and keeping their women alive. Indeed, he was among the corrupters.﴾

Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, he said: Amr narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Among the matters concerning Pharaoh was that he saw a dream in his sleep, that a fire came forth from Bayt al-Maqdis until it enveloped the houses of Egypt, burning the Copts and leaving the Children of Israel, and burning the houses of Egypt. So he summoned the sorcerers, the soothsayers, the physiognomists and the diviners [[Perhaps the original is al-Hazzah, with a damma on the ha, plural of al-Hazi, meaning the fortune-teller. In (Lisan: hazaa) tahazzi means to foretell, hazia hazyan, and tahazza: to foretell. We have not found the meaning of foretelling under the root (h-w-z). So what is in the text may be a copyist's error. What supports what we have said is that it will come later on page 8, line 23, correctly as we have said.]] and asked them about his dream. They said to him: A man will come forth from this city from which the Children of Israel came, meaning Bayt al-Maqdis, on whose account Egypt will be destroyed. So he commanded that no boy born to the Children of Israel be left alive but be slaughtered, and no girl be born to them but be spared. He said to the Copts: Look at your slaves who work outside, bring them in, and make the Children of Israel take over those filthy tasks. So he put the Children of Israel to work at the tasks of their slaves, and brought in their slaves. This is when He says: ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and made its people into factions﴾, meaning the Children of Israel, when he placed them in the filthy tasks.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and made its people into factions﴾: he said: he divided them.

al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿and made its people into factions﴾: he said: groups.

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿and made its people into factions﴾: the shi'a are the groups.

* *

As for His words ﴿oppressing a group among them﴾:

It is related that his oppression of them was enslaving them.

Those who said this:

al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Abu Sufyan narrated to me, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: he enslaves a group of them, slaughters a group, kills a group, and keeps a group alive.

* *

As for His words ﴿Indeed, he was among the corrupters﴾:

He says: indeed he was among those who corrupt the land by killing those who do not deserve to be killed by him, enslaving those he has no right to enslave, acting arrogantly over its people in the land, and being haughty toward the worship of his Lord.

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He:** ﴿And We wished to bestow favour upon those who were oppressed in the land, and to make them leaders and to make them the inheritors﴾ (28:5)

**His words: ﴿And We wished﴾**

This is coordinated with His words, ﴿he [Pharaoh] oppressed a group of them﴾ (28:4). The meaning of the statement is: Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and made its people, the Children of Israel, into factions, oppressing a group of them. ﴿And We wished to bestow favour upon those who﴾ Pharaoh had oppressed among the Children of Israel ﴿and to make them leaders﴾.

Those who practise ta'wil (interpretation, tafsir) have said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And We wished to bestow favour upon those who were oppressed in the land﴾, he said: "They are the Children of Israel."

* *

**His words: ﴿and to make them leaders﴾**

That is: governors and kings.

Those who practise ta'wil have said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and to make them leaders﴾, that is: rulers of the affair.

* *

And His words: ﴿and to make them the inheritors﴾

He says: And We will make them the heirs of the people of Pharaoh, inheriting the land after their destruction.

Those who practise ta'wil have said what we have said in the interpretation of this.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and to make them the inheritors﴾: that is, they will inherit the land after Pharaoh and his people.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and to make them the inheritors﴾, he said: "They will inherit the land after Pharaoh."

* *

And His words: ﴿And We will establish them in the land﴾

He says: And We will prepare for them a place in the land of Syria and Egypt. ﴿And We will show Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts﴾ — they had been informed that their destruction would be at the hand of a man from the Children of Israel, so they were apprehensive of them on account of that. For this reason Pharaoh used to slaughter their sons and spare their women. So God showed Pharaoh, Haman and their hosts, from among the Children of Israel, at the hand of Moses son of Imran, His prophet, what they had been fearing from them: their destruction and the ruin of their dwellings and homes.

As (narrated):

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And We will establish them in the land and show Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts from them that which they were fearing﴾: "something they had been wary of."

He said: It has been related to us that a soothsayer (hazi) foretold the enemy of God, Pharaoh, saying: "A boy will be born among the Children of Israel this year who will strip you of your kingdom." So Pharaoh pursued their sons that year, killing their sons and sparing their women, out of caution at what the soothsayer had told him.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: Pharaoh had a man who looked after him and informed him, meaning that he was a diviner (kahin). He said to him: "A boy will be born this year who will take your kingdom away from you." So Pharaoh used to slaughter their sons and spare their women, out of caution. This is His words: ﴿And We will show Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts from them that which they were fearing﴾.

The reciters differed over the reading of His words: ﴿And We will show Pharaoh and Haman﴾. The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz and Basra, and some of the Kufans, read it as ﴿وَنُرِيَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَامَانَ﴾ (wa-nuriya Fir'awna wa-Hamana) with the nun, meaning "and We will show," coordinating it with His words ﴿And We will establish them﴾. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as "وَيَرَى فِرْعَوْنُ" (wa-yara Fir'awnu), meaning that the verb belongs to Pharaoh: "and Pharaoh will see," with the yā' in yarā, and Pharaoh, Haman and the hosts in the nominative case.

The correct position on this matter is that both are well-known readings among the reciters of the regional centres, close in meaning. Scholars among the reciters have read each of them, so whichever reading the reciter uses is correct. This is because it is known that Pharaoh would not have seen from Moses what he saw except that God, mighty and majestic, showed it to him, and God, exalted is He and remembered, would not have shown him that from Moses unless he saw it.

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He:** ﴿And We wished to bestow favour upon those who were oppressed in the land, and to make them leaders and to make them the inheritors﴾ (28:5)

**His words: ﴿And We wished﴾**

This is coordinated with His words, ﴿he [Pharaoh] oppressed a group of them﴾ (28:4). The meaning of the statement is: Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and made its people, the Children of Israel, into factions, oppressing a group of them. ﴿And We wished to bestow favour upon those who﴾ Pharaoh had oppressed among the Children of Israel ﴿and to make them leaders﴾.

Those who practise ta'wil (interpretation, tafsir) have said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And We wished to bestow favour upon those who were oppressed in the land﴾, he said: "They are the Children of Israel."

* *

**His words: ﴿and to make them leaders﴾**

That is: governors and kings.

Those who practise ta'wil have said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and to make them leaders﴾, that is: rulers of the affair.

* *

And His words: ﴿and to make them the inheritors﴾

He says: And We will make them the heirs of the people of Pharaoh, inheriting the land after their destruction.

Those who practise ta'wil have said what we have said in the interpretation of this.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and to make them the inheritors﴾: that is, they will inherit the land after Pharaoh and his people.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and to make them the inheritors﴾, he said: "They will inherit the land after Pharaoh."

* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 7:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And We inspired to the mother of Moses, "Suckle him; but when you fear for him, then cast him into the yarn (al-yamm), and do not fear or grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers."﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And We inspired to the mother of Moses﴾ when she gave birth to Moses ﴿to suckle him﴾.

Qatadah used to say, regarding the meaning of that: ﴿And We inspired to the mother of Moses﴾ means: We cast it into her heart.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And We inspired to the mother of Moses﴾: a revelation that came to her from Allah, which He cast into her heart, and it is not prophetic revelation (wahy nubuwwah), "that you suckle Moses; and when you fear for him, then cast him into the yarn, and do not fear or grieve..." ... the verse.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to me, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning his saying: ﴿And We inspired to the mother of Moses﴾, he said: It was cast into her soul.

⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Pharaoh ordered that the male children born to the Children of Israel be slaughtered for one year and spared for a year. When it was the year in which they were to be slaughtered, she conceived Moses. When she was about to give birth to him, she grieved over his situation, so Allah inspired to her, ﴿"Suckle him; but when you fear for him, then cast him into the yarn"﴾.

The commentators differed concerning the circumstance in which the mother of Moses was commanded to cast Moses into the yarn. Some of them said: She was commanded to cast him into the yarn four months after his birth, for at that stage he asks for suckling more than a child does after leaving its mother's womb.

Those who said that:

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, concerning his saying: ﴿"Suckle him; but when you fear for him"﴾, he said: When he reaches four months and cries out, and seeks more suckling than that, ﴿"then cast him"﴾ at that time ﴿"into the yarn"﴾. That is His saying: ﴿"when you fear for him"﴾.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah, who said: He did not say to her: when you give birth to him, cast him into the yarn. Rather He said to her: ﴿"Suckle him; but when you fear for him, then cast him into the yarn"﴾. By this she was commanded. He said: She placed him in an orchard, and she would come to him every day and suckle him, and come to him every night and suckle him, and that sufficed him.

Others said: Rather, she was commanded to cast him into the yarn after her giving birth to him and after her suckling him.

Those who said that:

⁕ Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When she gave birth to him, she suckled him. Then she summoned a carpenter for him, who made him a chest (tabut), and the key of the chest was on the inside, and she placed him in it, and cast him into the yarn.

The most correct of what has been said regarding this, is that it should be said as He, His praise be exalted, said: that Allah, He, may His remembrance be exalted, commanded the mother of Moses to suckle him, and when she feared for him from the enemy of Allah, Pharaoh, and his soldiers, that she should cast him into the yarn. It is permissible that her fear of them was after months from her giving birth to him; whichever of these was the case, she did what Allah inspired to her regarding it, and there is no report establishing a proof, nor any rational indication, clarifying which of these was the case. So the most sound of the sayings regarding this is to say as He, may His majesty be exalted, said, and the yarn into which she was commanded to cast him is the Nile.

As:

⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿"cast him into the yarn (al-yamm)"﴾, he said: It is the sea, and it is the Nile. We have explained this with its evidences, and mentioned the reports concerning it previously, in a manner that suffices without repeating it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿"and do not fear or grieve"﴾

He says: Do not fear for your child from Pharaoh and his soldiers that they will kill him, and do not grieve over his separation.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿"and do not fear or grieve"﴾, he said: Do not fear for him the sea, and do not grieve over his separation; ﴿"Indeed, We will return him to you"﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿"Indeed, We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers"﴾

He says: Indeed We will return your child to you for suckling, so that you yourself will suckle him, and We will send him as a messenger to the one you fear will kill him; and Allah did that for her and for him.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, ﴿"Indeed, We will return him to you"﴾ and send him as a messenger to this tyrant, and [make] his destruction, and the deliverance of the Children of Israel from the affliction they were in at his hands.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 8:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then the family of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might be to them an enemy and a grief. Indeed, Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers were ever sinners.﴾ (28:8)

Say: His exalted remembrance says: "Then the family of Pharaoh picked him up," meaning they came upon him, found him and took him. Its root is from luqtah (that which is found lost and taken up), and the Arabs say: when something comes upon you suddenly, without you seeking it or intending it, "I found it iltiqatan (by chance)," and "I met so-and-so iltiqatan." Among this is the saying of the rajiz (rajaz poet):

"A watering place I came upon by chance... I did not meet, when I came upon it, any stragglers [of the flock]."

[These are two verses of mashtur rajaz, by Naqadah al-Asadi, which he cited in (Lisan al-Arab: lqt) and added to them a third verse: "except the pigeon and the sandgrouse (al-Ghattat)." He said: "And I met him iltiqatan" when you meet him without expecting or supposing him. Naqadah al-Asadi said: "A watering place I came upon..." the three verses. Sibawayh said: iltiqatan means suddenly, and it is among the verbal nouns that occur as circumstantial accusatives, like "he came running." And "I came upon the water and the thing iltiqatan" when you fall upon it abruptly and did not expect it. Ibn al-A'rabi related: "I met him laqatan": face to face. In a hadith of Umar, that a man from Tamim picked up a shabakah, and asked that it be made his. The shabakah: wells near the water. And its iltiqat: finding it without seeking it. End. He said under (frt): furat al-qata: those which go ahead of them to the valley and the water. He recited the verse and attributed it to Naqadah al-Asadi. (Under ghtt): al-Ghattat is the qata, with a fatha on the ghayn. It was said: a type of qata, its singular ghattatah. It was said: qata is of two kinds: the short-legged, yellow-necked, black-bodied... the ones with tawny flight feathers, namely the kadriyyah and the junziyyah (with the first letter vowelled), and the long-legged, white-bellied, dusty-backed, wide-eyed: these are the ghattat. It was said: al-Ghattat is a kind of bird, not of the qata; they are dusty in bellies, backs and bodies, black in wings. It was said: black underwings, long legs and necks, slender. End. Consult other sayings in (Lisan al-Arab: ghtt). The first verse is in (Mu'jam ma Ista'jam by al-Bakri, Cairo edition arranged by Mustafa al-Saqqa, p. 779). And in Sibawayh's Kitab (1:186).]] meaning suddenly.

The exegetes differed concerning the referent of His saying: ﴿the family of Pharaoh﴾ in this place. Some of them said: it means the female slaves of Pharaoh's wife.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Musa narrated to us, he said: Amr narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, he said: The waves brought the chest, lifting it once and lowering it another time, until they placed it among trees near the house of Pharaoh. The female slaves of Asiyah, Pharaoh's wife, came out to wash, and they found the chest and brought it into Asiyah, and they thought there was money in it. When Asiyah looked at it, mercy for him fell upon her and she loved him. When she informed Pharaoh of him, he wanted to slaughter him, but Asiyah kept speaking to him until he left him to her. He said: "I fear that this is one of the Children of Israel, and that the one at whose hands is our destruction is this one." That is the saying of God: ﴿Then the family of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might be to them an enemy and a grief.﴾

Others said: rather, it refers to the daughter of Pharaoh.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn Qays, he said: Pharaoh's daughter had leprosy. She came to the Nile, and there was the chest in the Nile, tossed by the waves. Pharaoh's daughter took it, and when she opened the chest, there was a child. When she looked at his face she was cured of the leprosy. She brought him to her mother and said: "This child is blessed; when I looked at him I was healed." Pharaoh said: "This is one of the children of Israel; come, let me kill him." She said: ﴿The coolness of the eye for me and for you; do not kill him.﴾

Others said: it refers to Pharaoh's helpers.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, he said: Pharaoh rose one morning in a sitting that he used to hold each morning on the bank of the Nile. While he was seated, the Nile carried the chest, casting it forth, and Asiyah bint Muzahim, his wife, was sitting beside him. She said: "This is indeed something in the sea; bring it to me." His helpers went out to it until they brought it. The chest was opened, and in it there was a child in his cradle. God cast His love upon him and inclined his (Pharaoh's) soul toward him. His wife Asiyah said: ﴿Do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may take him as a son.﴾

We have no saying regarding this more correct than what God, mighty and majestic, has said: ﴿Then the family of Pharaoh picked him up﴾.

We have already explained the meaning of "the family" earlier sufficiently, so there is no need to repeat it here.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿that he might be to them an enemy and a grief﴾

One might say: that Musa would be to the family of Pharaoh an enemy and a grief, so they picked him up. It is said: when they picked him up, they did not pick him up for that purpose, but for what had preceded its mention; yet it (the outcome) will occur, if God wills.

As:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, concerning His saying: ﴿Then the family of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might be to them an enemy and a grief﴾: he said: that he would be, in the outcome of his affair, an enemy and a grief for them, according to what God intended for him. They did not take him for that; rather, Pharaoh's wife said: ﴿The coolness of the eye for me and for you.﴾ So God's saying: ﴿that he might be to them an enemy and a grief﴾ refers to what would come about in the outcome of his affair for them. It is like the saying of another, when he rebukes someone for an act which the doer thought was good, but which led to harm, and so he regrets it: "You did this to harm yourself, and you did it to harm yourself." The doer, in the state of doing it, was doing it hoping for benefit, but the outcome came contrary to what he hoped. Likewise His saying: ﴿Then the family of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might be to them an enemy and a grief﴾ means: the family of Pharaoh picked him up, thinking they were doing good to themselves, that he might be a coolness of the eye for them; but the outcome of their picking him up was their destruction at his hands.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿an enemy and a grief﴾

He says: he would be an enemy to them in their religion, and a grief over what befalls them from him of harm.

Those who spoke by the same as what we have said are the exegetes.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Bishr narrated to me, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿Then the family of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might be to them an enemy and a grief﴾: an enemy to them in their religion, and a grief over what comes to them.

The readers differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra, and some of the people of Kufa, recited: ﴿wa-hazanan﴾ with fatha on the ha and the za. The majority of the readers of Kufa recited "wa-huznan" with damma on the ha and sukun on the za. Al-hazan with fatha on the ha and za is a verbal noun of "hazintu hazanan," and al-huzn with damma on the ha and sukun on the za is the noun, like al-'adam and al-'udm, and the like.

The correct statement on this is that they are two recitations close in meaning; despite the difference in their wording they stand in the position of al-'adam and al-'udm, so whichever of them the reader recites is correct.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers were ever sinners﴾

His exalted remembrance says: Indeed, Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers were sinful toward their Lord, and therefore Musa was for them an enemy and a grief.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 9:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And the wife of Pharaoh said: "A comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may take him as a son," while they did not perceive.﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿And the wife of Pharaoh said﴾ — this, ﴿"A comfort of the eye for me and for you"﴾ — O Pharaoh. The phrase "a comfort of the eye" is in the nominative, governed by an implied element, which is "this," or "it is."

* *

And His saying: ﴿"Do not kill him"﴾

This is a request from Pharaoh's wife that he not be killed. It has been related that when the woman said this statement to Pharaoh, Pharaoh said: "As for you, yes; as for me, no." And so it was.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: Pharaoh's wife said: ﴿"A comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may take him as a son."﴾ Pharaoh said: "A comfort of the eye for you; as for me, no." Muhammad ibn Qays said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If Pharaoh had said, 'A comfort of the eye for me and for you,' it would have been for both of them together."

⁕ Musa related to us, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Pharaoh adopted him as a son, and he was called the son of Pharaoh. When the boy began to move, his mother Asiya showed him to a child, and while she was dandling him and playing with him, she handed him to Pharaoh and said: "Take him, a comfort of the eye for me and for you." Pharaoh said: "He is a comfort of the eye for you, not for me." Abdullah ibn Abbas said: If he had said, "And he is a comfort of the eye for me too," then he would have believed in him, but he refused.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada: Pharaoh's wife said: ﴿"A comfort of the eye for me and for you"﴾, meaning by that: Musa.

⁕ Al-Abbas ibn al-Walid related to us, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: al-Asbah ibn Yazid informed us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr related to me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When Pharaoh's wife brought Musa to Pharaoh, she said: ﴿"A comfort of the eye for me and for you."﴾ Pharaoh said: "It is for you; as for me, I have no need of him." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, if Pharaoh had acknowledged that he could be a comfort of the eye for him as she did, Allah would have guided him through him as He guided his wife, but Allah deprived him of that."

* *

And His saying: ﴿"Do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may take him as a son."﴾

It has been related that Pharaoh's wife said this statement when he intended to kill him. Some said: when he was brought to him on the day he was picked up from the river. Others said: on the day he plucked his beard, or struck him with a staff that was in his hand.

Mention of those who said she said it on the day he plucked his beard:

⁕ Musa related to us, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When Pharaoh was brought the boy, he took him to himself, and Musa seized his beard and plucked it. Pharaoh said: "Bring me the slaughterers; this is he!" Asiya said: ﴿"Do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may take him as a son."﴾ He is only a child who does not understand, and he did this out of his childishness.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada: ﴿"Do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may take him as a son."﴾ He said: Her mercy was cast upon him when she saw him.

* *

And His saying: ﴿"while they did not perceive"﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding its meaning. Some said: the meaning is: while they did not perceive their destruction at his hand.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada: ﴿"while they did not perceive"﴾ He said: while they did not perceive that their destruction would be at his hands, and in his time.

⁕ Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Sufyan related to me, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿"or we may take him as a son, while they did not perceive"﴾ He said: Their destruction is at his hands.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr related to us, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿"while they did not perceive"﴾ He said: The family of Pharaoh, he is their enemy.

And others said: rather, the meaning is: ﴿"while they did not perceive"﴾ what was to come of their affair and his.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Pharaoh's wife Asiya said: ﴿"Do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may take him as a son, while they did not perceive."﴾ Allah says: while they did not perceive, that is, what is to come by what Allah intended for him.

And others said: rather, the meaning of His saying: ﴿"while they did not perceive"﴾ is: the Children of Israel did not perceive that We had picked him up.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn Qays: ﴿"Do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may take him as a son, while they did not perceive."﴾ He said: He says: the Children of Israel did not know that We had picked him up.

The correct view on this matter is the view of those who said: the meaning is: and Pharaoh and his family did not perceive what was to come of their destruction at his hands.

We have said that this is the most preferable interpretation because it follows His saying: ﴿"And the wife of Pharaoh said: 'A comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may take him as a son.'"﴾ When that is what follows it, it is more fitting that it explain the statement that immediately precedes it than that it explain something else.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 10:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And the heart of Moses' mother became empty; she was about to disclose him, had We not fortified her heart so that she would be among the believers.﴾

The exegetes differed concerning the meaning which God intended when He said that the heart of Moses' mother became empty. Some of them said: What God, great is His praise, meant by the heart of Moses' mother becoming empty was: empty of everything except the remembrance of her son Moses.

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to me, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Mujahid and Hassan Abu al-Ashras, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿And the heart of Moses' mother became empty﴾: He said: emptied of everything except the remembrance of Musa.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Hassan, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿And the heart of Moses' mother became empty﴾: He said: empty of everything except the remembrance of Musa.

Muhammad ibn 'Ammarah narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from a man, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿And the heart of Moses' mother became empty﴾: He said: empty of everything except the concern for Musa.

'Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And the heart of Moses' mother became empty﴾: He said: it means: she does not remember anything but Musa.

Muhammad ibn 'Ammarah narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, ﴿And the heart of Moses' mother became empty﴾: He said: from everything other than the remembrance of Musa.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And the heart of Moses' mother became empty﴾: He said: emptied of everything except the remembrance of Musa.

'Abd al-Jabbar ibn Yahya al-Ramli narrated to us, saying: Damrah ibn Rabi'ah narrated to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, from Mutar, concerning His words ﴿And the heart of Moses' mother became empty﴾: He said: empty of everything except the concern of Musa.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿And the heart of Moses' mother became empty﴾: That is: idle from everything except the remembrance of Musa.

It was related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words ﴿And the heart of Moses' mother became empty﴾: He said: emptied of everything except the remembrance of Musa.

Others said: rather, He meant that her heart became empty of the revelation which God had revealed to her, when He commanded her to cast him into the river, and said ﴿Do not fear and do not grieve. We shall return him to you and make him one of the messengers﴾. He said: she grieved and forgot the covenant of God with her, so God, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿And the heart of Moses' mother became empty﴾ of Our revelation which We had revealed to her.

Those who said this:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿And the heart of Moses' mother became empty﴾: He said: empty of the revelation which God had revealed to her when He commanded her to cast him into the sea, and not to fear or grieve. He said: then Satan came to her and said: O mother of Musa, you disliked that Pharaoh should kill Musa, so that you would have his reward and recompense, and you yourself undertook his killing; you cast him into the sea and drowned him. So God said: ﴿And the heart of Moses' mother became empty﴾ of the revelation which He had revealed to her.

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah, saying: al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: she became empty of the covenant which We had made with her, and the promise which We had promised her, that We would return her son to her; so she forgot all of that, until she nearly disclosed him, had We not fortified her heart.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq said: Moses' mother used to watch for news of him after she had cast him into the sea, whether she would hear any mention of him, until news came to her that Pharaoh's people had found a baby in the Nile in the chest that morning; she recognised the description, and saw that he had fallen into the hands of the enemy from whom she had fled with him. Her heart became empty of the covenant of God with her concerning him, for the great trial had made her forget the covenant that she had with God concerning him.

Some scholars of the Arabic language said: the meaning is: ﴿And the heart of Moses' mother became empty﴾ of grief, because she knew that he had not drowned. He said: this is from their saying: "dam farigh" (blood that is spilled), i.e., void and wasted, unclaimed; there is no retaliation nor blood-money for it. This is a view that has no meaning, since it contradicts the saying of all the exegetes.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: the most correct of the opinions regarding this, in my view, is the saying of the one who said: its meaning is: ﴿And the heart of Moses' mother became empty﴾ of everything except the concern for Musa.

We said that this is the most correct of the opinions because of the indication of His words: ﴿she was about to disclose him, had We not fortified her heart﴾. Had He meant by that the emptiness of her heart of the revelation, He would not have followed it with ﴿she was about to disclose him﴾, for if she had been about to disclose the revelation, she would only have been about to do so because of her frequent remembrance of it and her passionate attachment to it. And it is impossible that there be such passion without constant remembrance.

Since this is so, the view that her heart was empty of what had been revealed to her is invalid. Furthermore, God, exalted is His remembrance, informed of her that she became empty-hearted, and did not specify the emptiness of her heart from one thing rather than another; so it is general, except for what is established by proof that her heart did not become empty of it. It has been reported from Fudalah ibn 'Ubayd that he used to recite it: "wa asbaha fu'adu ommi Musa fazi'an" (with a zayn), from fazaʿ (fright).

* *

As for His words: ﴿she was about to disclose him﴾

The exegetes differed concerning the referent of the pronoun in His words ﴿him [bihi]﴾. Some of them said: it refers to the mention of Musa, and it is to him that it returns.

Those who said this:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Mujahid and Hassan Abu al-Ashras, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿she was about to disclose him﴾: to say: "O my sons!"

He said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to me, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Hassan, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿she was about to disclose him﴾: to say: "O my sons!"

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Hassan, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿she was about to disclose him﴾: to say: "O my sons!"

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿she was about to disclose him﴾: that is, to disclose that he was her son out of intense grief.

Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: when his mother came, he took from her, meaning the suckling; she was about to say: "He is my son," but God protected her, and this is the saying of God: ﴿she was about to disclose him, had We not fortified her heart﴾.

Others said: with what We had revealed to her: that is, she would succeed.

The correct view on this matter is what those whose sayings we have mentioned said: that she was about to say, "O my sons!" This is because of the consensus of the authoritative exegetes upon it, and because it follows His words: ﴿And the heart of Moses' mother became empty﴾; and since those who said that it refers to Musa, being closest to him, were in consensus, that is more fitting than that it refer to the revelation.

Some said: rather, the meaning of ﴿she was about to disclose﴾ is about Musa, that she would say, "He is my son." They said: this is because her chest was constrained when he was attributed to Pharaoh and it was said: "the son of Pharaoh." By His words ﴿to disclose him﴾ is meant: to make him manifest and to inform of him.

The exegetes said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words ﴿she was about to disclose him﴾: to make him known.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿she was about to disclose him﴾: she would have announced his matter, had We not fortified her heart so that she would be among the believers.

* *

As for His words: ﴿had We not fortified her heart﴾

He says: had We not protected her from that by strengthening her and granting her success in keeping silent about it.

The exegetes said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: God said: ﴿had We not fortified her heart﴾: that is, with faith, ﴿so that she would be among the believers﴾.

Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: she was about to say, "He is my son," but God protected her, and this is the saying of God: ﴿she was about to disclose him, had We not fortified her heart﴾.

* *

As for His words: ﴿so that she would be among the believers﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: We protected her from making that manifest and uttering it with her tongue, and We strengthened her for the covenant that We had made with her, ﴿so that she would be among the believers﴾ in the promise of God, those who are certain of Him.

**The Commentary on the Words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And she said to his sister, "Follow him," so she watched him from a distance while they did not perceive﴾ (28:11)**

His saying, exalted is He, means: ﴿And she said﴾ the mother of Musa to the sister of Musa when she placed him in the river, ﴿"Follow him" (qussīhi)﴾, meaning: follow the trail of Musa, pursue his track. It is said: "I followed the traces of the people" (qaṣaṣtu āthār al-qawm) when I pursued their tracks.

Those who engage in tafsir (interpretation of the Qur'an, ahl al-ta'wīl) have said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, he said: Abu 'Asim told us, he said: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, he said: al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿to his sister, "Follow him"﴾: he said, "Follow his trail and see what they do with him."
- al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, ﴿"Follow him"﴾: i.e., follow his trail.
- Ibn Humayd told us: Salama told us, from Ibn Ishaq, ﴿And she said to his sister, "Follow him"﴾: he said, "Follow his trail."
- Bishr ibn Mu'adh told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, ﴿And she said to his sister, "Follow him"﴾: i.e., watch what they do with him.
- Musa told us, he said: 'Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, ﴿And she said to his sister, "Follow him"﴾: meaning, follow his trail.
- al-'Abbas ibn al-Walid told me, he said: Yazid informed us, he said: al-Asbagh ibn Zayd informed us, he said: al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub told us, he said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr told me, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿And she said to his sister, "Follow him"﴾: i.e., follow his trail and seek him out, to see whether you hear any mention of him: is my son alive, or has the creatures of the sea and its fish devoured him? And she had forgotten what Allah had promised her.

* *

His saying: ﴿so she watched him from a distance (ʿan junub)﴾

His saying, exalted is He, means: so the sister of Musa followed his trail, and she watched Musa ʿan junub, meaning: she watched Musa from a distance, not coming close to him or drawing near, lest he know that she had any connection to him. It is said of this: baṣurtu bihi and abṣartuhu, two well-known dialectal forms (lughatān mashhūratān). And abṣarat ʿan junub and ʿan janābah, as the poet said:

*I came to Ḥurayth visiting from afar (ʿan janābah),*
*but Ḥurayth was denying my gift.*

Those who engage in tafsir have said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, he said: Abu 'Asim told us, he said: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, he said: al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿ʿan junub﴾: he said, "From a distance."
- al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, ﴿ʿan jubin﴾: he said, "From a distance." Ibn Juraij said, ﴿ʿan junub﴾: she was on the bank of the river, and Musa was being carried by the Nile while they were parallel to one another like that; she looked at him in one glance and at the people in another glance. He had been placed in a coffin sealed with pitch on its back and belly, and she had locked it upon him.
- al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, from Abu Sufyan, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿So she watched him from a distance﴾, he said: she watched him while she was parallel to him, without going to him.
- al-'Abbas ibn al-Walid told me, he said: Yazid informed us, he said: al-Asbagh ibn Zayd informed us, he said: al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub told me, he said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr told me, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿So she watched him from a distance﴾: and al-junub is that a person's sight rises to a distant thing while he is beside it and does not perceive it.

* *

His saying: ﴿while they did not perceive﴾

He says: and the people of Pharaoh did not perceive that the sister of Musa was his sister.

Those who engage in tafsir have said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, he said: Abu 'Asim told us, he said: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, he said: al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿and they did not perceive﴾: he said, "The family of Pharaoh."
- al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the same.
- Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, (so she watched him from a distance while they did not perceive) that she was his sister: he said, "She began to look at him as though she did not want him."
- Musa told us, he said: 'Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, ﴿and they did not perceive﴾ that she was his sister.
- Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Salama told us, from Ibn Ishaq, ﴿and they did not perceive﴾: i.e., they did not know that she had any connection to him.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And We had forbidden him the nurses before, so she said, "Shall I direct you to a household who will undertake his upbringing for you, and they will be sincere toward him?"﴾ (28:12)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We prevented Moses from nursing from the wet-nurses before his mother. It is mentioned that it was Moses' sister who said to the people of Pharaoh: ﴿Shall I direct you to a household who will undertake his upbringing for you, and they will be sincere toward him?﴾

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what we have said on this matter.

Those who said this:

- Musa related to us, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: They wanted nurses for him, but he would not take from any of the women. The women began seeking this so that they might gain a place with Pharaoh as nurses, but he refused to take [any of them]. This is His saying: ﴿And We had forbidden him the nurses before﴾, [so] his sister ﴿said, "Shall I direct you to a household who will undertake his upbringing for you, and they will be sincere toward him?"﴾ Then when his mother came, he took from her.

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿And We had forbidden him the nurses before﴾, he said: He would not accept the breast of any woman until he returned to his mother.

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Hassan, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And We had forbidden him the nurses before﴾, he said: He would not be brought a nurse whom he would accept.

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿And We had forbidden him the nurses before﴾, he said: He would not nurse from the breast of any woman until he returned to his mother.

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And We had forbidden him the nurses before﴾, he said: Whenever a woman was brought to him, he would not take her breast. He said: ﴿So she said﴾, [his sister] ﴿"Shall I direct you to a household who will undertake his upbringing for you, and they will be sincere toward him?"﴾

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: They gathered the nurses when God placed love for him in their hearts, but whenever a woman was brought and he took her breast, it would distress them [[In (al-Lisan: r-m-d) al-ramd means burning of anger. "Armadani hadha al-amr" means it pained me, and "ramidtu" means I was pained. It is also said: "armadani" means it hurt me.]], so one nurse after another would be brought, yet he would not accept any of them. Then his sister said to them, seeing their longing for him and their eagerness for him, ﴿"Shall I direct you to a household who will undertake his upbringing for you"﴾. By His saying ﴿will undertake his upbringing for you﴾ he means: they will take him into their care for you.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and they will be sincere toward him﴾

It is mentioned that she was seized, and it was said: "You know this boy, so direct us to his family." She said: "I do not know him; I only meant that they are sincere toward the king."

Those who said this:

- Musa related to me, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When his sister said, ﴿"Shall I direct you to a household who will undertake his upbringing for you, and they will be sincere toward him?"﴾, they seized her and said: "You know this boy, so direct us to his family." She said: "I do not know him; I only said: they are sincere toward the king."

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿"Shall I direct you to a household who will undertake his upbringing for you, and they will be sincere toward him?"﴾, he said: They detained her when she said "and they are sincere toward him." They said: "You know him." She said: "I only meant: they are sincere toward the king."

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding ﴿and they are sincere toward him﴾, i.e., because of their standing with you and their eagerness for the king's pleasure. They said: "Bring her."

The commentary on the words of God the Exalted: ﴿So We returned him to his mother that her eye might be comforted and she would not grieve, and that she might know that the promise of God is true; but most of them do not know﴾ (13).

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿So We returned him﴾, Musa, ﴿to his mother﴾ after the family of Pharaoh had picked him up, so that her eye would be comforted by her son, when he came back to her safe from the killing of Pharaoh, ﴿and she would not grieve﴾ over his separation from her. (And that she might know that the promise of God) which He made to her when He said: ﴿And when you fear for him, then cast him into the river, and do not fear and do not grieve; indeed, We will return him to you and will make him among the messengers﴾ ... the verse, ﴿is true﴾.

And the people of interpretation have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿So We returned him to his mother﴾, and he recited until ﴿do not know﴾, and [God] promised her that He would return him to her and make him among the messengers, and God did that for her.

* *

As for His words: ﴿but most of them do not know﴾

He, the Exalted, says: but most of the polytheists do not know that the promise of God is true; they do not believe that it is so.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 14:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when he reached his full strength and was mature, We gave him judgment and knowledge. Thus do We reward the good-doers.﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿When Musa reached his full strength﴾, meaning: when the strength of his body and his powers came to completion, and that reached its end in him. We have already explained the meaning of ashudd (full strength) earlier, with its evidences, so that suffices and there is no need to repeat it in this place.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and was mature﴾

He says: his youth reached its completion, his form was perfected and firmly established. There has been difference over the span of years of istiwa' (maturity). Some of them said: it occurs at forty years.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿and was mature﴾, he said: forty years.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿When he reached his full strength﴾, he said: thirty-three years.

* *

His words: ﴿and was mature﴾

He said: he reached forty years.

al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas ﴿When he reached his full strength﴾, he said: a little over thirty years.

He said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿When he reached his full strength﴾, he said: thirty-three years.

al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada ﴿full strength and was mature﴾, he said: forty years, and full strength: thirty-three years.

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿When he reached his full strength and was mature﴾, he said: My father used to say: al-ashudd is vigour and robustness, and al-istiwa' is forty years.

Others said: it occurs at thirty years.

* *

As for His words: ﴿We gave him judgment and knowledge﴾

By judgment is meant: understanding of the religion and knowledge.

As related:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿We gave him judgment and knowledge﴾, he said: understanding, reason and action before prophethood.

al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid ﴿We gave him judgment and knowledge﴾, he said: understanding and action before prophethood.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq ﴿When he reached his full strength and was mature﴾: God gave him judgment and knowledge: understanding of His religion and the religion of his fathers, and knowledge of what is in His religion, its laws and its limits.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Thus do We reward the good-doers﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: just as We rewarded Musa for his obedience to Us and his goodness in being patient with Our command, so likewise We reward everyone among Our messengers and servants who does good, who is patient with Our command, obeys Us, and refrains from what We have forbidden him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 15:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And he entered the city at a time of heedlessness from its people, and found therein two men fighting, one from his own party and the other from his enemy. So the one from his party sought his help against the one from his enemy, and Moses struck him and killed him. He said, "This is of the work of Satan. Indeed, he is an enemy, a misleading, manifest one."﴾ (15)

His, may He be remembered, saying: ﴿And he entered﴾ Moses ﴿the city﴾, the city of Memphis (Munf) in Egypt, ﴿at a time of heedlessness from its people﴾, and that was at the time of the qa'ilah (midday rest), the middle of the day.

The scholars differed concerning the reason why Moses entered this city at this time. Some of them said: he entered it following the trail of Pharaoh, because Pharaoh had ridden out while Moses was not present; when Moses arrived he was informed of Pharaoh's riding, so he rode and followed his trail, and the midday rest overtook him in this city.

Mention of those who said this:

Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When Moses grew up, he would ride the mounts of Pharaoh and dress as Pharaoh dressed, and he was only called "Moses, son of Pharaoh." Then Pharaoh rode a mount while Moses was not with him; when Moses came, he was told: "Pharaoh has ridden out," so he rode after him and the midday rest overtook him in a land called Munf, so he entered it at midday, its markets had been closed and there was no one in its roads, and it is the city of which God says: ﴿And he entered the city at a time of heedlessness from its people﴾.

Others said: rather, he entered it concealing himself from Pharaoh and his people, because he had opposed them in their religion and criticized what they were upon.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: When Moses reached his full strength and matured, God gave him wisdom and knowledge, and he had among the Children of Israel a party who listened to him, obeyed him and gathered around him. When his judgment became sound (istadda ra'yuhu: from sadad, meaning his intellect became firm and his experiences grew strong), and he recognized what he was upon of the truth, he saw separation from Pharaoh and his people in their religion to be a truth; so he spoke, opposed and denounced, until mention of him reached them, and until they frightened him and he feared them, so that he would not enter Pharaoh's town except in fear and concealment. So he entered it one day at a time of heedlessness from its people.

Others said: rather, Pharaoh had ordered his expulsion from his city when he struck him with the staff, so he did not enter it until he had grown up and reached his full strength. They said: the meaning of the speech is: "And he entered the city at a time of heedlessness from its people" regarding the mention of Moses, i.e., after they had forgotten his news and his matter.

Mention of those who said this:

Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿at a time of heedlessness from its people﴾: it was not heedlessness from an hour, but heedlessness from the mention of Moses and his matter. And Pharaoh said to his wife: "Remove him from me," when he struck his head with the staff, "this is the one because of whom the Children of Israel were killed." She said: "He is a child, and he is such-and-such; bring a coal." A coal was brought, and he took a coal and placed it in his mouth, and it became a knot in his tongue, and that is the knot about which God said: ﴿And loosen a knot from my tongue, that they may understand my speech﴾. He said: "Remove him from me," so he was removed, and he did not enter upon them until he had grown up, so he entered at a time of heedlessness from the mention of him.

The most sound of these sayings is that it should be said as God, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿And when he reached his full strength and became mature ... and he entered the city at a time of heedlessness from its people﴾.

They differed concerning the time intended by His words: ﴿at a time of heedlessness from its people﴾. Some of them said: it is midday.

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And he entered the city at a time of heedlessness﴾, he said: midday. Ibn Jurayj said, from Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: they say it is at the qa'ilah (midday rest), and between maghrib and 'isha'.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And he entered the city at a time of heedlessness from its people﴾, he said: he entered it after he had reached his full strength, at the qa'ilah, midday.

Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: he entered at midday.

* *

And His words: ﴿and he found therein two men fighting, one from his party and the other from his enemy﴾

That is: this one is from the people of Moses' religion, from the Children of Israel, ﴿and this one is from his enemy﴾, from the Copts, from the people of Pharaoh. ﴿So the one from his party sought his help against the one from his enemy﴾: that is, the one who was of the people of Moses' religion sought his help against the one from his enemy, from the Copts. ﴿And Moses struck him and killed him﴾: that is, he punched him and thrust at his chest with the gathered palm.

In accordance with what we have said, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) also spoke.

Mention of those who said this:

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hafs narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Moses did wrong in what he did, and he was very angry and very strong. He passed by a man of the Copts who was subjecting a man of the Muslims to forced labor. When he saw Moses, he sought his help, saying: "O Moses!" Moses said: "Let him go." He said: "I have resolved to carry him upon you." ﴿And Moses struck him and killed him﴾. He said: then, when the next day came, at midday he went out to look for news, and behold, that man had been seized by another of the same kind; he said: "O Moses!" He said: then Moses' anger flared, and he lunged; he feared that it was himself he intended, and he said: ﴿Do you intend to kill me as you killed a soul yesterday?﴾ The man said: "Did I not see you, O Moses, you are the one who killed!"

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Uthram ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿and he found therein two men fighting﴾, he said: a man from the Children of Israel fighting a tyrant of Pharaoh's. ﴿So he sought his help ... and Moses struck him and killed him﴾. When the next day came, he was called upon for help, and he found him fighting another, so he came to his aid, and he said: ﴿Do you intend to kill me as you killed a soul yesterday?﴾ So they knew that he was Moses, and he left the city in fear, watching warily. 'Uthram said: or something like this.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and he found therein two men fighting, this one from his party and this one from his enemy﴾. As for the one from his party, he was from the Children of Israel, and as for the one from his enemy, he was a Copt from the family of Pharaoh.

Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿and he found therein two men fighting, this one from his party and this one from his enemy﴾, he says: from the Copts, ﴿so the one from his party sought his help against the one from his enemy﴾.

al-'Abbas ibn al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: al-Asbagh ibn Zayd informed us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated to me, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Moses reached his full strength and became a man, none of the family of Pharaoh could reach any of the Children of Israel with him by oppression or forced labour, until they were utterly restrained. Then, while he was walking one day in a part of the city, he came upon two men fighting: one from the Children of Israel and the other from the family of Pharaoh. The Israelite sought his help against the Pharaonic man, so Moses became angry and his anger intensified, because he (the Pharaonic man) had assaulted him while knowing Moses' standing among the Children of Israel and his protection of them. People did not know but that this was from the milk-suckling of Moses' mother, unless God had informed Moses of knowledge that no one else was informed of. Moses struck the Pharaonic man and killed him, and no one saw them except God and the Israelite. So ﴿he said﴾ when he killed the man: ﴿"This is of the work of Satan..."﴾, the verse.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿and he found therein two men fighting, this one from his party﴾, a Muslim, ﴿and this one from the people of Pharaoh's religion, an unbeliever﴾, ﴿so the one from his party sought his help against the one from his enemy﴾. Moses had been given physical stature and strength in seizing, so he became angry at their enemy and contended with him. ﴿And Moses struck him﴾, a blow by which he killed him, though he did not intend to kill him. ﴿He said: "This is of the work of Satan. Indeed, he is an enemy, a misleading, manifest one."﴾

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿This is of his party﴾, he said: from his people, from the Children of Israel, and Pharaoh was from Persia, from Istakhr.

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah, from his companions: ﴿this one from his party﴾, an Israelite, ﴿and this one from his enemy﴾, a Copt, ﴿so the one from his party sought his help against the one from his enemy﴾.

In accordance with what we have said, they also spoke regarding the meaning of His words: ﴿And Moses struck him﴾.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And Moses struck him﴾, he said: with the gathered palm.

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And Moses struck him﴾, the Prophet of God, and he did not intend to kill him.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: he killed him while not intending to kill him.

* *

And His words: ﴿and he killed him﴾

That is: he finished off killing him. It has already been explained earlier that the meaning of qada' is "finishing," which suffices so that it need not be repeated here.

Mention that he killed him and then buried him in the sand.

As follows:

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah, from his companions: ﴿So Moses struck him and killed him﴾, then buried him in the sand.

* *

And His words: ﴿He said, "This is of the work of Satan"﴾

That is, may His remembrance be exalted, saying: Moses said when he killed the slain man: this killing is from the instigation of Satan against me, by inflaming my anger until I struck this one and he perished from my blow. ﴿Indeed, he is an enemy﴾: that is, indeed Satan is an enemy to the son of Adam, ﴿misleading﴾ him from the path of right guidance by adorning for him ugly deeds and making them seem good to him. ﴿Manifest﴾: meaning that he clearly shows his enmity toward them from of old, and his misleading of them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verses 16–17:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿My Lord, I have wronged myself, so forgive me.⁠ So He forgave him. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.⁠ (16) He said, "My Lord, for that You have bestowed upon me, I will never be a supporter of the criminals."⁠ (17)

Says God, may He be remembered, reporting the regret of Musa (Moses) over what had occurred of his killing of the soul he had killed, his repentance to Him for it, and his request for His forgiveness of that: ﴿My Lord, I have wronged myself⁠﴾ by killing a soul that had not commanded me to kill it. So pardon my sin, cover it over for me, and do not hold me accountable for it so as to punish me for it.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said in agreement with what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding His saying: ﴿My Lord, I have wronged myself⁠﴾, he said: by my killing, because it is not fitting for a prophet to kill until he is commanded, and he had not been commanded.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: "He recognized the way out, so he said: ﴿I have wronged myself, so forgive me. So He forgave him⁠﴾."

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿So He forgave him⁠﴾

Says God, may He be remembered: God pardoned Musa for his sin and did not punish him for it. ﴿Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful⁠﴾ means: indeed God is the one who covers over the sins of those who turn to Him in repentance, concealing their sins, the one who bestows upon them the favor of pardoning them, and the Merciful toward people, not punishing them for their sins after they have repented of them.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿He said, "My Lord, for that You have bestowed upon me⁠﴾

Says God, may He be remembered: Musa said, "My Lord, by Your bestowal upon me, through Your pardon of my killing of this soul," ﴿so I will never be a supporter of the criminals⁠﴾, meaning the polytheists, as though he had sworn an oath to that effect.

It has been mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) it is: "So do not make me a supporter of the criminals." As though, according to this reading, he was supplicating his Lord, saying: "O God, I will never be a supporter," and he, peace be upon him, did not add the exception (istithna') when he said ﴿so I will never be a supporter of the criminals⁠﴾, so he was tested.

Qatadah used to say regarding this:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿so I will never be a supporter of the criminals⁠﴾ — he says: "I will never again help a wrongdoer in his wickedness." He said: "Rarely does a man say this except that he is tested." He said: "So he was tested, as you hear."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verses 16–17:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿My Lord, I have wronged myself, so forgive me.⁠ So He forgave him. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.⁠ (16) He said, "My Lord, for that You have bestowed upon me, I will never be a supporter of the criminals."⁠ (17)

Says God, may He be remembered, reporting the regret of Musa (Moses) over what had occurred of his killing of the soul he had killed, his repentance to Him for it, and his request for His forgiveness of that: ﴿My Lord, I have wronged myself⁠﴾ by killing a soul that had not commanded me to kill it. So pardon my sin, cover it over for me, and do not hold me accountable for it so as to punish me for it.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said in agreement with what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding His saying: ﴿My Lord, I have wronged myself⁠﴾, he said: by my killing, because it is not fitting for a prophet to kill until he is commanded, and he had not been commanded.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: "He recognized the way out, so he said: ﴿I have wronged myself, so forgive me. So He forgave him⁠﴾."

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿So He forgave him⁠﴾

Says God, may He be remembered: God pardoned Musa for his sin and did not punish him for it. ﴿Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful⁠﴾ means: indeed God is the one who covers over the sins of those who turn to Him in repentance, concealing their sins, the one who bestows upon them the favor of pardoning them, and the Merciful toward people, not punishing them for their sins after they have repented of them.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿He said, "My Lord, for that You have bestowed upon me⁠﴾

Says God, may He be remembered: Musa said, "My Lord, by Your bestowal upon me, through Your pardon of my killing of this soul," ﴿so I will never be a supporter of the criminals⁠﴾, meaning the polytheists, as though he had sworn an oath to that effect.

It has been mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) it is: "So do not make me a supporter of the criminals." As though, according to this reading, he was supplicating his Lord, saying: "O God, I will never be a supporter," and he, peace be upon him, did not add the exception (istithna') when he said ﴿so I will never be a supporter of the criminals⁠﴾, so he was tested.

Qatadah used to say regarding this:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿so I will never be a supporter of the criminals⁠﴾ — he says: "I will never again help a wrongdoer in his wickedness." He said: "Rarely does a man say this except that he is tested." He said: "So he was tested, as you hear."

The commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So he woke up in the city, fearful and watchful, and suddenly the one who had sought his help the day before cried out to him for help. Moses said to him, "You are clearly a quarreler."﴾ (28:18)

Allah, may He be exalted and remembered, says: Moses woke up in the city of Pharaoh, fearful of the crime he had committed and of his killing of the soul he had killed, lest he be seized and killed for it. ﴿Watchful﴾ means: watching for news, that is, waiting to learn what people were saying and what they were going to do regarding his affair and the affair of the slain man.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

* Al-Abbas ibn al-Walid told me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Asbagh ibn Zayd informed us, saying: al-Qasim narrated to us, from Abu Ayyub, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated to us, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿So he woke up in the city, fearful and watchful﴾, he said: Fearful of his killing the soul, watchful lest he be seized.

* Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿So he woke up in the city, fearful and watchful﴾, he said: Fearful that he would be seized.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿And suddenly the one who had sought his help the day before cried out to him for help﴾

Allah, may He be exalted and remembered, says: When Moses entered the city in fear, watching for news about his affair and the affair of the slain man, suddenly the Israelite who had sought his help the day before against the Egyptian was fighting another Egyptian. The Israelite saw him and called out to him for help against the Egyptian. That is: he again sought his aid against the Egyptian. The word is derived from al-sarakh (the cry), as people say: "The sons of so-and-so said: O morning!" Moses said to him: ﴿"You are clearly a quarreler."﴾ Allah, His praise be exalted, says: Moses said to the Israelite who had called out to him for help, and Moses had encountered him regretful over what had previously happened from him, the killing of the slain man the day before, while he was calling on him today against another: "Indeed, you, O one who calls for help, are a quarreler," meaning: indeed you are one of error, clearly so. That is: your error has become evident by your fighting a man yesterday and another today.
