We have said the same as this, and the people of interpretation have said the same.

Those who said this:

* Al-Abbas told me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Asbagh ibn Zayd informed us, saying: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated to us, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: It was reported to Pharaoh that the Children of Israel had killed a man from the family of Pharaoh, so he said: "Take our right from them and do not give them leniency in this." He said: "Bring me his killer and whoever bears witness against him. It is not right for us to judge without evidence or proof" [[al-thabt: in (al-Lisan, th-b-t) al-thabt, with a vowel on the tha, means proof and evidence.]]. So they sought that, and while they were searching and finding nothing, Moses passed by the next day and saw that Israelite fighting an Egyptian. The Israelite called on him for help against the Egyptian. Moses encountered him regretful over what he had done the day before and disliking what he saw. Moses became angry and stretched out his hand, wanting to strike the Egyptian. So he said to the Israelite, because of what he had done yesterday and today: ﴿"You are clearly a quarreler."﴾ The Israelite looked at Moses after he had said this, and saw him angry as he had been angry the day before when the Egyptian was killed. He feared that by saying to him ﴿"You are clearly a quarreler"﴾ Moses meant him, and he had not meant him; he meant the Egyptian. So the Israelite became afraid and argued with him, saying: ﴿"O Moses, do you intend to kill me as you killed a soul yesterday? You only intend to be a tyrant in the land"﴾? He said this only out of fear that Moses intended him, to kill him, so they parted.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And suddenly the one who had sought his help the day before cried out to him for help﴾, he said: al-istinsar (seeking help) and al-istisrakh (crying for help) are one.

* Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And suddenly the one who had sought his help the day before cried out to him for help﴾, he said: He was calling on him for aid.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: When Moses killed the slain man, he went out and joined his dwelling from Egypt, and the people spoke of his affair, and it was said: "Moses has killed a man." This reached Pharaoh. Moses woke up the next morning going out, and suddenly his companion of the day before was embracing another man from his enemies. Moses said to him: ﴿"You are clearly a quarreler; yesterday a man, and today another?"﴾

* Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hafs narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Shaybani, from 'Ikrimah, who said: The one he sought help from is the one who called on him for help.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 19:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when he was about to seize the one who was an enemy to both of them, he said, "O Musa, do you intend to kill me as you killed a soul yesterday? You intend only to be a tyrant in the land, and you do not intend to be of the reformers."﴾

His saying, exalted is He, means: When Musa was about to seize the Egyptian, who was an enemy to him and to the Israelite, the Israelite said to Musa, supposing that it was himself that he intended, ﴿"Do you intend to kill me as you killed a soul yesterday?"﴾

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿So when he was about to seize the one who was an enemy to both of them, he said﴾: He feared him, the one from his own party, when Musa said to him: ﴿Indeed, you are clearly misguided.﴾

Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Musa said to the Israelite: ﴿Indeed, you are clearly misguided.﴾ Then he turned to help him. When he saw Musa approaching toward him to seize the man who was fighting the Israelite, ﴿he said﴾ — the Israelite, fearing that Musa would seize him because he had spoken harshly to him — ﴿"O Musa, do you intend to kill me as you killed a soul yesterday? You intend only to be a tyrant in the land, and you do not intend to be of the reformers."﴾ So Musa left him.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr ibn Abd Allah, from his companions, who said: [Musa] regretted after he had killed the victim, and he said: ﴿"This is from the work of Satan. Indeed, he is an enemy, a clear misleader."﴾ He said: Then the Israelite sought his help again against another Copt, and [Musa] said to him: ﴿"Indeed, you are clearly misguided."﴾ When he was about to seize the Copt, the Israelite thought it was himself that he intended, and said: "O Musa, ﴿do you intend to kill me as you killed a soul yesterday?﴾"

He said: Ibn Jurayj, or Ibn Abi Najih — al-Tabari is in doubt, and in the book it is Ibn Abi Najih — said: When Musa rose in the morning, he rose regretful and repentant, wishing he had not seized either of them. He had said to the Israelite: ﴿"Indeed, you are clearly misguided,"﴾ so the Israelite knew that Musa would not help him. When the Israelite wanted to seize the Copt, Musa forbade him, and the Israelite feared Musa and said: ﴿"Do you intend to kill me as you killed a soul yesterday?"﴾ So the Copt spread the report of it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿"You intend only to be a tyrant in the land"﴾

His saying, exalted is He, reports the speech of the Israelite to Musa: You intend nothing but to be a tyrant in the land. The conduct of tyrants was the killing of souls unjustly, without right. It was said: he said this to Musa only because among them, the Israelite, there was one who had killed two souls, from the tyrants.

Those who said this:

Musa ibn Sahl narrated to us... — [see below]

Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Hushaym ibn Bashir narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Salim, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Whoever kills two men is a tyrant. He said: Then he recited: ﴿"Do you intend to kill me as you killed a soul yesterday? You intend only to be a tyrant in the land, and you do not intend to be of the reformers."﴾

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿"You intend only to be a tyrant in the land"﴾: Indeed, the tyrants are like this, they kill a soul for other than a soul.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, ﴿"You intend only to be a tyrant in the land"﴾: He said: That is the way of the tyrants, that they kill a soul for other than a soul.

* *

And His saying: ﴿"and you do not intend to be of the reformers"﴾

He says: You do not intend to be among those who act in the land with what brings good to its people, by obedience to God. It is related from Ibn Ishaq that he said concerning this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿"and you do not intend to be of the reformers"﴾: That is, this is not how reform is done.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 28, Verse 20**

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And a man came running from the farthest part of the city. He said, "O Moses, the chiefs are conspiring against you to kill you, so leave. I am indeed one of your sincere advisors."﴾

It has been mentioned that the words of the Israelite were overheard by a listener, who then disclosed them and informed the family of the slain man. At that point Pharaoh sought Moses and ordered that he be killed. When Pharaoh ordered his killing, a man came to Moses and informed him of what Pharaoh had decided concerning him, and advised him to leave Egypt, the land of Pharaoh and his people.

Their view is similar to what we have said on this matter, and the exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same.

Those who said this:

Al-Abbas narrated to me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: al-Asbagh ibn Zayd informed us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Egyptian who had been fighting the Israelite went off to his people and informed them of what he had heard from the Israelite when he said, ﴿Do you want to kill me as you killed a person yesterday?﴾ So Pharaoh sent the slaughterers to kill Moses. They took the main road, not fearing that he would escape them. But a man from the partisans of Moses was at the farthest part of the city, and he took a shorter route until he reached Moses before them and informed him of the news.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: The Copt, who was their enemy, informed them, so the chiefs conspired to kill him. Then a man came from the farthest part of the city, and he recited, ﴿Indeed, the chiefs...﴾ to the end of the verse. He said: We used to narrate that he was a believer from the family of Pharaoh.

Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: The Copt, meaning the one who had been fighting the Israelite, went and disclosed against him that Moses was the one who had killed the man. Pharaoh sought him and said, "Seize him, for he is our companion." He said to those who were searching for him, "Search for him in the small side-paths (bunayat al-tariq) of the road, for Moses is a youth who does not know the way." Moses took to the small side-paths, and the man had come to him and informed him: ﴿Indeed, the chiefs are conspiring against you to kill you.﴾

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr ibn Abd Allah, from his companions, who said: When the Copt heard the Israelite's words to Moses, ﴿Do you want to kill me as you killed a person yesterday?﴾ he carried them to the family of the slain man and said, "It is Moses who killed your companion, and no one would have known it had he not heard it from the Israelite." When Moses learned that they had found out, he went out fleeing, and the people sought him but he outran them. He said: Ibn Abi Najih said: "The Copt ran (sa'a)."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, who said: The Israelite said to Moses, ﴿Do you want to kill me as you killed a person yesterday?﴾ A Copt was close to them, listening, and he disclosed them both.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: An enemy heard that and disclosed them both.

* * *

On His words, ﴿And a man came﴾

It has been mentioned that he was a believer from the family of Pharaoh, and his name, it is said, was Sam'an.

Some said: Rather, his name was Shim'un.

Those who said that:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Wahb ibn Sulayman informed me, from Shu'ayb al-Jubba'i, who said: His name was Shim'un, the one who said to Moses, ﴿Indeed, the chiefs are conspiring against you to kill you.﴾

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: The chiefs of Pharaoh's people woke up having resolved to kill Moses, as had reached them about him, and a man came running from the farthest part of the city, called Sam'an, and said, ﴿O Moses, the chiefs are conspiring against you to kill you, so leave. I am indeed one of your sincere advisors.﴾

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, who said: ﴿And a man came from the farthest part of the city, running to Moses. He said, "O Moses, the chiefs are conspiring against you to kill you, so leave. I am indeed one of your sincere advisors."﴾

* * *

On His words, ﴿from the farthest part of the city﴾

He means: from the outermost part of Pharaoh's city. ﴿Running (yas'a)﴾ means: hastening.

As:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿And a man came from the farthest part of the city, running﴾, he said: Hastening, not in a hard run.

* * *

On His words, ﴿He said, "O Moses, the chiefs are conspiring against you to kill you"﴾

He, glory be to His praise, means: the man who came to Moses from the farthest part of the city, running, said: O Moses, the nobles and leaders of Pharaoh's people are conspiring to kill you; they are consulting and deliberating about you. From this is the poet's saying:

"What you deliberate among us (ma ta'tamir feena), then your right hand or your left hand decides it."¹

That is: what you deliberate upon and resolve. From this is the saying of al-Namir ibn Taulab:

"I see the people have invented a custom, and in every new event there is deliberation (yu'tamar)."²

That is: it is consulted upon and considered.

---

¹ In *al-Lisan* (root *amr*): In the revelation: "Indeed, the chiefs are conspiring against you (ya'tamirun bika) to kill you." Abu Ubayda said: that is, they consult about you to kill you. The author took from this the poet's saying "ma ta'tamir feena." He means: whatever the men of judgment consult upon concerning our affair is a binding command, with no one objecting to it. But the author's explanation of the verse, "meaning what he deliberates and resolves," makes the meaning not consultation (ilti'mar as mushawara) but resolving alone, without consulting anyone other than oneself. Al-Azhari said: *a'tamara fulan ra'yahu*: when a person consults his intellect about the right course he will take. He who deliberates may be right once and wrong another time.

² This verse is one of the evidences cited by Abu Ubayda in *Majaz al-Qur'an* (folio 187: 1). *Al-shiyma* means character or disposition; he means: they have invented dispositions that were not known before. The poet points to the stirring up of doubts and disputes over political matters such as the caliphate, or over doctrines such as the discussion of qadar and the like. These are the dispositions that people invented in the early period of Muslim life after the lifetime of the Messenger (ﷺ). Al-Namir ibn Taulab was a *mukhadram* poet (one who lived in both the pre-Islamic and Islamic eras). The evidence lies in his phrase "yu'tamar," meaning that consultation, exchange of opinions and disputation arise. Perhaps the poet saw the early signs of disagreement and the portents of division appearing through events, and so he warned of them.

That is: it is consulted upon and considered in them.

* * *

On His words, ﴿So leave, indeed I am for you one of the sincere advisors﴾

He means: leave this city, for I, in my advice to you to leave it, am indeed one of the sincere advisors to you.

**Commentary on the words of God Most High: ﴿So he left it, fearful and watchful. He said, "My Lord, deliver me from the wrongdoing people." (21) And when he turned his face toward Madyan, he said, "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way." (22)﴾**

God Most High says: So Moses left the city of Pharaoh, fearing that he would be killed in retaliation for the soul he had taken. ﴿Watchful﴾ means that he was waiting for the pursuers to catch up with him and seize him.

As related:

* He narrated to us Bishr, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, on the authority of Qatadah, regarding ﴿So he left it, fearful and watchful﴾: "Fearful of being killed for the soul he had taken, watching for the pursuit," and ﴿He said, "My Lord, deliver me from the wrongdoing people."﴾

* He narrated to us al-Qasim, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Abu Sufyan narrated to me, on the authority of Ma'mar, on the authority of Qatadah, regarding ﴿So he left it, fearful and watchful﴾: "Fearful of the killing of the soul, watching lest the pursuit seize him."

* He narrated to us Ibn Humayd, who said: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: It was mentioned to me that he left heading in whatever direction, fearful and watchful, not knowing which way to take, and he was saying: ﴿My Lord, deliver me from the wrongdoing people.﴾

* He narrated to me Yunus, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿So he left it, fearful and watchful﴾: "Watchful out of fear of the pursuit."

* * *

As for His words: ﴿He said, "My Lord, deliver me from the wrongdoing people."﴾

God Most High says: Moses said, while departing from the city of Pharaoh in fear: "My Lord, deliver me from these people, the disbelievers, who have wronged themselves by disbelieving in You."

* * *

As for His words: ﴿And when he turned his face toward Madyan﴾

God Most High says: When Moses turned his face toward Madyan, heading there, departing from the city of Pharaoh and leaving his authority, ﴿he said, "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way."﴾ By His words "toward" (tilqa') He means in the direction of Madyan. It is said: "He did that of his own accord (min tilqa' nafsihi)," meaning from himself, by his own initiative; and "his house is opposite (tilqa') the house of so-and-so," meaning it faces it. The name Madyan is not declined (in the sense of not taking nunation) because it is the name of a well-known town, and the Arabs treat the names of well-known towns this way. Among the evidence is the verse of the poet:

*"The monks of Madyan, had they seen you, would have descended,*
*and the wild goats from the summits of the steep cliffs."* [[The line is by Jarir, and its citation was previously given for "monks" (rahban), the plural of rahib, in (7:3) of this tafsir. It is cited here to show that Madyan is not declined because it is a proper name for a town, combining definiteness and feminine form.]]

* * *

As for His words: ﴿Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way﴾

He says: Perhaps my Lord will show me the direct way to Madyan. He said this only because he did not know the road to it.

It is mentioned that when he said, ﴿My Lord, deliver me from the wrongdoing people﴾, God sent to him an angel who set him on the road and showed it to him.

Those who said this:

* He narrated to us Musa, who said: Amr narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said: When Moses set out on the untrodden paths, an angel came to him on a horse, holding a staff (anazah). When Moses saw him he prostrated to him out of fear. [The angel] said: "Do not prostrate to me, but follow me." So he followed him, and he guided him toward Madyan. Moses, heading toward Madyan, said: ﴿Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way﴾, and he [the angel] led him until he reached Madyan with him.

* He narrated to us al-Abbas, who said: Yazid informed us, who said: al-Asbagh ibn Zayd informed us, who said: al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Moses went out heading toward Madyan, having no knowledge of the road except his good opinion of his Lord, for he said: ﴿Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way﴾.

* He narrated to us Ibn Humayd, who said: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: It was mentioned to me that he left saying: ﴿My Lord, deliver me from the wrongdoing people﴾, so God made the way to Madyan easy for him. He left Egypt without provisions, without sandals, without a mount [[al-zahr: the beast one rides, such as a camel or the like]], without a dirham or a loaf of bread, fearful and watchful, until he arrived at a community of people watering (their flocks) in Madyan.

* He narrated to us Abu 'Ammar al-Husayn ibn Huraith al-Marwazi, who said: al-Fadl ibn Musa narrated to us, on the authority of al-A'mash, on the authority of al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Moses left Egypt for Madyan, and between them was a journey of eight [nights]. He said: It was said that it was about the distance from Kufa to Basra. He had no food except the leaves of trees, and he went out barefoot, and he did not reach it until the sole of his foot had worn away.

* He narrated to us Abu Kurayb, who said: 'Uthham narrated to us, who said: al-A'mash narrated to us, on the authority of al-Minhal, on the authority of Sa'id, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When Moses left Egypt for Madyan, and between him and it were eight nights, it was said: "It is about the distance from Basra to Kufa." Then he mentioned something similar.

Madyan was, at that time, inhabited by the people of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him.

Those who said this:

* He narrated to us Bishr, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, on the authority of Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And when he turned his face toward Madyan﴾: Madyan was a water source where the people of Shu'ayb were, ﴿he said, "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way."﴾

As for His words ﴿the right way﴾, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation, in the same manner as we have said.

Those who said this:

* He narrated to us al-Qasim, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Juraij, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly.

* He said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Ma'mar, on the authority of Qatadah, regarding ﴿Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way﴾: "The direction of the path."

* He narrated to us Ibn Bashshar, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, who said: 'Abbad ibn Rashid narrated to us, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding ﴿Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way﴾: "The straight road."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 23:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when he arrived at the water of Madyan, he found upon it a community of people watering [their flocks], and he found beside them two women driving back [their sheep]. He said, "What is your matter?" They said, "We cannot water until the shepherds have finished dispatching [their flocks], and our father is a very old man."﴾ (23)

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿And when Musa arrived at the water of Madyan, he found upon it a community﴾, meaning a group, ﴿of people watering﴾ their livestock and their flocks.

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

- Musa b. Harun narrated to us, he said: ʿAmr narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿he found upon it a community of people watering﴾: he means a multitude of people watering.

- Muhammad b. ʿAmr narrated to us, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, he said: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding his words ﴿a community of people﴾: he said: "people."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, he said: He came upon a community of people watering in Madyan, people of camels and sheep.

- ʿAli b. Musa and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, they said: Abu Dawud narrated to us, he said: ʿImran al-Qattan informed us, he said: Abu Hamza narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿when he arrived at the water of Madyan﴾. ʿAli b. Musa said: He said: "like the water of your answer," meaning the newly-occurring [matter]. Ibn Bashshar said: "like your present newly-occurring [matter]," meaning your answer.

* *

His saying: ﴿and he found beside them two women driving back﴾

He says: and he found, beyond the community of people who were at the water, two women driving back. By His words ﴿driving back﴾ is meant: holding back their sheep. It is said of this: "Fulan drove back his sheep and livestock" when he wants something of that to bolt and go off, so he turns it back and prevents it; he drives it back (yadhudduha) driving (dhawdan).

One of the Kufan grammarians of the Arabic language said: it is not permissible to say "I drove back the man" in the sense of "I held him back"; rather, that is said of sheep and camels.

It has been narrated from the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed I am at the edge of my pool, driving the people away from it with my staff," so he made the driving (dhawd) apply to people. And from the usage of driving is the saying of Suwayd b. Kurâʿ:

أَبِيتُ عَلَى بَابِ الْقَوَافِي كَأَنَّمَا ... أَذُودُ بِهَا سِرْبًا مِنَ الَوَحْشِ نزعا

[The verse is by Suwayd b. Kurâʿ al-ʿUkli, who had satirised the Banu ʿAbd Allah b. Darim, so they sought redress against him from Saʿid b. ʿUthman, who wanted to strike him, so Suwayd recited a qasida whose opening is: "The daughter of al-ʿAwfi, Layla, says: do you not see Ibn Kurâʿ, who is never without fright." The verse is among the evidences cited by Abu ʿUbayda in Majaz al-Qur'an. He said at the words of the Exalted ﴿and he found beside them two women driving back﴾: its meaning (majaz) is: they prevent and repel and strike. Suwayd b. Kurâʿ said: "I pass the night at the gate of rhymes..." the verse. The author of al-Aghani has also cited Suwayd b. Kurâʿ's verses, including the verse of evidence, in volume 12, page 344, Dar al-Kutub edition. In it, "usadi" stands in place of "adhudd." Its editor said: sadaha means: to court and to conceal. There is then no evidence in it.]

And another saying:

وَقَدْ سَلَبَتْ عَصَاكَ بَنُو تَمِيمٍ ... فَمَا تَدْرِي بأيّ عَصًا تَذُودُ

[The verse is among the evidences of Abu ʿUbayda in (Majaz al-Qur'an, folio 178b). He said: "tadhudan" its meaning is: they prevent, repel, and strike.]

The interpreters have said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

- ʿAli narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding his words ﴿driving back﴾: he says: "holding back."

- al-ʿAbbas narrated to me, he said: Yazid informed us, he said: al-Asbagh informed us, he said: al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Saʿid b. Jubayr narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿and he found beside them two women driving back﴾, meaning by that: they are holding back.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Saʿid b. Jubayr, regarding his words ﴿two women driving back﴾: he said: "holding back."

- Musa narrated to us, he said: ʿAmr narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿and he found beside them two women driving back﴾: he says: they hold back their sheep.

The interpreters differed concerning that from which these two women were driving back. Some of them said: they were driving their sheep back from the water until the livestock of the people had left it, then they would water their own livestock, because of their weakness.

Mention of those who said that:

- al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, he said: Husayn informed us, from Abu Malik regarding his words ﴿two women driving back﴾: he said: they hold back their sheep from the people until they finish, and the well is left clear for them.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿and he found beside them two women﴾, meaning beside the people, driving back their sheep from the water, which is the water of Madyan.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: they drive the people back from their sheep.

Mention of those who said that:

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿when he arrived at the water of Madyan, he found upon it a community of people watering, and he found beside them two women driving back﴾, he said: holding back their sheep, driving the people back from their sheep.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from his companions: ﴿driving back﴾, he said: driving the people back from their sheep.

The more correct of the two interpretations is the saying of the one who said its meaning is: they hold back their sheep from the people until the people have finished watering their livestock.

We only say that this is more correct because of the indication of His words ﴿What is your matter?" They said, "We cannot water until the shepherds have finished dispatching [their flocks]﴾ that this is so. For they only complained that they could not water until the shepherds had dispatched their flocks, when Musa asked them about their driving back. Had they been driving the people back from their sheep, they would undoubtedly have informed him of the reason for their driving the people back from them, not of the reason for the delay of their watering until the shepherds had dispatched [their flocks].

* *

His saying: ﴿He said, "What is your matter?"﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Musa said to the two women, "What is your matter and your affair, that you drive your livestock back from the people? Why do you not water them along with the flocks of the people and the Arabs?" One says to a man, "Ma khatbuk?" meaning: what is your affair and your state, as the rajiz said:

يَا عَجَبًا مَا خَطْبُهُ وَخَطْبِي

[The verse is among Abu ʿUbayda's evidences in Maʿani al-Qur'an (folio 187-1). In explaining His words ﴿what is your matter﴾, he said: that is, what is your affair and your situation? He said: "O wonder, what is his matter and my matter." The verse is from a rajaz hemistich of Ru'ba b. al-ʿAjjaj (Diwan, p. 16), from a rajaz poem in praise of Bilal b. Abi Burda, who is ʿAmir b. ʿAbd Allah b. Qays, whose opening is: "Are you reproaching me while love is full of reproach..."]

The interpreters have said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

- al-ʿAbbas narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: al-Asbagh informed us, he said: al-Qasim informed us, he said: Saʿid b. Jubayr narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbas, he said: He said to them: ﴿What is your matter?﴾, [seeing them] standing apart, not watering with the people.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, he said: He found compassion for them, and fear entered him concerning them, because of what he saw of their weakness and the people's dominance over the water to their exclusion. So he said to them: "What is your matter?" meaning: what is your affair.

* *

His saying: ﴿They said, "We cannot water until the shepherds have finished dispatching [their flocks]"﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says: The two women said to Musa: "We do not water our livestock until the shepherds have dispatched their flocks, because we are not able to water; we only water our livestock with what remains of the flocks of the shepherds in the trough."  "Ra'a'" (shepherds) is the plural of "ra'in" (a shepherd); the plural of "al-ra'i" is "ru'a'," "ru'ah," and "ru'yan."

The interpreters have said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

- al-ʿAbbas narrated to me, he said: Yazid informed us, he said: al-Asbagh informed us, he said: al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Saʿid b. Jubayr narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbas, he said: When Musa said to the two women: ﴿What is your matter?﴾ "They said, 'We cannot water until the shepherds have dispatched [their flocks], and our father is a very old man'": that is, we are not able to water until the people have watered, then we follow their leftovers.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, His words: ﴿until the shepherds have dispatched﴾, he said: you wait, and you water from the surplus in the troughs of the shepherds.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿They said, "We cannot water until the shepherds have dispatched [their flocks]"﴾: two women who cannot contend with men, ﴿and our father is a very old man﴾, who is unable to bear that himself and cannot water his livestock; so we wait for the people, until when they have finished we water and then go away.

The readers differed in reading His words ﴿until the shepherds have dispatched﴾. The common readers of the Hijaz, except Abu Jaʿfar al-Qari', and the common readers of Iraq, except Abu ʿAmr, read ﴿yusdira al-ruʿaʾ﴾ with a dammed yaʾ (yusdiru, "they dispatch"); while Abu Jaʿfar and Abu ʿAmr read with a fathah on the yaʾ, "yasdura al-ruʿaʾ 'an al-hawd" (the shepherds go away from the trough). As for the others, they dammed the yaʾ, meaning: the shepherds dispatch their flocks. These are, in my view, two readings close in meaning; scholars among the readers have read with each of them, and whichever reader recites either of them is correct.

* *

His saying: ﴿and our father is a very old man﴾

They mean: because of old age and weakness he cannot water his livestock.

* *

His saying: ﴿So he watered for them﴾

It is mentioned that he, peace be upon him, opened for them the mouth of a well over which there was a stone that only a group of people could lift; then he drew water and watered their livestock from it.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad b. ʿAmr narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, he said: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, he said: He opened for them, from a well, a stone over its mouth, and watered for them from it.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, similar, and he added in it: Ibn Jurayj said: a stone that not even ten men could lift.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Abu Muʿawiya narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Hakam, from Shurayh, he said: He came upon a stone that could not be raised except by ten men, and he raised it alone.

- Musa narrated to us, he said: ʿAmr narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, he said: Musa had pity on them when they said: ﴿We cannot water until the shepherds have dispatched [their flocks], and our father is a very old man﴾; so he came to the well and uprooted a rock over the well which a group of the people of Madyan would gather around to lift. Musa watered for them one bucket, and their sheep were satisfied, and they returned quickly, for they had only been watering from the leftovers of the troughs.

- al-ʿAbbas narrated to me, he said: Yazid informed us, he said: al-Asbagh informed us, he said: al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Saʿid b. Jubayr narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿So he watered for them﴾: he began to scoop much water into the bucket until they were the first of the shepherds to be satisfied, and they went back to their father with their sheep.

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, and he said: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, he said: The Prophet of God ﷺ was charitable to them, watered for them, and it was not long before he had satisfied their sheep.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, he said: Musa took their bucket, then went forward to the water-carrier with his surplus strength, and contended with the people for the water until he held them back from it, then he watered for them.

**The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So he watered their flocks for them, then turned back to the shade and said, "My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need."﴾ (28:24)**

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Musa watered the flocks of the two women, then turned to the shade of a tree, which is reported to have been an acacia (samurah).

Those who said this:

* Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿then turned﴾: Musa turned to the shade of an acacia tree and said, ﴿My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need.﴾

* al-Abbas narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: al-Asbagh informed us, saying: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Musa went to a tree and sought shelter in its shade, ﴿and said, "My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need."﴾

* al-Husayn ibn Amr al-Anqazi narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr ibn Maymun, from Abdullah, who said: I rode my camel for two nights until I reached Madyan in the morning. I asked about the tree under which Musa had taken shelter, and there was a green tree, luxuriant. My camel went toward it, for it was hungry, and took hold of it, struggled with it for a while, then spat it out. So I invoked Allah for Musa, peace be upon him, and then I went back.

* * *

As for His saying, ﴿and said, "My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need."﴾

"In need" means in want. It is reported that the Prophet of Allah Musa, peace be upon him, said this while in great hardship, and he was alluding to the two women, hoping that they would feed him from what he suffered of severe hunger.

It has also been said: the "good" that the Prophet of Allah referred to when he said, ﴿for whatever good You send down to me, in need﴾, meant only a single meal of food.

The people of ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation, ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When Musa fled from Pharaoh, he suffered severe hunger, so that his intestines could be seen through the outer membrane of his abdomen (al-sifaq, the peritoneum). When he watered for the two women and took shelter in the shade, he said, ﴿My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need.﴾

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, saying: Anbasa narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying, ﴿And when he arrived at the water of Madyan﴾: He arrived at the water, and the greenness of the herbs could be seen in his belly from the emaciation. ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need."﴾ He said: a single meal.

* Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi narrated to me, saying: Hakkam ibn Salm narrated to us, from Anbasa, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying, ﴿And when he arrived at the water of Madyan﴾: He arrived at the water, and the greenness of the herbs was visible in his belly from the emaciation.

* Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, saying: Hakkam ibn Salm narrated to us, from Anbasa, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need﴾: He said: a single meal that day.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, regarding His saying, ﴿and said, "My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need."﴾ He said: He said this while he had neither a dirham nor a dinar with him.

* He said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need﴾: He asked for nothing but food.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿and said, "My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need."﴾ He said: He asked his Lord for nothing but food.

* Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: ﴿"My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need."﴾ He said: Ibn Abbas said: Musa said it, and if a man wished to look at the greenness of his intestines because of the severity of his hunger, he could have; and he asked Allah for nothing but a single morsel.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: ﴿"My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need."﴾ He said: The Prophet of Allah was in dire straits.

* Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, regarding His saying, ﴿indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need﴾: He said: It has reached me that Musa said it while the woman could hear him.

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to me, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿in need of good﴾ [﴿مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ﴾]: He said: food.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿in need of good﴾: He said: food.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying, ﴿indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need﴾: The food he asks for; he had no food with him, and he only asked for food.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 25:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then came to him one of the two women, walking shyly. She said, "Indeed, my father invites you so that he may reward you for having watered [our flock] for us." So when he came to him and related to him the narrative, he said, "Fear not. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people."﴾ (28:25)

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Then came to him one of the two women, walking shyly﴾ means: one of the two women for whom he had watered [their flock] came to Moses, walking shyly before Moses, having covered her face with her garment.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

- Abu al-Sa'ib and al-Fadl ibn al-Sabbah related to us, both saying: Ibn Fudayl related to us, from Dirar ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, from Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), regarding His saying: ﴿Then came to him one of the two women, walking shyly﴾, he said: "Veiled with the sleeve of her shift, or with the sleeve of her dress."

- Ibn WakI' related to us, he said: Abu Usamah related to us, from Hammad ibn Amr al-Asadi, from Abu Sinan, from Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: "Placing her hand over her face, veiled."

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Nawf: ﴿Then came to him one of the two women, walking shyly﴾, he said: "She had covered her face with her hands."

- He said: Yahya related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Nawf, similarly.

- Ibn WakI' related to us, he said: My father related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Nawf: ﴿Then came to him one of the two women, walking shyly﴾, he said: "Speaking, with her hands upon her face, and my father placed his hand upon his face."

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Isra'il related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr ibn Maymun: ﴿Then came to him one of the two women, walking shyly﴾, he said: "She was not a bold woman, going out and coming in frequently, but was placing her garment over her face, saying: ﴿Indeed, my father invites you so that he may reward you for having watered [our flock] for us﴾."

- Ibn WakI' related to us, he said: My father related to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr ibn Maymun, from Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him): ﴿Then came to him one of the two women, walking shyly﴾, he said: "She was not a bold woman, going out and coming in frequently, speaking with her hand over her face: ﴿Indeed, my father invites you so that he may reward you for having watered [our flock] for us﴾."

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, he said: Qurrah ibn Khalid related to us, he said: I heard al-Hasan say, regarding His saying: ﴿Then came to him one of the two women, walking shyly﴾, he said: "Far from vulgarity (al-badha')."

- Musa related to us, he said: Amr related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿walking shyly﴾, he said: "She came to him walking shyly before him."

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿Then came to him one of the two women, walking shyly﴾, he said: "Placing her hand upon her forehead."

And His saying: ﴿She said, "Indeed, my father invites you so that he may reward you for having watered [our flock] for us"﴾

His saying, mighty and majestic is He, means: the woman who came to Moses walking shyly said: "Indeed, my father invites you so that he may reward you": she says, "so that he may recompense you the wage for having watered [our flock] for us."

And His saying: ﴿So when he came to him and related to him the narrative﴾

He means: Moses went with her to her father. When he came to her father and related to him his story with Pharaoh and his people from the Copts, her father said to him: ﴿Fear not﴾, for you have ﴿escaped from the wrongdoing people﴾, meaning: from Pharaoh and his people, since he has no authority in our land where you are.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

- Al-Abbas related to me, he said: Yazid informed us, he said: Al-Asbagh related to us, he said: Al-Qasim related to us, he said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr related to us, from Ibn Abbas, he said: The father of the two girls was surprised at how quickly they returned with their sheep, their udders full and swollen, and he said: "Indeed, something has happened to you today."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: I think he said: "So they informed him of the news. When Moses came to him, he spoke to him: ﴿He said, 'Fear not. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people.'﴾ Pharaoh and his people have no authority over us, and we are not in his kingdom."

- Musa related to us, he said: Amr related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, he said: When the two girls returned to their father quickly, he asked them, and they informed him of the news of Moses. So he sent for him, and one of them came to him walking shyly, being shy of him, and said: ﴿Indeed, my father invites you so that he may reward you for having watered [our flock] for us.﴾ So he (Moses) stood up with her, and said to her: "Go ahead." She walked in front of him, but the wind blew against her, and he looked at her buttocks. So Moses said to her: "Walk behind me, and guide me to the path if I go astray." When the old man came and related the narrative to him, ﴿he said, "Fear not. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people."﴾

- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Then came to him one of the two women, walking shyly. She said, "Indeed, my father invites you so that he may reward you for having watered [our flock] for us."﴾ He said: Mutarrif said: "By Allah, if the Prophet of Allah had had anything, he would not have drunk the two of their milk mixed with water [[mudhiqayhuma: the dual of mudhiq, which is milk mixed with water and drunk. He means that Moses, peace be upon him, had no wealth or provision with him.]]; but hunger had driven him to that." ﴿So when he came to him and related to him the narrative, he said, "Fear not. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people."﴾

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, he said: They returned to their father at an hour when they would not usually return, so he noticed their state and asked them, and they informed him of the news. He said to one of them: "Hurry, bring him to me." She came to him shyly and came to him, and said: ﴿Indeed, my father invites you so that he may reward you for having watered [our flock] for us.﴾ So he went with her, as has been mentioned to me, and he said to her: "Walk behind me, and direct me to the way, and I will walk in front of you, for we do not look at the backs of women." When he came to him, she informed him of the news and of what had driven him out of his land. ﴿So when he came to him and related to him the narrative, he said, "Fear not. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people."﴾ She had informed her father of his saying: "We do not look at the backs of women."

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿She said, "O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy."﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: One of the two women for whom Musa gave water to their flocks said to her father when Musa came to him. The name of one of them was Safura, and the name of the other was Layya; it is also said: Shurfa.

◆ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Wahb ibn Sulayman al-Ramadi informed me, from Shu'ayb al-Jaba'i, who said: The names of the two maidens were Layya and Safura, and Musa's wife was Safura, daughter of Yathrun [[Yathrun and Yathra: so it is in the original. In al-'Ara'is (Qisas al-anbiya', by Abu Ishaq Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Nisaburi, known as al-Tha'labi, d. 427 AH, p. 174: "Thabrun"). It is perhaps a copyist's error.]], the priest of Madyan. And the kahin (priest) is a ḥibr (scholar).

◆ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: One of them was Safura, daughter of Yathrun, and her sister was Shara, and it is said: Layya; and they were the two who were holding back their flocks. As for their father, there is disagreement about his name. Some of them said: His name was Yathrun.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Amr ibn Murra, from Abu 'Ubayda, who said: The one who hired Musa was the son of Shu'ayb's brother, Yathrun.

◆ Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Amr ibn Murra, from Abu 'Ubayda, who said: The one who hired Musa was Yathrun, the son of Shu'ayb's brother, peace be upon him.

Others said: Rather, his name was Yathra.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salama, from Abu Hamza, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The one who hired Musa was Yathra, the lord of Madyan.

◆ Abu al-'Aliya al-'Abdi Isma'il ibn al-Haytham narrated to me, saying: Abu Qutayba narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salama, from Abu Hamza, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The one who hired Musa was Yathra, the lord of Madyan.

◆ Abu al-'Aliya al-'Abdi Isma'il ibn al-Haytham narrated to me, saying: Abu Qutayba narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salama, from Abu Hamza, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The name of the woman's father was Yathra.

Others said: Rather, his name was Shu'ayb, and they said: He is Shu'ayb the Prophet (ﷺ).

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Qurra ibn Khalid narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Hasan say: They say Shu'ayb was the companion of Musa, but he was the chief of the people of the water on that day.

Abu Ja'far said: This is something whose knowledge is not attained except through a report, and there is no report establishing it as binding evidence. So there is no statement more correct regarding this than what Allah, majestic is His praise, said: ﴿And he found, beside them, two women holding back [their flocks]... She said, "O my father, hire him."﴾ By her saying "hire him," she meant: hire him to herd your flock for you.

﴿Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy.﴾ She says: Indeed, the best one you can hire for herding is the strong, capable of guarding your flock and tending to it in its repair and welfare, the trustworthy whom you need not fear will betray you in what you entrust to him.

It was also said: When she said that to her father, her father disapproved of her describing him in this way and said to her: "And how do you know this?" She said: As for his strength, I saw what he lifted when he drew water at the well; and as for his trustworthiness, I saw him lower his gaze from me.

Reports from the people of interpretation came in similar terms.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: al-Asbagh ibn Zayd informed us, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: ﴿She said, "O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy."﴾ He said: Jealousy seized him so that he said: "And what do you know of his strength and trustworthiness?" She said: As for his strength, I saw what he did when he watered for us; I never saw a man stronger in that watering than him. As for his trustworthiness, when I came to him and approached him, he looked at me, and when he knew I was a woman, he lowered his head and did not raise it, nor did he look at me until he conveyed your message to him. Then he said: "Walk behind me and direct me on the way." He would not have done that unless he were trustworthy. So her father was relieved and believed her, and he thought well of him as she had said.

◆ Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, his words, to Musa: ﴿Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy.﴾ He says: Trustworthy in what he is entrusted with, trustworthy in what is deposited with him.

◆ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, his words: ﴿She said, "O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy."﴾ He said: When Musa watered for them, and she saw his strength, and he moved a stone over the well, which thirty men could not move, he removed it from the well. He went with the girl when she invited him, and he said to her: "Walk behind me and I will be in front of you," out of dislike that he should see anything of her from behind that Allah has forbidden him to look at. It was a windy day.

◆ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughira, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Nu'm, regarding His words: ﴿O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy.﴾ Her father said to her: "What did you see of his trustworthiness?" She said: When I invited him, I walked before him, and the wind kept striking my garments so that they clung to my body. He said: "Be behind me, and when you reach the road, go on." She said: And I saw him fill the basin with a single bucket.

◆ Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿the strong, the trustworthy﴾. He said: He lowered his gaze from them. Muhammad ibn 'Amr said in his report: "when" or "until he watered for them, and they went back." Al-Harith said in his report: "until he watered," without doubt.

◆ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: He removed a stone from the mouth of a well, and watered for them with it, and the trustworthy: that he lowered his gaze from them when he watered for them and they went back.

◆ Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar and Hani' ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Qasim, from Mujahid: ﴿Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy.﴾ He said: He lifted a stone that only a large group of people could lift.

◆ Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, who said 'Amr ibn Maymun, regarding His words: ﴿the strong, the trustworthy﴾: It was a windy day, and she said: "Do not walk in front of me, lest the wind shape you for me, but walk behind me and guide me to the road." He said: She said to him: "How did you know his strength?" She said: "The stone could not be lifted except by ten, and he lifted it alone."

◆ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to me, from al-Hajjaj ibn Artat, from al-Hakam, from Shurayh, regarding His words: ﴿the strong, the trustworthy﴾: As for his strength: he came to a stone that only ten could lift, and he lifted it alone. As for his trustworthiness: she walked in front of him and the wind described her, so he said to her: "Walk behind me and describe the road to me."

◆ Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Za'ida, from al-A'mash, who said: I asked Tamim ibn Ibrahim: "How did you know his trustworthiness?" He said: "By his glance, by his lowering his gaze from her."

◆ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy.﴾ He said: The strong in the work, the trustworthy in what he is entrusted with.

He said: It was mentioned to us that what she saw of his strength was that her flock did not stay long before he watered them; and that the trustworthiness she saw in him was that when she came to summon him, he told her: "Be behind me," and he disliked to walk with her in front of him. That is what she saw of his strength and trustworthiness.

◆ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, his words: ﴿O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy.﴾ He said: We were told that his strength was in how quickly he watered their sheep. And we were told that he filled the basin with one bucket. As for his trustworthiness, he told her to walk behind him.

◆ Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿She said, "O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy."﴾ She was the maiden who invited him. The shaykh said: "This strength you have seen when he uprooted the rock. As for his trustworthiness, what do you know of it?" She said: "I walked in front of him, and he did not wish to betray me in myself, so he commanded me to walk behind him."

◆ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿She said, "O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy."﴾ He said to her: "And what is your knowledge of his strength and trustworthiness?" She said: "As for his strength, he lifted the rock that was over the well of the family of so-and-so, which could not be lifted by fewer than seven men. As for his trustworthiness, when I came to summon him, he said: 'Be behind my back, and point out your house to me,' so I knew that this was from him a sign of trustworthiness."

◆ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿She said, "O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy."﴾ Because of what she saw of his strength, and his saying to her what he said, "Walk behind me, lest he see anything of her that he would dislike," this increased her in his regard.

**Commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿He said, "I wish to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine, on condition that you serve me for eight years. But if you complete ten, it is from you. I do not want to burden you. You will find me, God willing, among the righteous."﴾ (28:27)**

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿He said﴾, meaning the father of the two women for whom Musa had watered (their flock), to Musa: ﴿"I wish to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine, on condition that you serve me for eight years"﴾. By his words ﴿"on condition that you serve me"﴾ he means: on condition that you reward me, through her marriage, with the herding of my livestock for eight years. This is from the people's saying, "Allah rewarded you (ajarak Allah), so He is the one who rewards (yaʾjurak), meaning: Allah gave you a reward (athabak Allah)." The Arabs also say, "I hired the laborer (ajartu al-ajīr), I hire him (ājuruhu)," meaning: I gave him that (wage), just as one says, "I took it, so I take it." Some of the Arabic grammarians from Basra have related that the language of the Arabs is: "I hired (ajart) my boy, so he is hired (majūr)," and "I made him hire (ājartuhu), so he is hired out (muʾjar)," meaning: I made him do (it).

He said: Some of them said: "He hired (ājarahu), so he is one who hires out (muʾājir)," meaning: he made him do (it) in a mutual way (fāʿalahu). It seems to me that the father of the two women made the bride-price of his daughter, whom he married to Musa, the herding of his livestock by Musa, for eight years. The word ḥijaj (years) means years.

* *

As for His words: ﴿"But if you complete ten, it is from you"﴾

He says: If you complete the eight years that I stipulated for you in exchange for marrying you to one of my daughters, by making them ten years, then that is a kindness from you, and it is not something I stipulated on you in return for marrying you to my daughter. ﴿"And I do not want to burden you"﴾ by stipulating on you that the eight years become ten. ﴿"You will find me, God willing, among the righteous"﴾ in fulfilling what I have said to you.

As related:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding ﴿"You will find me, God willing, among the righteous"﴾: that is, in good companionship and in fulfilling what I have said.

* *

On the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿He said, "That is between me and you. Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there will be no injustice against me. And Allah is Witness over what we say."﴾ (28:28)

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿He said﴾, meaning Musa to the father of the two women: ﴿"That is between me and you"﴾, that is, what you have said, that you will marry me to one of your two daughters on condition that I serve you for eight years, is binding between me and you, and each of us must fulfill to the other what he has obligated himself to.

* *

As for His words: ﴿"Whichever of the two terms I fulfill"﴾

He says: whichever of the two terms, the eight years or the ten years, I complete, meaning: I finish it and fulfill it to you by tending your sheep and livestock. ﴿"There will be no injustice against me"﴾ means: you have no right to wrong me by demanding from me more than that. The word "mā" in His words "ayyamā al-ajalayn" is an added particle that connects with it, meaning "whichever" always.[[It appears that there is a lacuna in the original text, which can be known from al-Farraʾ's explanation of the following verse. His words "always" mean that the added (mā) always attaches to the word ayy. His words "and the grammarians claim..." etc. mean that the grammarians said: "mā" either attaches to the word ayy, or comes after what "ayy" is added to, and this is more common in the speech of the Arabs, as is known from the two verses cited below.]] The grammarians claim that this is more common in the speech of the Arabs than "ayy," and they cited the saying of the poet:

"And whichever of them I follow, indeed I am
Eager to follow the path of the one I am following."[[This verse is among the evidences of al-Farraʾ in Maʿānī al-Qurʾān (p. 241) that "mā" may be added after what is annexed to "ayy" as a conditional particle. He said: His words "ayyamā al-ajalayn" make "mā," which is one of the conditional particles, with "ayy." It is also in the reading of Abdullah (ibn Masʿud): "Ayy al-ajalayn mā qaḍaytu fa-lā ʿudwāna ʿalayy." And this is more common in the speech of the Arabs than the first. It is clear from this that the author's expression is deficient, or that there is a missing part before his words "and the grammarians claim...," etc.]]

And ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās said:

"So whichever of yours and mine was evil,
Let him be shackled to the assembly, not seeing it."[[This verse is by ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās, and its citation has been mentioned previously in several places. The evidence here is the addition of "mā" after what "ayy" is annexed to. Al-maqāma means the assembly. "Shackled to the assembly" is an invocation against him that he be blinded, so that he cannot reach the gathering of his people unless he is shackled.]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿"And Allah is Witness over what we say"﴾

Ibn Ishaq used to hold that this statement was from the father of the two women.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Musa said: ﴿"That is between me and you. Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there will be no injustice against me."﴾ He (the father) said: "Yes, and Allah is Witness over what we say." So he married him to her, and he stayed with him, serving him, working for him in tending his sheep, and in whatever else he needed from him.

On the wife of Musa, Ṣafūrā or her sister Sharfā or Layyā:

⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: The girl who called him is the one who was married.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: He (the father) said to him: ﴿"I wish to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine, on condition that you serve me..."﴾ until the end of the verse. He said: And which of them do you want to marry me to? He said: The one who called you. He said: Indeed she is innocent of what has entered your mind about her. He said: She is with you as such, so he married him to her.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding His words: ﴿"Whichever of the two terms I fulfill"﴾.

Those who said that:

⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī: ﴿"That is between me and you. Whichever of the two terms I fulfill"﴾: either eight or ten.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Lahīʿa informed me, from ʿImāra ibn Ghaziyya, from Yahyā ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, and a man asked him: ﴿"Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there will be no injustice against me"﴾. Al-Qāsim said: I do not mind which of them it was; it is only a promise and a fulfillment.

* *

As for His words: ﴿"And Allah is Witness over what we say"﴾

He says: And Allah is witness and guardian over what each of us has obligated himself to the other by this statement.

Like what was said by:

⁕ Al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid: ﴿"And Allah is Witness over what we say"﴾. He said: a witness over the words of Musa and his father-in-law.

It is mentioned that when Musa and his companion concluded this contract between them, he ordered one of his two daughters to give Musa a staff from among the staves that shepherds carry, and she gave it to him. Some of them mentioned that it was the staff that Allah made a sign for him. Others said that it was a staff that Gabriel, peace be upon him, gave him.

Those who said that:

⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī, who said: He (the father of the two women) ordered one of his daughters to go to him, meaning to go to Musa with a staff. So she came to him with a staff, and that staff was a staff which a angel in the form of a man had entrusted to him. He handed it to him, and the girl went in, took the staff, and brought it to him. When the old man saw it, he said: Go back to him, do not bring anything other than it. So she threw it, wanting to take another, but nothing came into her hand except that one; she kept trying, and each time nothing came out in her hand but it. When he saw that, he went to it, took it out with him, and tended his flock with it. Then the old man regretted and said: It was a deposit. So he went out to meet Musa, and when he met him he said: Give me the staff. Musa said: It is my staff. He refused to give it, so they disputed, and they agreed to make the first man who met them their judge. Then an angel came to them walking, and said: Place it on the ground; whoever lifts it, it is his. The old man tried to lift it but could not, and Musa took it in his hand and lifted it, so the old man left it to him, and he tended his flock for him for ten years. Abdullah ibn ʿAbbās said: Musa was more deserving of fulfilling (the contract).

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: He (the father of the girl) said, when he married her to Musa: Enter that room and take a staff, lean on it. So he entered, and when he stood at the door of the room, that staff flew to him, and he took it. He said: Return it and take another in its place. So he returned it, then went to take another, but it flew to him as it was. He said: I will not return it. He did that three times. Then he said: Return it. He said: I do not find another today. So he turned to his daughter and said to her: Indeed your husband is a prophet.

Those who said: The staff that was the sign was a staff that Musa had been given by Gabriel, peace be upon him:

⁕ Al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Abū Bakr, who said: I asked ʿIkrima, and he said: As for the staff of Musa, Adam came out of Paradise with it; then Gabriel, peace be upon him, took it back after that, met Musa with it at night, and handed it to him.
