The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding His words: ﴿"Whichever of the two terms I fulfill"﴾.

Those who said that:

⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī: ﴿"That is between me and you. Whichever of the two terms I fulfill"﴾: either eight or ten.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Lahīʿa informed me, from ʿImāra ibn Ghaziyya, from Yahyā ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, and a man asked him: ﴿"Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there will be no injustice against me"﴾. Al-Qāsim said: I do not mind which of them it was; it is only a promise and a fulfillment.

* *

As for His words: ﴿"And Allah is Witness over what we say"﴾

He says: And Allah is witness and guardian over what each of us has obligated himself to the other by this statement.

Like what was said by:

⁕ Al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid: ﴿"And Allah is Witness over what we say"﴾. He said: a witness over the words of Musa and his father-in-law.

It is mentioned that when Musa and his companion concluded this contract between them, he ordered one of his two daughters to give Musa a staff from among the staves that shepherds carry, and she gave it to him. Some of them mentioned that it was the staff that Allah made a sign for him. Others said that it was a staff that Gabriel, peace be upon him, gave him.

Those who said that:

⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī, who said: He (the father of the two women) ordered one of his daughters to go to him, meaning to go to Musa with a staff. So she came to him with a staff, and that staff was a staff which a angel in the form of a man had entrusted to him. He handed it to him, and the girl went in, took the staff, and brought it to him. When the old man saw it, he said: Go back to him, do not bring anything other than it. So she threw it, wanting to take another, but nothing came into her hand except that one; she kept trying, and each time nothing came out in her hand but it. When he saw that, he went to it, took it out with him, and tended his flock with it. Then the old man regretted and said: It was a deposit. So he went out to meet Musa, and when he met him he said: Give me the staff. Musa said: It is my staff. He refused to give it, so they disputed, and they agreed to make the first man who met them their judge. Then an angel came to them walking, and said: Place it on the ground; whoever lifts it, it is his. The old man tried to lift it but could not, and Musa took it in his hand and lifted it, so the old man left it to him, and he tended his flock for him for ten years. Abdullah ibn ʿAbbās said: Musa was more deserving of fulfilling (the contract).

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: He (the father of the girl) said, when he married her to Musa: Enter that room and take a staff, lean on it. So he entered, and when he stood at the door of the room, that staff flew to him, and he took it. He said: Return it and take another in its place. So he returned it, then went to take another, but it flew to him as it was. He said: I will not return it. He did that three times. Then he said: Return it. He said: I do not find another today. So he turned to his daughter and said to her: Indeed your husband is a prophet.

Those who said: The staff that was the sign was a staff that Musa had been given by Gabriel, peace be upon him:

⁕ Al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Abū Bakr, who said: I asked ʿIkrima, and he said: As for the staff of Musa, Adam came out of Paradise with it; then Gabriel, peace be upon him, took it back after that, met Musa with it at night, and handed it to him.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 29:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when Musa had fulfilled the term and set out with his family, he perceived a fire from the side of the Mount. He said to his family, "Wait, indeed I have perceived a fire. Perhaps I will bring you from it news or a burning brand from the fire, that you may warm yourselves."﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: So when Musa fulfilled for his father-in-law the term upon which he had parted from him, at his marrying him to his daughter, and it has been mentioned that what he fulfilled of the two terms was the more complete and more perfect of them, namely the ten years, although some of the people of knowledge have related from him that he said: he added ten more to the ten.

Mention of those who said: what he fulfilled of that was the ten years:

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas: Which of the two terms did Musa fulfil? He said: The better of them and the more complete of them.

* Ibn Wakic narrated to us, he said: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who was asked: Which of the two terms did Musa fulfil? He said: The more complete of them and the better of them.

* Muhammad ibn Umara narrated to me, he said: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, he said: Musa ibn Ubayda narrated to us, from his brother, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Musa fulfilled the last of the two terms.

* Ibn Wakic narrated to us, he said: Ibn Ubayda narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from Ikrimah: Ibn Abbas was asked: Which of the two terms did Musa fulfil? He said: The more complete of them and the more perfect of them.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salama narrated to us, he said: Ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Hakim ibn Jubayr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A Jew in Kufa said, while I was preparing for the pilgrimage: "I see you are a man who seeks knowledge. Tell me, which of the two terms did Musa fulfil?" I said: "I do not know, but I am now going to the scholar of the Arabs, meaning Ibn Abbas; I will ask him about it." When I arrived at Mecca I asked Ibn Abbas about that and told him what the Jew had said. Ibn Abbas said: "He fulfilled the more numerous of them and the more pleasant of them, for indeed the Prophet, when he promises, does not break it." Sa'id said: I then went to Iraq, met the Jew, and informed him, and he said: "He has spoken truly, and this was not revealed to Musa; and God knows best."

* He said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: al-Asbagh ibn Zayd narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A man from the Christians asked me: "Which of the two terms did Musa fulfil?" I said: "I do not know," and at that time I did not know. Then I met Ibn Abbas and mentioned to him what the Christian had asked me. He said: "Did you not know that eight is obligatory upon him? The Prophet of God did not reduce any of it. And you know that God was the one who fulfilled for Musa the promise which He had made him, for He fulfilled ten years."

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning ﴿So when Musa fulfilled the term﴾, he said: Ibn Abbas related: The Prophet of God pastured for him the more numerous and the more pleasant of them.

* Ibn Wakic narrated to us, he said: my father narrated to us, from Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ was asked: "Which of the two terms did Musa fulfil?" He said: "The more faithful of them and the more complete of them."

* Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi narrated to us, he said: al-Humaydi Abu Bakr ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr [[In al-Khulasa by al-Khazraji: Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr ibn Abd Allah (Abu Ubayd Allah) al-Asadi al-Humaydi al-Makki, one of the imams.]] narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, he said: Ibrahim ibn Yahya ibn Abi Ya'qub narrated to me, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "I asked Jibril: Which of the two terms did Musa fulfil? He said: The more complete of them and the more perfect of them."

* al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujahid said: The Prophet ﷺ asked Jibril: "Which of the two terms did Musa fulfil?" He said: "I will ask Israfil." He asked him, and he said: "I will ask God, blessed and exalted is He." He asked Him, and He said: "The more righteous of them and the more faithful of them."

Mention of those who said: he fulfilled the ten years and added ten more to the ten:

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿So when Musa fulfilled the term﴾, he said: Ten years, then he stayed after that ten more.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿Musa fulfilled the term﴾: ten years, then he stayed after that ten more.

* al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, he said: my father narrated to us, from Qatada, he said: Anas narrated to us, he said: When the Prophet of God Musa called his father-in-law to the term that was between them, his father-in-law said to him: "Every sheep that gives birth to a lamb of a colour other than its own shall be yours." So he devised a plan: he set up a shape before the water, and when the sheep saw the shape, they were frightened and ran about in a flurry, and they all gave birth to spotted young, except one sheep, and he took their young that year.

* * *

And His saying: ﴿and set out with his family, he perceived a fire from the side of the Mount﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿So when Musa fulfilled the term and set out with his family﴾, journeying with them toward his home from Egypt, ﴿he perceived from the side of the Mount﴾. By His saying "perceived" (anasa) is meant: he saw and sensed, as al-'Ajjaj said:

*He perceived the falcon of an open plain and swooped down, / its two wings reaching toward the Mount, and it passed.*

[[These are two verses of rajaz by al-'Ajjaj the rajaz poet (his Diwan, Leipzig edition 1903, p. 17; the first verse is no. 76 and the second no. 74). In one version of the first verse "absara" (saw) stands in place of "anasa", and they have the same meaning. "Al-Kharbān" with a kasra is the plural of "kharab" (like "sabab"), the male bustard, and it is said it is the whole bustard. Its plurals include also "akhrab" and "kharab". "Inkadara" means: hastened and swooped. The pronoun in both verbs refers to the falcon mentioned in the preceding verse; the poet likens the praised one, Umar ibn Ubayd Allah, to a falcon swooping on his enemies, as a falcon swoops on a bustard and catches it. See the full explanation of the second verse in volume 9, p. 243. This rajaz praises Umar ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Ma'mar, whom Ibn al-Zubayr appointed over Iraq to fight Ubayd Allah ibn Bashir ibn al-Majuz of the Kharijites; in that war he appointed his brother Uthman ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Ma'mar, who was killed. (See al-Baladhuri, manuscript at the Egyptian National Library.)]]

The people of interpretation have spoken in accordance with what we have said on this, and we have previously mentioned the narrations on it, except that we mention here some of what we did not mention before.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning ﴿he perceived from the side of the Mount a fire, he said to his family: wait, indeed I have perceived a fire﴾: that is, I sensed a fire.

We have already explained the meaning of "the Mount" earlier, with its evidences and what is related on it from the people of interpretation.

* * *

And His saying: ﴿He said to his family: wait, indeed I have perceived a fire﴾

He says: Musa said to his family: "Be patient and wait; indeed I have seen a fire," ﴿perhaps I will bring you from it﴾, meaning from the fire, ﴿news, or a burning brand from the fire﴾. He says: or I will bring you a thick piece of firewood in which there is fire, which is like the stump from the root of a tree. From it is the saying of Ibn Muqbil:

*The gatherers of firewood for Layla spent the night seeking for her / sturdy stumps, neither weak nor smoking.*

[[The verse is by Tamim ibn Muqbil (Lisan al-Arab: j-dh-a). He said: it is said of the root of a tree: "jidhya" and "jadha'" (the first with a kasra on the jim, the second with a fath). Al-Asma'i: "jidhm" of everything and its "jidhy" is its root, and "al-jada'" are the great root-stocks of trees, whose upper part has decayed while the lower part remains. Tamim ibn Muqbil said: "The gatherers of Layla..." the verse. "Hawatib" is the plural of "hatiba", a woman who gathers firewood. Abu Ubayda said in Majaz al-Qur'an: "a brand from the fire": that is, a thick piece of firewood with no flame, like the stump from the root of a tree; Ibn Muqbil said: "The gatherers..." the verse. "Al-Khawwar" is the weak one. "Al-Da'r" is the wood that smokes much and does not burn well, the bad smoke. It is also said that "al-da'r" among firewood is the decayed one.]]

The Arabs have three dialect forms for "jidhwa": "jidhwa" with a kasra on the jim, by which the readers of the Hijaz, Basra and some of the readers of Kufa recited; this is the most famous of the three forms; and "jadhwa" with a fath on the jim, by which some readers of Kufa also recited. [[The copyist omitted the third form, which is: "judhwa" (with a damma on the jim), by which it was also recited.]] Although these three forms are well known in Arab speech, recitation with the most famous of them is more pleasing to me, though I do not reject the recitation of anyone who recites with other than the most famous of them.

The people of interpretation have spoken in accordance with what we have said about the meaning of "jadhwa".

Mention of those who said that:

* Ali narrated to me, he said: Abd Allah narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿or a burning brand from the fire﴾, he said: a meteor.

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning ﴿or a burning brand﴾: "al-jadhwa" is the root of a tree that has fire in it.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed I have perceived a fire, perhaps I will bring you from it news or a burning brand from the fire﴾, he said: the root of the tree, at the end of which is fire; this is His saying ﴿or a burning brand﴾. He said: the palm frond with fire in it. Ma'mar said: Qatada said concerning ﴿or a burning brand﴾: or a flame of fire.

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿or a burning brand from the fire﴾, he said: the root of a tree.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, ﴿or a burning brand from the fire﴾, he said: the root of a tree.

* Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿or a burning brand from the fire﴾: "al-jadhwa" is the piece of firewood in which there is fire; that is the "jadhwa".

* * *

And His saying: ﴿that you may warm yourselves﴾

He says: that you may be warmed by it from the cold, for it was in winter.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 30:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when he came to it, he was called from the right side of the valley, in the blessed spot, from the tree: "O Moses, indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ (28:30)

His exalted remembrance says: when Moses came to the fire which he perceived from the side of Mount Sinai (al-Tur), ﴿he was called from the right side of the valley﴾. By "al-shati' (shore, bank)" is meant the shore (al-shatt), which is the side and slope of the valley. The word shati' has the plurals shawati' and shutan. Al-Shatt is the plural of shatt (shore, edge). "Al-ayman (the right)" is an adjective qualifying al-shati', meaning on the right of Moses.

Those who give interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿from the right side of the valley﴾. Ibn Amr said in his report: "near the Tur." Al-Harith said in his report: "from the right side of the valley, near the Tur, on the right of Moses."

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿So when he came to it, he was called from the right side of the valley﴾ — he said: the side of the valley on the right of Moses, near the Tur.

* *

His saying: ﴿in the blessed spot﴾

This is connected to al-shati' (the shore).

The meaning of the speech is: when he came to it, God called Moses from the right side of the valley, in the blessed spot of it, from the tree: ﴿"O Moses, indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾

It has been said that the meaning of His saying: ﴿from the tree﴾ is: near the tree.

Mention of those who said that:

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿So when he came to it, he was called from the right side of the valley, in the blessed spot, from the tree﴾ — he said: he was called from near the tree: ﴿"O Moses, indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾

It has been said that the tree from which Moses heard his Lord was an 'awsaj (a thorny tree). Others said: rather, it was a 'ulayq (a thorny bush, dodder/boxthorn).

Mention of those who said that:

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Abu Sufyan related to me, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿in the blessed spot, from the tree﴾ — he said: the tree is an 'awsaj. Ma'mar said, from Qatadah: the staff of Moses was of 'awsaj, and the tree was of 'awsaj.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some whom one does not suspect, from some of the people of knowledge, concerning ﴿Indeed, I have perceived a fire﴾ — he said: he went toward it, and it was a tree of 'ulayq. Some of the People of the Book say it was an 'awsajah.

- Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from al-A'mash, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from Abdullah, who said: I saw the tree from which Moses, peace be upon him, was called: it was a green samura tree, its leaves trembling.

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And throw down your staff.﴾ So when he saw it moving as if it were a snake, he turned to flee and did not look back. ﴿O Moses, come forward and do not fear; indeed you are among those secure.﴾ [28:31] ﴿Insert your hand into your bosom; it will come out white without disease. And draw your arm close to your side against fear. These are two proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his chiefs. Indeed, they have been a defiantly disobedient people.﴾ [28:32]

His exalted remembrance says: Moses was called: ﴿O Moses, indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds, and [I said], "Throw down your staff."﴾ So Moses threw it down, and it became a moving snake.

﴿So when he saw it﴾ (Moses saw it) ﴿moving﴾, meaning: it moved and shook ﴿as if it were a jann﴾. The jann is the singular of jinn-snakes (jinnan), a known kind of snake, and among the largest of them. The meaning of the statement is: as if it were a jann among the snakes. ﴿He turned to flee, retreating﴾, meaning: Moses turned away fleeing from it.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿he turned to flee, retreating﴾: fleeing from it. ﴿And did not look back﴾: meaning he did not return upon his heels.

We have already mentioned the narrations on this and what the people of interpretation have said earlier, so we disliked repeating it, but we will mention some of what we did not mention there.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And did not look back﴾: meaning he did not turn around out of fear.

* Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And did not look back﴾: meaning he did not wait.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿O Moses, come forward and do not fear﴾

His exalted remembrance says: Moses was called: O Moses, come to Me and do not fear what you are fleeing from. ﴿Indeed you are among those secure﴾, from anything that could harm you; it is only your staff.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿Insert your hand into your bosom﴾

Meaning: put your hand in. There are two dialects: salaktuhu and aslaktuhu. ﴿Into your bosom﴾, meaning: into the bosom of your shirt.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Insert your hand into your bosom﴾: that is, into the bosom of your shirt.

We have already explained earlier the reason why he was commanded to put his hand into the bosom rather than the sleeve.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿It will come out white without disease﴾

Meaning: it will come out white, without vitiligo.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Qurrah ibn Khalid narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿Insert your hand into your bosom; it will come out white without disease﴾, he said: It came out like a lamp, and Moses was certain that he had met his Lord.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿And draw your arm close to your side﴾

Meaning: draw your hand close to yourself.

As related:

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said regarding ﴿And draw your arm close to your side﴾: he said: your hand.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And draw your arm close to your side﴾, he said: "And its two wings: the forearm. The upper arm is the janah (wing), and the palm is the yad (hand)": ﴿Draw your hand to your side; it will come out white without disease﴾.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿From fear﴾

Meaning: from the terror and dread that has overtaken you from witnessing what you saw of the horror of the snake.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said so:

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿from fear﴾, he said: al-Faraq (dread).

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And draw your arm close to your side against fear﴾: that is, from terror.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿from fear﴾: from the dread and fear that entered him from the snake. He said: that is the rahb, and he recited the word of Allah: ﴿They call upon Us in hope and in fear﴾, meaning: in fear and in hope.

The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of reciters of the Hijaz and Basra read ﴿min al-rahab﴾ with a fatha on the ra and the ha. The majority of reciters of Kufa read ﴿min al-ruhb﴾ with a damma on the ra and a sukun on the ha. The position regarding this is that both are readings with agreeing meanings, both well known among the reciters of the regions, so whichever one the reciter reads is correct.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿These are two proofs from your Lord﴾

His exalted remembrance says: These two that I have shown you, O Moses, the transformation of the staff into a snake, and your hand, which was brown, becoming white and shining without disease, are two proofs (burhanan): meaning two signs and two evidences. The root of burhan is bayan (clarity). It is said of a man who, when asked for proof of his statement, says: "Bring your proof for what you say," meaning: bring the clarification and confirmation of that.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said so:

* Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿These are two proofs from your Lord﴾: the staff and the hand are two signs.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the word of Allah ﴿These are two proofs from your Lord﴾: two clarifications from your Lord.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding ﴿These are two proofs from your Lord﴾: these are two proofs.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿These are two proofs from your Lord﴾: he recited: ﴿Bring your proof﴾, meaning a sign we know, and said: ﴿Two proofs﴾ are two signs from Allah.

The reciters differed in reading His words ﴿fa-dhanika﴾. The majority of reciters of the regions, except Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr, read ﴿fa-dhanika﴾ with a light nun, as it is the dual nun. Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read ﴿fa-dhanni-ka﴾ with a doubled nun.

The grammarians differed on the reason for doubling it. Some Basran grammarians said: the nun was doubled for emphasis, just as they added the lam in that. Some Kufan grammarians said: it was doubled to distinguish it from the nun that drops in the construct (idafa), because hatani and hadhani are not made construct. Another among them said: it is from the dialect of those who say "hadha'an" and add an alif upon an alif, so likewise they add a nun upon a nun to distinguish them from the declinable nouns; and for ﴿dhanika﴾ it was only so among those who say "hadhan ya hadha," disliking the dual in the construct, so they followed it with the lam, because the construct is followed by the lam. Abu 'Amr used to say: doubling the nun in ﴿dhanika﴾ is from the dialect of Quraysh.

Meaning: ﴿to Pharaoh and his chiefs﴾, to Pharaoh and the nobles of his people, as a proof against them and an indication of the truth of your prophethood, O Moses. ﴿Indeed they have been a people who are defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning: indeed Pharaoh and his chiefs were a disbelieving people.

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And throw down your staff.﴾ So when he saw it moving as if it were a snake, he turned to flee and did not look back. ﴿O Moses, come forward and do not fear; indeed you are among those secure.﴾ [28:31] ﴿Insert your hand into your bosom; it will come out white without disease. And draw your arm close to your side against fear. These are two proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his chiefs. Indeed, they have been a defiantly disobedient people.﴾ [28:32]

His exalted remembrance says: Moses was called: ﴿O Moses, indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds, and [I said], "Throw down your staff."﴾ So Moses threw it down, and it became a moving snake.

﴿So when he saw it﴾ (Moses saw it) ﴿moving﴾, meaning: it moved and shook ﴿as if it were a jann﴾. The jann is the singular of jinn-snakes (jinnan), a known kind of snake, and among the largest of them. The meaning of the statement is: as if it were a jann among the snakes. ﴿He turned to flee, retreating﴾, meaning: Moses turned away fleeing from it.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿he turned to flee, retreating﴾: fleeing from it. ﴿And did not look back﴾: meaning he did not return upon his heels.

We have already mentioned the narrations on this and what the people of interpretation have said earlier, so we disliked repeating it, but we will mention some of what we did not mention there.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And did not look back﴾: meaning he did not turn around out of fear.

* Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And did not look back﴾: meaning he did not wait.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿O Moses, come forward and do not fear﴾

His exalted remembrance says: Moses was called: O Moses, come to Me and do not fear what you are fleeing from. ﴿Indeed you are among those secure﴾, from anything that could harm you; it is only your staff.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿Insert your hand into your bosom﴾

Meaning: put your hand in. There are two dialects: salaktuhu and aslaktuhu. ﴿Into your bosom﴾, meaning: into the bosom of your shirt.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Insert your hand into your bosom﴾: that is, into the bosom of your shirt.

We have already explained earlier the reason why he was commanded to put his hand into the bosom rather than the sleeve.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿It will come out white without disease﴾

Meaning: it will come out white, without vitiligo.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Qurrah ibn Khalid narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿Insert your hand into your bosom; it will come out white without disease﴾, he said: It came out like a lamp, and Moses was certain that he had met his Lord.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿And draw your arm close to your side﴾

Meaning: draw your hand close to yourself.

As related:

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said regarding ﴿And draw your arm close to your side﴾: he said: your hand.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And draw your arm close to your side﴾, he said: "And its two wings: the forearm. The upper arm is the janah (wing), and the palm is the yad (hand)": ﴿Draw your hand to your side; it will come out white without disease﴾.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿From fear﴾

Meaning: from the terror and dread that has overtaken you from witnessing what you saw of the horror of the snake.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said so:

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿from fear﴾, he said: al-Faraq (dread).

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And draw your arm close to your side against fear﴾: that is, from terror.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿from fear﴾: from the dread and fear that entered him from the snake. He said: that is the rahb, and he recited the word of Allah: ﴿They call upon Us in hope and in fear﴾, meaning: in fear and in hope.

The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of reciters of the Hijaz and Basra read ﴿min al-rahab﴾ with a fatha on the ra and the ha. The majority of reciters of Kufa read ﴿min al-ruhb﴾ with a damma on the ra and a sukun on the ha. The position regarding this is that both are readings with agreeing meanings, both well known among the reciters of the regions, so whichever one the reciter reads is correct.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿These are two proofs from your Lord﴾

His exalted remembrance says: These two that I have shown you, O Moses, the transformation of the staff into a snake, and your hand, which was brown, becoming white and shining without disease, are two proofs (burhanan): meaning two signs and two evidences. The root of burhan is bayan (clarity). It is said of a man who, when asked for proof of his statement, says: "Bring your proof for what you say," meaning: bring the clarification and confirmation of that.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said so:

* Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿These are two proofs from your Lord﴾: the staff and the hand are two signs.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the word of Allah ﴿These are two proofs from your Lord﴾: two clarifications from your Lord.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding ﴿These are two proofs from your Lord﴾: these are two proofs.

Abu 'Amr used to say: doubling the nun in ﴿dhanika﴾ is from the dialect of Quraysh.

Meaning: ﴿to Pharaoh and his chiefs﴾, to Pharaoh and the nobles of his people, as a proof against them and an indication of the truth of your prophethood, O Moses. ﴿Indeed they have been a people who are defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning: indeed Pharaoh and his chiefs were a disbelieving people.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said: "My Lord, I killed a man among them, so I fear that they will kill me. And my brother Aaron, he is more eloquent in tongue than I, so send him with me as a helper, to confirm me. Indeed I fear that they will deny me."﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿He said﴾, that is Moses: ﴿"My Lord, I killed a man from the people of Pharaoh, so I fear that if I come to them I will not be able to clear myself with proof, that they will kill me"﴾, because there is a knot in my tongue, and I cannot make clear with it what I want to say. ﴿"And my brother Aaron, he is more eloquent in tongue than I"﴾ means: he is better at expressing what he wants to express. ﴿"So send him with me as a helper"﴾ means: as an aide. ﴿"To confirm me"﴾: that is, to explain on my behalf what I address to them.

As related:

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding ﴿"And my brother Aaron, he is more eloquent in tongue than I, so send him with me as a helper, to confirm me"﴾: that is, to make clear to them on my behalf what I speak to them, for he understands what they do not understand. It has also been said: Moses only asked his Lord to support him with his brother, because when two people agree upon good, the soul is more at rest with confirming the two than with confirming the report of one alone.

Mention of those who said that:

* Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿"So send him with me as a helper, to confirm me"﴾, "Because two are more worthy to be believed than one."

And according to what we have said about this, the people of interpretation have said.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa narrated to us, both from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿"So send him with me as a helper, to confirm me"﴾: "as an aide."
* Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.
* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿"As a helper, to confirm me"﴾: that is, "an aide."

Others said: the meaning of that is: "so that he may confirm me."

Mention of those who said that:

* Ali narrated to me, he said: Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿"As a helper, to confirm me"﴾: he says, "so that he may confirm me."
* Musa narrated to us, he said: Amr narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿"So send him with me as a helper, to confirm me"﴾: he says, "so that he may confirm me."
* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿"As a helper, to confirm me"﴾: he says, "so that he may confirm me." And "ridR" (helper) in the speech of the Arabs means aid; it is said from it: "I have ardhadtu so-and-so in his affair," meaning: I sufficed him and helped him.

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His saying: ﴿"to confirm me"﴾ (yusaddiqunī). The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz and Basra recited it: "ridan yusaddiqnī" with a jussive on yusaddiqnī. Asim and Hamzah recited: "yaṣduqunī" with a raised ending. Whoever raised it made it a relative clause describing the helper, meaning: "so send him with me as a helper of such a description that he confirms me." Whoever made it jussive made it a response to His saying "so send him," since when you send him, he confirms me as a statement of fact. The raised reading is the more preferred of the two recitations in my view, because it is Moses asking his Lord to send his brother as an aide to him with this description.

And His saying: ﴿"Indeed I fear that they will deny me."﴾

That is: "Indeed I fear that they will not believe me in what I say to them: 'Indeed I have been sent to you.'"

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿He said: "We will strengthen your arm through your brother, and We will give you both authority, so they shall not reach you. With Our signs, you two and whoever follows you will be the victorious."﴾ (35)

His exalted remembrance says: God said to Musa, ﴿We will strengthen your arm﴾; that is, We will fortify you and help you through your brother. The Arabs say, when a man honours another man, helps him, and protects him from one who wishes him harm: "So-and-so has strengthened the arm of so-and-so," and it derives from "he supported him in his affair" (ʿāḍadahu ʿalā amrihi), when he helps him. Among the instances of this is the verse of Ibn Muqbil:

ʿāḍadtuhā bi-ʿatūdin ghayra muʿtalithi ... ka-annahu waqfu ʿājin bāta maknūnā [[The line is by Tamim ibn Muqbil. The author cites it from Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu ʿUbayda, who said: "(We will strengthen your arm through your brother): that is, We will strengthen you by him and help you by him. It is said, when a man honours a man and protects him: 'So-and-so has strengthened the arm of so-and-so.' It derives from 'I supported him in his affair,' meaning I helped him in it and backed him. Ibn Muqbil said: 'I supported her... lay concealed,' meaning a bow, i.e., he supported it with an arrow." End quote. See the manuscript (no. 26059 at Cairo University). The ʿatūd is the sidra or the ṭalḥa tree, and perhaps Ibn Muqbil's arrow was of sidr or ṭalḥ wood. The muʿtalith is either from iʿtalatha al-zind, when it does not spark, in which case the lam is kasra, or from iʿtalatha al-rajul zanadan, when he took it from a tree that one does not know whether it sparks or is hard; Abu Hanifa said: iʿtalatha zanduhu when he took wood across the trees by chance, using whatever he found, and the ghayn is also a dialectal form from him, in which case the lam is fatha. The waqf of ivory is like a bracelet; he means the dark lines on the arrow that serve as its mark, like those on an ivory bracelet. His saying "bāta maknūnā" is the transmission of Abu ʿUbayda, and perhaps what is in the original is a scribal distortion. Its meaning is that the arrow was prepared, readied and placed in the quiver, the case of arrows, and remained there until it was fitted to the bow.]]

It means: a bow that it supported with an arrow. And for ʿaḍud (arm) there are four forms: the best of them is al-ʿaḍud, then al-ʿaḍd, then al-ʿuḍud, and al-ʿuḍd. All of them are pluralised as aʿdād.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and We will give you both authority﴾

He says: and We will give you both proof.

As related:

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿authority for you both﴾: proof.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, ﴿and We will give you both authority﴾: and the sultan is the proof.

* *

And His saying: ﴿so they shall not reach you﴾

His exalted remembrance says: so Pharaoh and his people shall not reach you two with harm.

* *

And His saying: ﴿with Our signs﴾

His exalted remembrance says: ﴿so they shall not reach you two, Pharaoh and his people, with Our signs. You two and whoever follows you will be the victorious﴾. The bāʾ in His saying "with Our signs" is connected to "victorious" (ghālibūn). The meaning of the speech is: you two and whoever follows you are the victors over Pharaoh and his council by Our signs; that is, by Our proof and authority which We shall give you both.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verses 36–37:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿So when Moses came to them with Our clear signs, they said, "This is nothing but fabricated magic, and we never heard of this among our forefathers of old."﴾ (36)

He, exalted is He, says: When Moses came to Pharaoh and his chiefs with Our proofs and Our arguments, clear in showing that they bear witness to the truth of what Moses brought from his Lord, they said to Moses: "What you have brought us is nothing but magic which you have invented yourself and fabricated, a lie and falsehood." ﴿And we never heard of this﴾ that you call us to, namely worshipping the one you call us to worship, ﴿among our forefathers of old﴾, those who passed away before us.

* *

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And Moses said, "My Lord knows best who has come with guidance from Him, and whose will be the good outcome in the Final Abode. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed."﴾ (37)

He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And Moses said﴾ in reply to Pharaoh: ﴿"My Lord knows best"﴾ who among us, O Pharaoh, is in the right and who is in the wrong, and who has come with guidance to the path of rectitude and with clear demonstration of evident proof from Him, and who among us will have the praiseworthy outcome in the Hereafter. This is a counter-argument from the Prophet of God, Moses, peace be upon him, to Pharaoh, and a graceful address. He refrained from saying to him, "Rather, it is you who deceived your people, destroyed his soldiers and led his followers astray, not I," but instead said: ﴿"My Lord knows best who has come with guidance from Him, and whose will be the good outcome in the Final Abode."﴾ Then he went to the utmost in censuring the enemy of God with the most gracious of speech, saying: ﴿"Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed."﴾ He means: indeed, those who disbelieve in God, meaning Pharaoh, will not prosper nor attain their aims, because of their disbelief in Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 38:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Pharaoh said, "O assembly, I know of no god for you other than myself. So kindle for me, O Haman, [a fire] upon the clay and make for me a lofty tower that I may look at the God of Moses, though I think he is among the liars."﴾ (28:38)

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: Pharaoh said to the nobles and chiefs of his people: ﴿O assembly, I know of no god for you other than myself﴾, so that you worship him, and confirm what Moses has said concerning what he brought you, that there is a Lord for you and for him other than me, and a deity besides me. ﴿So kindle for me, O Haman, upon the clay﴾ means: make for me bricks. It is mentioned that he was the first to fire bricks and build with them.

Those who said this:

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿so kindle for me, O Haman, upon the clay﴾, he said: "Upon the clay that becomes fired brick."

Ibn Jurayj said: The first to order the making of fired bricks and to build with them was Pharaoh.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿so kindle for me, O Haman, upon the clay﴾, he said: "He was the first to fire bricks, with which he built the tower."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding God's saying ﴿so kindle for me, O Haman, upon the clay﴾: "The fired thing upon which one kindles is clay with which they build structures."

* *

And His saying: ﴿so make for me a lofty tower﴾

It means: build for me a structure of fired brick. Every raised building is a *sarh* (lofty tower), like a palace. Among the poetry on this is the verse of the poet:

*With them are ostrich-like [structures], which the winds built; you would think their landmarks were towers.* [[The verse is by Abu Dhu'ayb al-Hudhali describing the paths of a desert wasteland (Lisan: n‘m). He said: the *na‘ama* is every building, shade, or landmark by which one is guided among the landmarks of the deserts. It is also said: every building on a mountain, like a shade or landmark. Its plural is *ni‘am*. Abu Dhu'ayb, describing the paths of the wasteland, said: "With them are ostrich-like..." the verse. He said: al-Jawhari narrated the second half as: "*Upon which the scouts' [nagha'id] fill the wind-tossed*". He said: the *naqa'id* are the weakened camels. End. In (Lisan: n-q-d) the *nafida* is like the vanguard, a group sent out into the land as spies to see whether there is an enemy or danger; its plural is *nafa'id*. This is the explanation of al-Asma'i. Abu 'Amr narrated it likewise with the letter *fa'*, but he said in its explanation that they are the weakened camels. Ibn Bari said: *al-ni'am* are wooden beams under which one takes shade. *al-rijal* are foot-soldiers. *al-sarih* are thongs with which sandals are fastened, meaning the sandals of the scouts were torn. *al-surah* is the plural of *sarh*, which, as in (Lisan: s-r-h), is a single building erected alone, massive and tall toward the sky. Abu Dhu'ayb said: "Upon paths like the throats of gazelles, you would think their lairs were towers." End. Al-Zajjaj, regarding God's saying (It was said to her: "Enter the tower"), said: *al-sarh* in the language means a palace, and a courtyard; one says: this is the courtyard [sarha] of the house and its open space, meaning its court and its open area. Some exegetes said: *al-sarh* is a pavement made for her of glass. *al-Sarh* is a smooth land. *al-sarh* is a level stretch of land. End. Abu 'Ubayda said in Majaz al-Qur'an: *al-sarh* is a building and a palace. He added nothing, and he narrated the verse as the author of Lisan narrated it.]]

By *al-suruh* is meant the plural of *sarh*.

* *

And His saying: ﴿that I may look at the God of Moses﴾

It means: look at the deity of Moses, whom he worships and to whose worship he calls. ﴿And I think he is among the liars﴾ in what he says, that he has a deity whom he worships in the heavens, and that it is He who supports and aids him, and He who sent him to us. So it is mentioned to us that Haman built the tower for him, and he climbed upon it.

As for the account of his story and his ascent:

* Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Pharaoh said to his people: ﴿O assembly, I know of no god for you other than myself. So kindle for me, O Haman, upon the clay, and make for me a lofty tower that I may ascend into the heavens and look﴾ ﴿at the God of Moses﴾. When the tower was built for him, he climbed upon it, and he ordered an arrow to be shot toward the sky. It came back to him stained with blood, and he said: "I have killed the god of Moses." Exalted is God above what they say.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verses 39–40:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And he [Pharaoh] and his soldiers were arrogant in the land without right, and they thought that they would not be returned to Us﴾ [28:39] ﴿So We seized him and his soldiers and threw them into the sea. So observe how was the end of the wrongdoers.﴾ [28:40]

His, the Exalted's, saying means: ﴿And he [Pharaoh] was arrogant﴾ and his soldiers in the land of Egypt, in refusing to confirm Moses and following him in what he called them to of the Oneness of God and acknowledging servitude to Him, ﴿without right﴾, meaning through transgression and insolence against their Lord. ﴿And they thought that they would not be returned to Us﴾ means: they reckoned that after their deaths they would not be resurrected, and there would be no reward nor punishment. So they indulged their desires, and did not know that God is watching them, and that He will requite them for their wicked deeds.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So We seized him and his soldiers﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying means: So We gathered Pharaoh and his soldiers from the Copts, ﴿and threw them into the sea﴾, meaning: We cast them all into the sea and drowned them in it, as Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali said:

I looked at its title and cast it away, ... as you cast away a sandal worn out from your sandals.

[The verse is by Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali, as the author states, and it is quoted from Majaz al-Qur'an (Mu'ammar ibn al-Muthanna, Abu 'Ubayda) (folio 180b), who said: (So We seized him and his soldiers) i.e., We gathered him and his soldiers. (Then We threw them into the sea) i.e., We cast them into the sea, destroyed and drowned them. Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali said: "I looked at its title..." the verse. End of quote. In Lisan al-'Arab (root n-b-dh): "nabdh" is throwing a thing from your hand or behind you, and "nabadhtu al-shay'" means I threw it and cast it away.]

He mentioned that this sea was beyond Egypt,

as:

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿and threw them into the sea﴾, he said: The sea was a body of water called Isaf, beyond Egypt, in which God drowned them.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So observe how was the end of the wrongdoers﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying means: So observe, O Muhammad, with the eye of your heart: how was the affair of those who wronged themselves, disbelieved in their Lord, and rejected the counsel of His Messenger? Did We not destroy them, so that We bequeathed their dwellings and their wealth to Our friends, and gave them what they had of gardens, springs, treasures and a noble station, after they had been oppressed, their sons slain and their women spared? Likewise, We shall do with you, and with those who believed in you and confirmed you: We shall make you and them heirs of the dwellings of those who denied you and rejected the truth you brought them, and We shall destroy them by the sword, as the custom of God regarding those who passed away before.

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: ﴿And We made them leaders calling to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped.﴾ [41] ﴿And We caused a curse to follow them in this world, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the despised.﴾ [42]

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We made Pharaoh and his people leaders whom the people of defiance against Allah and disbelief in Him follow, calling people to the deeds of the people of the Fire. ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped﴾: He, may His praise be exalted, says: On the Day of Resurrection, no helper will help them when Allah punishes them, though they used to help one another in this world, so that help was nullified on that day.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And We caused a curse to follow them in this world, and on the Day of Resurrection﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We made Pharaoh and his people bear disgrace in this world, and wrath from Us upon them, so We decreed for them therein destruction, perdition and an evil reputation. And We will cause another curse to follow them on the Day of Resurrection, so We will disgrace them with a lasting disgrace and humiliate them with a constant humiliation.

The exegetes have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

He said: It is like His saying: ﴿And a curse followed them in this [world], and on the Day of Resurrection—how wretched is the gift that is given!﴾

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding His words: ﴿And We caused a curse to follow them in this world, and on the Day of Resurrection﴾: Another curse. Then he began anew and said: ﴿They are among the despised.﴾

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 43:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book after We had destroyed the former generations, as insights for mankind, and a guidance and a mercy, so that they might remember.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Torah after We had destroyed the nations that were before him, such as the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud, the people of Lot and the companions of Madyan.﴾ ﴿As insights for mankind⁠

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 44–45:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And you were not on the western side [of Mount Sinai] when We decreed the command to Musa, nor were you among the witnesses﴾ (28:44).

He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And you were not﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿on the western side﴾ of the mountain ﴿when We decreed the command to Musa﴾, meaning: when We enjoined upon Musa what We imposed on him and his people, and entrusted to him a covenant. ﴿Nor were you among the witnesses﴾, meaning: you were not present for that among those who witnessed it.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of Qur'anic interpretation) said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And you were not﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿on the western side﴾, he said: on the western side of the mountain ﴿when We decreed the command to Musa﴾.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: "On the western side of the mountain."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ali ibn Mudrik, from Abu Zur'ah ibn 'Amr, who said: "Indeed you, the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ), have been answered before you asked," and he recited: ﴿And you were not on the western side [of Mount Sinai] when We decreed the command to Musa﴾.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿But We produced generations, and the life span grew long for them. And you were not dwelling among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses, but We were [the ones] sending [messengers]﴾ (28:45).

He, the Exalted, means by His saying: ﴿But We produced generations﴾: but We created nations and brought them into being after that time. ﴿And the life span grew long for them﴾. His saying: ﴿And you were not dwelling among the people of Madyan﴾ means: you were not residing among the people of Madyan. It is said: "I dwelt (thawaytu) in the place, I dwell (uthwi) in it, a dwelling (thawa')," and al-A'sha of Tha'labah said:

He stayed and delayed his night to provision himself,
So he departed, and broke the appointment with Qutaylah.

[The line is by al-A'sha of Bani Qays ibn Tha'labah (al-Lisan: th-w-y; and the Diwan, Cairo edition with the commentary of Dr. Muhammad Husayn, p. 227). It is from a qasidah he composed for Khosrow when they wanted hostages from him after al-Harith ibn Wa'lah raided some of the countryside. In the line, the reading in some versions is "night ... so it passed" in place of "night ... and he departed." In the Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah the reading is "fa-mada," but the Diwan's reading is better, because of what follows it: "wa-mada li-hajatihi" (and he departed for his need). The commentator of the Diwan said: thawa and athwa have the same meaning, i.e., he stayed. Qassara: he lingered. Akhlafa fulanan: he found his appointment failed; "khalfan" (with a kasra on the kha') means failing. He means: he turned away from his journey, stayed, and lingered one night to provision himself from Qutaylah, so the night passed, and Qutaylah broke the appointment with him.]

Ahl al-ta'wil said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

As related:

* Isa ibn Uthman ibn Isa al-Ramli narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Isa narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ali ibn Mudrik, from Abu Zur'a, concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿And you were not on the side of the Mount when We called﴾, he said: He called out, "O community of Muhammad, I gave you before you asked Me, and I answered you before you called upon Me."

* Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning his saying: ﴿And you were not on the side of the Mount when We called﴾, he said: They were called: "O community of Muhammad, I gave you before you asked Me, and I responded to you before you called upon Me."

* Ibn WakI' narrated to me, saying: Harmala ibn Qays al-Nakha'i narrated to us, saying: I heard this hadith from Abu Zur'a ibn Amr ibn Jarir, from Abu Hurayrah, ﴿And you were not on the side of the Mount when We called﴾, he said: They were called, "O community of Muhammad, I gave you before you asked Me, and I responded to you before you called upon Me."

He said: And this is His saying, when Musa said: ﴿And ordain for us in this world good, and in the Hereafter...﴾ (7:156) ... the verse.

* He said: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, the like of that.

* * *

And His saying: ﴿But it is a mercy from your Lord﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: You did not witness any of that, O Muhammad, so that you would know it; rather, We made you know it, and sent it down to you, and We related all of that to you in Our Book, and We sent you with what We sent down to you of that as a Messenger to those to whom We sent you among creation, as a mercy from Us to you and to them.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿But it is a mercy from your Lord, that We have related to you, that you might warn a people﴾ ... the verse.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿But it is a mercy from your Lord﴾, he said: The mercy from your Lord was prophethood.

* * *

And His saying: ﴿That you might warn a people to whom no warner had come before you﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: But We sent you with this Book and this religion that you might warn a people to whom no warner had come before you, and they are the Arabs, to whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent. Allah sent him to them as a mercy, so that he might warn them of His punishment for their worship of idols and their associating with Him idols and rivals.

* * *

And His saying: ﴿That they might remember﴾

He says: That they might remember the error of what they were upon, remaining in their disbelief in their Lord, and so turn back to acknowledge Allah's oneness and to single Him out for worship apart from every other deity.

And with the like of what we have said concerning this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have spoken.

Mention of those who said that:

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning ﴿But it is a mercy from your Lord﴾, he said: It is what We sent down to you of the Qur'an, ﴿that you might warn a people to whom no warner had come before you﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 47–48:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And had it not been that a calamity should afflict them for what their hands have sent forth, and they should say, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so we could follow Your verses and be among the believers?"﴾

Almighty God says: And were it not that these people to whom We have sent you, O Muhammad, would say, if Our punishment struck them or Our chastisement came upon them before We sent you to them, because of their disbelief in their Lord, their acquisition of sins, and their committing of disobedience: "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger before Your wrath descended upon us and Your punishment came down on us, so that we might follow Your proofs and the verses of Your Book that You sent down to Your messenger, and be among the believers in Your divinity, those who affirm Your messenger in what You have commanded and forbidden us"—We would have hastened the punishment upon them for their polytheism before We sent you to them. But We sent you to them as a warner of Our might because of their disbelief, so that people would have no argument against God after the messengers. The "calamity" (muṣība) in this place means the punishment and vengeance. By His words ﴿for what their hands have sent forth﴾ He means: for what they have earned.

* *

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Why was he not given the like of what was given to Moses?" Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before? They said, "Two works of magic supporting each other," and they said, "Indeed, we are disbelievers in both."﴾

Almighty God says: So when there came to these people, who had not received a warner before you, O Muhammad, when We sent you to them as a warner, ﴿the truth from Us﴾, and that is Muhammad (ﷺ) with the message from God to them, they said, in rebellion against God and persistence in error: "Why was this one who has been sent to us, Muhammad (ﷺ), not given the like of what was given to Moses ibn Imran of the Book?" God, blessed and exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to your people of Quraysh, who say to you, "Why was he not given the like of what was given to Moses," "Did not those who knew this argument of the Jews disbelieve in what was given to Moses before you?"

And according to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have said.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: ʿIsa told us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: The Jews were commanding Quraysh to ask Muhammad for the like of what was given to Moses. God says to Muhammad (ﷺ): Say to Quraysh, let them say to them: "Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before?"

- al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿They said, "Why was he not given the like of what was given to Moses?"﴾ He said: The Jews were commanding Quraysh, then he mentioned something similar, ["They said, 'Two sorcerers supporting each other.'"]

The readers differed regarding the recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra recited: "wa-qālū sāḥirāni tažāharā" [i.e., "they said: two sorcerers who support each other"], meaning: "Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before?" and they said to him and to Muhammad (ﷺ), according to the view of some exegetes; and according to the view of others, to Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them; and according to others, to Jesus and Muhammad: "two sorcerers who cooperated." The majority of the readers of Kufa recited: ﴿qālū siḥrāni tažāharā﴾ [i.e., "siḥrān," "two works of magic"], meaning: they said regarding the Torah and the Furqan, according to the view of some of the people of interpretation; and according to others, regarding the Gospel and the Furqan.

The people of interpretation differed in explaining this according to the difference of the readers in its recitation.

Mention of those who said: By the two sorcerers who supported each other is meant Muhammad and Moses (peace be upon them):

- Sulayman ibn Muhammad ibn Maʿdi Karib al-Ruʿayni told us, saying: Baqiyya ibn al-Walid told us, saying: Shuʿba told us, from Abu Hamza, who said: I heard Muslim ibn Yasar narrate from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding the words of God "two sorcerers who support each other": He said: Moses and Muhammad.

- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, saying: Shuʿba told us, from Abu Hamza, who said: I heard Muslim ibn Yasar say: I asked Ibn ʿAbbas about this verse "two sorcerers who support each other," and he said: Moses and Muhammad.

- Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Yahya ibn Saʿid told us, from Shuʿba, from Abu Hamza, from Muslim ibn Yasar, that Ibn ʿAbbas recited "sāḥirāni," and said: Moses and Muhammad, peace be upon them.

- Ibn Waki' told us, saying: My father told us, from Shuʿba, from Kaysan Abu Hamza, from Muslim ibn Yasar, from Ibn ʿAbbas, the like of it.

And those who said: Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them:

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: ʿIsa told us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God "two sorcerers who support each other," he said: the Jews (said it) about Moses and Aaron.

- al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿They said, "Two works of magic supporting each other"﴾: the saying of the Jews about Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them.

- Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid informed us, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Abu Razin, that one of them recited "sāḥirāni tažāharā" and the other "siḥrāni." He said: The one who recited "siḥrāni" said: the Torah and the Gospel. And he said: The one who recited "sāḥirāni" said: Moses and Aaron.

Others said: By the two sorcerers is meant Jesus and Muhammad (ﷺ).

Mention of those who said that:

- al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Abu Sufyan told us, from Maʿmar, from al-Hasan, regarding His words "two sorcerers who support each other": He said: Jesus and Muhammad, or he said: Moses (ﷺ).

Mention of those who said: By that is meant the Torah and the Furqan, and directing its interpretation to the reading of the one who recited "siḥrāni tažāharā":

- ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Muʿawiya told me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words: "siḥrāni tažāharā": He says: the Torah and the Qur'an.

- Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿They said, "Two works of magic supporting each other"﴾, meaning: the Torah and the Furqan.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿They said, "Two works of magic supporting each other"﴾: the Book of Moses and the Book of the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

Mention of those who said: By it is meant the Torah and the Gospel:

- Ibn Waki' told us, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya told us, from Humayd al-Aʿraj, from Mujahid, who said: I was beside Ibn ʿAbbas while he was seeking refuge between the Corner and the Station, and I said: How do you recite "siḥrāni" or "sāḥirāni"? He did not answer me anything, and ʿIkrima said: "sāḥirāni." I thought that if he disliked that he would have denied it to me. Humayd said: Then I met ʿIkrima after that and mentioned this to him, and I said: How did he used to recite it? He said: He used to recite "siḥrāni tažāharā," meaning: the Torah and the Gospel.

Mention of those who said: By it is meant the Furqan and the Gospel:

- Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih told us, saying: ʿUbayd told us, from al-Dahhak, that he recited ﴿siḥrāni tažāharā﴾, meaning the Gospel and the Furqan.

- Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Saʿid told us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿They said, "Two works of magic supporting each other"﴾: The enemies of God, the Jews, said this about the Gospel and the Furqan; and whoever recites "sāḥirāni" means Muhammad and Jesus son of Mary.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two recitations in our view is the recitation of the one who recites ﴿qālū siḥrāni tažāharā﴾, meaning: the Book of Moses, which is the Torah, and the Book of Jesus, which is the Gospel.

We only say that this is the more correct of the two recitations because the preceding speech concerned mention of the Book, namely His words ﴿They said, "Why was he not given the like of what was given to Moses?"﴾, and what follows it also mentions the Book, namely His words ﴿Then bring a Book from God that is better guidance than both of them, that I may follow it﴾. What lies between them should be from the mention of the same thing, and more fitting to be from the mention of something else. Since that is the more correct recitation, it is known that the meaning of the speech is: Say, O Muhammad, did not these Jews disbelieve in what was given to Moses before? And they said, regarding what was given to Moses of the Book and what you were given: "Two works of magic that cooperate"?

* *

As for His words: ﴿And they said, "Indeed, we are disbelievers in both."﴾

Almighty God says: And the Jews said: We disbelieve in every book in the earth, of Torah and Gospel, and Psalms and Furqan.

And according to what we have said regarding this, some of the people of interpretation have said, and others have differed with them.

Mention of those who said so:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 50:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And if they do not respond to you, then know that they only follow their own desires. And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: If those who say of the Tawrat (Torah) and the Injil (Gospel), "two kinds of magic that support each other," and who claim that the truth lies in something other than them, the Jews, O Muhammad, do not respond to you by bringing a Book from Allah that is more guiding than these two, then know that they only follow their own desires. What they utter and say about the two books is a lie and falsehood with no reality. Perhaps someone will say: Did the Prophet (ﷺ) not know that what the people said, the Jews and others, about the Torah and the Gospel, of falsehood and lies, calling them two forms of magic, is nothing but vain speech, except that they would not respond to him by bringing a Book that is more guiding than them?

It is said: This statement is addressed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but what is meant is those being spoken to: ﴿Have they not disbelieved in what was given to Musa before?﴾ [Q. 28:48], referring to the disbelievers of Quraysh. This is because it was said to the Prophet (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of Quraysh: Have not those who ordered you to say, "Why was Muhammad not given the like of what was given to Musa?", disbelieved in what was given to Musa before this Qur'an? And [have they not] said of the one who was sent down to him and to Isa, "two kinds of magic that support each other"? So tell them: If you are truthful that what was given to Musa and Isa is magic, then bring me a Book from Allah that is more guiding than their two books. If they do not respond to you in this, then know that they are liars, and that in their denial of Muhammad and what he brought from Allah they only follow the desires of their own souls, abandoning the truth while they know it.

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And who is more astray﴾ from the path of right guidance and the way of rectitude, than one who follows the desire of his soul without clear proof from Allah and a covenant from Allah, and who abandons the covenant of Allah that He made with His creatures in His revelation and His sending down? ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed, Allah does not grant success in reaching the truth and the path of rectitude to the people who opposed the command of Allah, abandoned His obedience, denied His Messenger, changed His covenant, and followed the desires of their souls, preferring obedience to Satan over obedience to their Lord.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verses 51–52:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And We have certainly conveyed to them the word, that they might remember﴾ [28:51] ﴿Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it—they believe in it﴾ [28:52]:

Almighty God says: And We have certainly conveyed to them, O Muhammad, to your people of Quraysh and to the Jews of the Children of Israel, the word, through reports of those who passed before, and news of what We brought down upon them of Our punishment when they denied Our messengers, and of what We will do to those who follow their traces and take their path in disbelief in God and denial of His messengers, so that they may remember, take heed, and be admonished. Its root is from "wassala al-hibal" (he joined the ropes, one to another), and from it is the saying of the poet:

"So say to the Banu Marwan: what is with the covenant
and the weak rope that is continually joined?" [[The verse is among the evidences cited by Abu 'Ubayda in Majaz al-Qur'an (the Jami'a photocopy, folio 181b), where he said: (And We have certainly conveyed to them the word) means: We completed it. (See Lisan al-'Arab: wasala.) - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And We have certainly conveyed to them the word, that they might remember﴾: He said: It means Muhammad (ﷺ).

Others said: it refers to the Jews.

He mentioned that among them were Salman and 'Abdullah ibn Salam.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 53–54:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And when it is recited to them, they say, "We have believed in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were Muslims before it."﴾ (53)

Exalted is He, says: ﴿And when it is recited﴾ this Qur'an, to those whom We gave the Book before the revelation of this Qur'an, ﴿they say, "We have believed in it"﴾, meaning: they say, "We have affirmed it." ﴿Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord﴾, meaning: it was sent down from the presence of our Lord. ﴿Indeed, we were Muslims before it﴾, meaning: before the revelation of this Qur'an. That is because they were believers in what the prophets before the coming of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) had brought, and in the Books that were with them, and in their Books was the description and attributes of Muhammad. So they affirmed him, his mission, and his Book before the Qur'an was revealed. Therefore they said: ﴿Indeed, we were Muslims before it.﴾

* *

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured, and they repel evil with good, and from what We have provided them they spend.﴾ (54)

Exalted is He, says: those whose description has been mentioned, ﴿will be given﴾ the reward of their deeds ﴿twice for what they patiently endured﴾.

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of the patience for which God promised what He promised. Some of them said:

He promised them what He promised, Exalted is His praise, for their patience upon the earlier Book and their following of Muhammad (ﷺ), and their patience in that. This is the statement of Qatadah, and we have mentioned it before.

Others said: Rather, He promised them for their patience in their belief in Muhammad (ﷺ) before he was sent, and their following of him when he was sent. This is the statement of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, which we have also mentioned before. Among those who agreed with Qatadah in his statement was Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed, we were Muslims before it﴾, "upon the religion of Jesus. When the Prophet (ﷺ) came, they embraced Islam, so their reward was twice for what they patiently endured the first time, and they entered Islam with the Prophet (ﷺ)."

Some people said regarding this:

⁕ Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, who said: "Some people who were polytheists embraced Islam, and their people used to harm them, so this was revealed: ﴿Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured﴾." And His saying: ﴿and they repel evil with good﴾, meaning: they repel their evil deeds with the good deeds they perform. ﴿And from what We have provided them﴾ of wealth ﴿they spend﴾ in obedience to God, either in jihad in the way of God, or in charity to someone in need, or in maintaining ties of kinship.
