On the interpretation of His words, "And when they hear idle talk, they turn away from it and say, 'To us our deeds, and to you your deeds. Peace be upon you. We do not seek the ignorant'" (28:55):

He, exalted is His mention, says: When these people to whom We gave the Book hear idle talk, which is falsehood in speech.

As related to us:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, on the authority of Qatadah, regarding "And when they hear idle talk, they turn away from it and say, 'To us our deeds, and to you your deeds. Peace be upon you. We do not seek the ignorant'": They do not engage the people of ignorance and falsehood in their falsehood. There had come to them from the command of Allah what restrained them from that.

Others said: By idle talk in this place is meant what the People of the Book added to the Book of Allah of what is not part of it.

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words "And when they hear idle talk, they turn away from it and say..." to the end of the verse, he said: This is for the People of the Book, when they hear the idle talk which the people wrote with their own hands alongside the Book of Allah, and say, "It is from Allah." When those who had embraced Islam heard it and passed by it reciting it, they turned away from it, as if they had not heard that before they believed in the Prophet ﷺ, because they had been Muslims upon the religion of 'Isa. Do you not see that they say: "Indeed, we were Muslims before it" (28:53)?

Others said regarding that:

Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding "And when they hear idle talk, they turn away from it and say, 'To us our deeds, and to you your deeds. Peace be upon you'": He said: It was revealed concerning a people who were polytheists and then embraced Islam, and their people would harm them.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His words ("And when they hear idle talk, they turn away from it and say, 'To us our deeds, and to you your deeds'"): He said: There were people from among the People of the Book who embraced Islam, and the polytheists would harm them, and they would overlook them, saying: "Peace be upon you. We do not seek the ignorant."

* *

As for His words, "They turn away from it":

That is, they did not lend their ears to it nor listen to it. "And say, 'To us our deeds, and to you your deeds'": This indicates that the idle talk mentioned by Allah in this place is what Mujahid said, namely that the people hear from those who harm them with speech what they dislike in themselves, and they respond to them with gentle speech. "To us our deeds": We are content with them for ourselves. "And to you your deeds": You are content with them for yourselves.

* *

As for His words, "Peace be upon you":

That is, a safety from us to you, that we will not revile you, or that you will not hear from us what you dislike. "We do not seek the ignorant": That is, we do not desire to engage the people of ignorance in dispute or in reviling them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 56:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills, and He is most knowing of those who are guided﴾ (56)

He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed, you﴾ O Muhammad ﴿do not guide whom you love﴾ to guidance ﴿but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ to be guided among His creation, by granting them success (tawfiq) to believe in Him and in His Messenger. And if it were said that the meaning is: "Indeed, you do not guide whom you love because of his kinship to you, but Allah guides whom He wills," it would be a valid view. ﴿And He is most knowing of those who are guided﴾: He, may His praise be exalted, says: Allah knows best who has in His knowledge already been destined to be rightly guided, that is, the one whom Allah guides, makes firm and grants success.

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning the refusal of his uncle Abu Talib to answer him when he called him to faith in Allah and to what he called him to.

Mention of the narration to that effect:

* Abu Kurayb and al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Sudai related to us, both saying: al-Walid ibn al-Qasim related to us, from Yazid ibn Kaysan, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his uncle at the time of death: "Say: There is no god but Allah, and I will testify for you with it on the Day of Resurrection." He said: "Were it not that Quraysh would reproach me, I would have comforted your eye." So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love﴾ ... the verse.

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, from Yazid ibn Kaysan, who said: Abu Hazim al-Ashja'i related to me, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his uncle: "Say: There is no god but Allah," and then he mentioned the like of it.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Abu Usamah related to us, from Yazid ibn Kaysan, who heard Abu Hazim al-Ashja'i mention from Abu Hurayrah, who said: When the death of Abu Talib approached, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to him and said: "O uncle, say: There is no god but Allah." He mentioned the like of it, except that he said: "Were it not that Quraysh would reproach me, saying: 'Only the anguish of death made him do it.'"

* Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ubayd related to us, from Yazid ibn Kaysan, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, and he mentioned something like the hadith of Abu Kurayb al-Sudai.

* Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb related to us, saying: My paternal uncle Abdullah ibn Wahb related to me, saying: Yunus related to me, from al-Zuhri, who said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab related to me, from his father, who said: When the death of Abu Talib approached, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to him and found with him Abu Jahl ibn Hisham and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O uncle, say: There is no god but Allah, a word by which I will testify for you before Allah." Abu Jahl and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah said: "O Abu Talib, will you turn away from the religion of Abd al-Muttalib?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) kept presenting it to him and repeating that statement, until Abu Talib said, as the last of what he said to them: "He is upon the religion of Abd al-Muttalib," and he refused to say: "There is no god but Allah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, I will surely seek forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden from you." So Allah revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to seek forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives﴾, and Allah revealed concerning Abu Talib, and He said to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides﴾ ... the verse.

* Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from his father, with its like.

* Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: Ibn Uyaynah related to us, from Amr, from Abu Sa'id ibn Rafi', who said: I said to Ibn Umar: "Was ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love﴾ revealed concerning Abu Talib?" He said: "Yes."

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love﴾: It was the Prophet's saying to Abu Talib: "Say the word of sincerity (kalimat al-ikhlas), by which I will argue on your behalf on the Day of Resurrection." Muhammad ibn Amr said in his narration: He said: "O nephew, the religion of the elders," or "the custom of the elders." al-Harith said in his narration: He said: "O nephew, the religion of the elders."

* al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love﴾. He said: The Prophet said to Abu Talib: "Testify with the word of sincerity, by which I will argue on your behalf on the Day of Resurrection." He said: "O nephew, the religion of the elders." So Allah revealed ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love﴾. He said: This verse was revealed concerning Abu Talib.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love﴾: It was mentioned to us that it was revealed concerning Abu Talib. al-Asamm said: at his death he was asked to say: "There is no god but Allah," so that intercession might become lawful for him through it, but he refused.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Ata', from Amir: When the death of Abu Talib approached, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O uncle, say: There is no god but Allah, I will testify for you with it on the Day of Resurrection." He said to him: "O nephew, if it were not that it would be a disgrace upon you, I would not mind doing it," and he said that to him many times. When he died, this was very hard on the Prophet (ﷺ), and they said: "What benefit is Abu Talib's kinship to you?" He said: "Yes, by Him in whose hand is my soul, he is now in a shallow part of the Fire, upon him are two sandals of fire, from which his brain boils. And there is no one in the Fire who has a lighter punishment than him, and he is the one concerning whom Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills, and He is most knowing of those who are guided﴾."

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿And He is most knowing of those who are guided﴾

He says: He is most knowing of those for whom guidance has been decreed.

As related:

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿And He is most knowing of those who are guided﴾, he said: of those for whom guidance and misguidance have been decreed.

* al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 57:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And they say, "If we were to follow the guidance with you, we would be snatched from our land." Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary, to which are brought the fruits of all things as provision from Us? But most of them do not know.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The disbelievers of Quraysh said: "If we follow the truth you have brought, and disavow the rivals and deities, people will snatch us from our land, by the consensus of all of them against us and in war against us." God says to His Prophet: Say, ﴿Have We not established for them a sanctuary?ⴝ That is, have We not made ready for them a land that We have made sacred, forbidding people to shed blood in it, and preventing them from harming its inhabitants within it, and making its people safe from raids, killing, or capture?

The interpretation of those who have interpreted this agree with what we have said.

Those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ibn Abbas, that al-Harith ibn Nawfal, the one who said: ﴿If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched from our land﴾, and they claimed that they said: "We know that you are the Messenger of God, but we fear that we will be snatched from our land." ﴿Have We not established for them⦆ the verse.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And they say, "If we were to follow the guidance with you, we would be snatched from our land"﴾. He said: They were people from Quraysh who said to Muhammad: "If we follow you, people will snatch us away." So God said: ﴿Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary, to which are brought the fruits of all things﴾.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿And people are snatched away from around them﴾: He said: some of them used to raid others.

The interpretation of those who have interpreted this agree with what we have said regarding the meaning of His saying: ﴿Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary﴾.

Those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿And they say, "If we were to follow the guidance with you, we would be snatched from our land"﴾. God said: ﴿Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary, to which are brought the fruits of all things﴾. He means: Were they not secure in their sanctuary, where no one raids them and they feel no fear?

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan related to me, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary﴾. He said: The people of the sanctuary were secure; they went wherever they wished. If one of them went out and said, "I am from the people of the sanctuary," he was not molested, whereas if any other person went out, he might be killed.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary﴾: He said: "We made it secure for you." He said: It is Mecca, and they are Quraysh.

* *

And His saying: ﴿to which are brought the fruits of all things﴾

He means: they are gathered to it. This derives from their saying: "I gathered water in the basin" (jabaytu al-ma' fi al-hawd), when one collects it there. What is intended is that the fruits of every land are carried to it.

As:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Atiyyah narrated to us, from Sharik, from Uthman ibn Abi Zar'ah, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿to which are brought the fruits of all things﴾: He said: "The fruits of the earth."

* *

And His saying: ﴿as provision from Us﴾

He says: and a provision We have provided for them from Us, meaning: from Our presence. ﴿But most of them do not know﴾. God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: But most of these polytheists who said to the Messenger of God ﷺ: ﴿If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched from our land﴾ do not know that it is We who established for them a secure sanctuary, provided for them therein, and made the fruits of every land be brought to them. Thus, in their ignorance of the One who did this for them, they are disbelievers, not giving thanks to the One who bestowed this blessing upon them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 58:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And how many a town did We destroy that had exulted in its livelihood! So those are their dwellings, not inhabited after them except a little. And We were the inheritors.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And how many a town did We destroy﴾ that had exulted (abtarat) ﴿in its livelihood﴾, so it exulted, became insolent (ashirat), and transgressed (tagha), and so disbelieved in its Lord.

It has also been said: "bataratu ma'ishataha" (it exulted in its livelihood), where the verb is attributed to the town (qarya), though in origin it belongs to the livelihood (ma'isha), as one says: "Asfahaka ra'yuka fa-safihtahu" (your opinion made you foolish, so you were foolish), and "Abtaraka maluka fa-bataratahu" (your wealth made you exult, so you exulted). Here ma'isha is in the accusative as a specification (tafsir).

We have already explained similar instances in other places in this book of ours.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the interpreters) have said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿And how many a town did We destroy that had exulted in its livelihood﴾: "Al-batar (exultation) is the insolence of the people of heedlessness and the people of falsehood, and their riding roughshod over the disobedience of God." He said: "That is the exultation in blessing." ﴿So those are their dwellings, not inhabited after them except a little﴾: he says, "So those are the homes of the people whom We destroyed for their disbelief in their Lord, and their dwellings were not inhabited after them except a little," meaning: they were ruined after them, and only the least of them was resettled, while most of it was in ruin. Although the wording of the statement is that their dwellings were inhabited a little, its meaning is: "So those are their dwellings, not inhabited after them except a little part of them," as one says: "I have paid your right, except a little of it."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We were the inheritors﴾:

He says: "There was no inheritance for them from what We ruined of their dwellings, and they returned as they were before they were inhabited, with no owner for them except God, to whom belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 59:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And your Lord would never destroy the cities until He sends into their mother [city] a messenger reciting to them Our verses. And We would never destroy the cities unless their people were wrongdoers.﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿And your Lord would not be ...﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿destroying the cities﴾ that are around Makkah in your time and your era, ﴿until He sends into their mother [city] a messenger﴾. He says: until He sends to Makkah a messenger, and it is Umm al-Qura (the mother of the cities), reciting to them the verses of Our Book. The messenger is Muhammad (ﷺ).

The interpreters of the Qur'an have said in agreement with what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿until He sends into their mother [city] a messenger﴾: Umm al-Qura is Makkah, and God sent to them a messenger, Muhammad (ﷺ).

* *

And His words: ﴿And We would never destroy the cities unless their people were wrongdoers.﴾

He says: We would not destroy a city while its people are believers in God; rather We destroy it because of its wronging of itself by its disbelief in God. And We destroyed the people of Makkah only because of their disbelief in their Lord and their wronging of themselves.

The interpreters of the Qur'an have said in agreement with what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿And We would never destroy the cities unless their people were wrongdoers.﴾ He said: God does not destroy a city for its faith, but He destroys cities for wrongdoing when its people do wrong. Had a city believed, they would not have been destroyed along with those who were destroyed; rather they denied and did wrong, and for that they were destroyed.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 28, verses 60–61:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And whatever you have been given is but the enjoyment of worldly life and its adornment. But what is with Allah is better and more lasting. Then will you not reason?﴾ (60)

The Exalted says: Whatever you, O people, have been given of wealth and children, it is merely a provision you enjoy in this worldly life, and it is part of its adornment with which one adorns oneself therein. It will not avail you anything with Allah, and nothing of it will benefit you in your return. What is with Allah for the people of His obedience and His allegiance is better than what you have been given of this world's provision and adornment, ﴿and more lasting﴾. He says: more lasting for its people, because it is everlasting and has no end.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding His words: ﴿But what is with Allah is better and more lasting﴾, he said: better in reward, and more lasting with us.

The Exalted says: ﴿Then will you not reason?﴾ Will you not, O people, have intellects by which you reflect, so that you recognize good from evil, and choose for yourselves the better of the two outcomes over the worse of them, and prefer the everlasting bliss that has no end over the perishing thing that has no permanence?

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Is one to whom We have promised a good promise and who will meet it like one We have given the enjoyment of worldly life and then, on the Day of Resurrection, he will be among those brought forward [to punishment]?﴾ (61)

The Exalted says: Is one of Our creatures to whom We have promised Paradise for his obedience to Us, who believed in what We promised, affirmed it, and obeyed Us, thereby deserving that We fulfil for him what We promised, so that he will meet what was promised and arrive at it, like one to whom We gave the enjoyment of its provision in the world, so he enjoyed it, forgot to act upon what We promised the people of obedience, abandoned seeking it, and preferred the hasty pleasure over the deferred? Then on the Day of Resurrection, when he comes before Allah, he will be among those brought forward, meaning among those present for the punishment of Allah and His painful retribution.

The people of interpretation have said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿Is one to whom We have promised a good promise and who will meet it﴾, he said: this is the believer who heard the Book of Allah, affirmed it, believed in what Allah promised therein. ﴿Like one We have given the enjoyment of worldly life﴾ — this is the disbeliever. By Allah, he is not like the believer. ﴿Then on the Day of Resurrection he will be among those brought forward﴾: i.e., in the punishment of Allah.

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to us, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Waqqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid. Ibn Amr said in his narration regarding His words: ﴿among those brought forward﴾, he said: they are brought to it. Al-Harith said in his narration: ﴿Then on the Day of Resurrection he will be among those brought forward﴾: the people of the Fire, who are brought to it.

* al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿Then on the Day of Resurrection he will be among those brought forward﴾, he said: the people of the Fire, who are brought to it.

The people of interpretation differed concerning who this verse was revealed about. Some of them said it was revealed concerning the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Abu al-Nu'man al-Hakam ibn Abdullah al-Ijli related to us, he said: Shu'bah related to us, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Mujahid: ﴿Is one to whom We have promised a good promise and who will meet it like one We have given the enjoyment of worldly life, then on the Day of Resurrection he will be among those brought forward﴾, he said: it was revealed concerning the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.

* al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿Is one to whom We have promised a good promise and who will meet it﴾, he said: the Prophet ﷺ.

Others said: it was revealed concerning Hamzah and Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, and Abu Jahl, may Allah curse him.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Badal ibn al-Muhabbar al-Taghlibi [[In al-Khazraji's Khulasah: Badal ibn al-Muhabbar, with the mim vowelled with damma and the muhmalah with fatha and the ba' with fatha, al-Yarbu'i, Abu al-Munir (like Mut'i), al-Basri. Abu Hatim said: truthful. He died around the year 215 AH.]] said: Shu'bah related to us, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Mujahid: ﴿Is one to whom We have promised a good promise and who will meet it like one We have given the enjoyment of worldly life, then on the Day of Resurrection he will be among those brought forward﴾, he said: it was revealed concerning Hamzah, Ali ibn Abi Talib, and Abu Jahl.

* Abd al-Samad related to us, he said: Shu'bah related to us, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Mujahid, he said: it was revealed concerning Hamzah and Abu Jahl.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 62–66:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And the Day He calls to them and says, "Where are My partners, whom you used to claim?" (62) Those about whom the word has come into effect will say, "Our Lord, these are the ones whom we led astray. We led them astray just as we went astray. We disassociate ourselves before You; they did not used to worship us."﴾ (63)

His, may His remembrance be exalted, says: On the Day when the Lord of Might calls to those who associated with Him rivals and idols in the world, He will say to them: ﴿"Where are My partners whom you used to claim"﴾ that they were partners to Me in the world. ﴿Those about whom the word has come into effect will say﴾, meaning: those upon whom the wrath and curse of God have become binding will say, and they are the devils who used to lead the children of Adam astray: ﴿"Our Lord, these are the ones whom we led astray. We led them astray just as we went astray."﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 67:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿But as for one who repents, believes, and does righteous deeds, perhaps he will be among the successful﴾ (28:67).

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿But as for one who repents﴾ from among the polytheists, turning back in repentance and returning to the truth, sincerely devoting worship to God alone, singling Him out for worship, and not associating anything with Him in His worship. ﴿And believes﴾ means: and affirms His prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) as true. ﴿And does righteous deeds﴾ means: and acts upon what God has commanded him to do in His Book and on the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ). ﴿Then perhaps he will be among the successful﴾ means: then he is among those who attain success and obtain their aims with God, abiding forever in His gardens. And "perhaps" (ʿasā) from God is binding.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 68:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses. They do not have the choice. Glory be to Allah, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.﴾ (28:68)

His, the Exalted's, words mean: ﴿And your Lord﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿creates whatever He wills﴾ to create, ﴿and chooses﴾ for His guardianship, ﴿the choice﴾ from His creation, and whoever has been granted happiness by Him. The Exalted One said: ﴿and chooses what they have no choice in﴾, and the meaning is: what I have described, because the polytheists, as is reported about them, would choose their wealth and set it aside for their idols. So Allah said to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Your Lord, O Muhammad, creates whatever He wills to create, and chooses for guidance, faith, and righteous deeds from His creation whomever He knows in His prior knowledge to be their best, in the same way these polytheists chose the best of their wealth for their idols. Likewise, My choosing for Myself, My selecting for My guardianship, and My choosing for My service and obedience, is the best of My kingdom and My creation.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said something similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses. They do not have the choice.﴾ He said: In the Jahiliyyah they would set the best of their wealth aside for their idols.

If the meaning is as such, then there is no doubt that "ma" in His words ﴿and chooses what they have no choice in﴾ is in the accusative position, governed by the verb "chooses" (yakhtar) preceding it, and that it means "alladhi" (that which).

If someone says: If the matter is as you have described, that "ma" is a noun in the accusative governed by the verb ﴿chooses﴾ before it, then where is the predicate of "kana" (was)? You have acknowledged that "kana" contains a pronoun referring back to "ma", and "kana" therefore needs a complement; where is the complement? It is said: The Arabs sometimes make the prepositions of attribute (huruf al-sifat), when the predicates come after them, into predicates, just as they do with nouns when their predicates come after them. Al-Farra' reported that al-Qasim ibn Ma'n recited to him the verse of 'Antara:

Is the tears of the eye flowing from Sumayya ... if this kindness from you had been known before today.

[[The line is from the poetry of 'Antara ibn 'Amr ibn Shaddad al-'Absi (Mukhtar al-Shi'r al-Jahili, with the commentary of Mustafa al-Saqqa, Mustafa al-Babi al-Halabi edition, p. 394). The version there is the one transmitted by al-Mufaddal, which the author pointed to: "Is the tears of the eye flowing from Suhayya ... if this kindness from you had been known before today." The commentator said: Suhayya, or Sumayya, was his father's wife. Abu Sa'id al-Sukkari narrated... Its meaning is that the sorrow and compassion from you are denied, since had it been known before, he would not have denied it. According to this narration there is no evidence in the line. As for the author's version, which al-Farra' transmitted from al-Qasim ibn Ma'n the judge, he made the phrase "if this were from you known before today" with "ma'ruf" in the nominative as a predicate after the attribute. The author added: "Because the Arabs make the prepositions of attribute into predicates when the predicates come after them, just as they do with nouns when their predicates follow." ... Then he recited the line and said: "He raised 'ma'ruf' by the preposition of attribute, and it is undoubtedly the predicate of 'dha'." Qultu: It seems his meaning is that the preposition of attribute stands in place of a pronoun subject, and "ma'ruf" is its predicate; as if he said: "if this one is known." In this expression there is considerable strain. Had he said that "ma'ruf" is the predicate of an omitted subject, its supposed meaning being "he is known from you," and the clause is the predicate of "kana," it would have been clearer in expression. I did not find the line nor the analysis of its grammar in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an.]]

So he raised "ma'ruf" by the preposition of attribute, and it is undoubtedly the predicate of "dha." It was also mentioned that al-Mufaddal recited it as:

If that from you had been known before today.

And from it also is the verse of 'Umar ibn Abi Rabi'a:

I said: Answer me, a lover ... with your love, obsessed ... In them are three like statues ... and a maiden and a mature one.

[[The two lines belong to 'Umar ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Rabi'a al-Makhzumi, the poet of love in the Umayyad period, as the author said. "Mukallaf" means one obsessed with something; love and passion for a thing. "Thalath" means neighbours or women. "Duma" is the plural of duma, a statue of ivory, marble, or the like. "Ka'ib" is a girl whose breasts have just swelled. "Muslif" in the lexicon (Lisan al-Arab, s-l-f) is a woman of middle age, said to be one who has reached about forty-five. It is a description used specifically of women. The point of evidence in the line is that "mukallaf" is in the nominative as a predicate, because it comes after the preposition that stands in place of the subject, as if he said: "Answer, a lover who is obsessed." It is similar in meaning to the previous evidence from 'Antara's "if this from you had been known before today."]]

So "mukallaf" is an attribute of "'ashiq," and he raised it by the preposition of attribute, the letter "ba'" (with), in addition to many similar examples. Likewise His words ﴿and chooses what they have no choice in﴾: "al-khiyara" is raised by the attribute "lahum" (for them), if it is the predicate of "ma," since it came after the attribute, and the attribute took the place of the predicate. This is like the speaker saying: "Kana 'Amr wa abuhu qa'im" (was 'Amr and his father standing). There is no doubt that if "qa'im" were in the place of the father, and the father came after it, it would be accusative. Likewise is the way of raising "al-khiyara," which is the predicate of "ma."

If someone says: Is it permissible that "ma" in this position be a negation, and the meaning of the speech be: Your Lord creates whatever He wills to create, and chooses whatever He wills to choose, so that His words ﴿and chooses﴾ end the report about creation and choosing, and then the speech begins afresh with the meaning: they did not have the choice; that is, the creatures did not have the choice, and choice belongs to Allah alone?

It is said: This is a view whose corruption is not hidden from the intelligent, for several reasons; even if there were no opinion of the people of interpretation contrary to it, how much more so when the interpretation of those we have mentioned is contrary to it. As for one of the reasons for its corruption: if His words ﴿what they have no choice in﴾ were as the one who holds this view supposes, with "ma" meaning negation in the manner of the interpretation I mentioned, then He, the Exalted, would only be denying that they had choice in the past, before the revelation of this verse. As for the future, they would have choice, because the saying of the speaker, "ma kana laka hadha" (this was not for you), is undoubtedly a report that it was not his in the past, and it may be his in the future. Such speech is undoubtedly defective, because what was not for the creatures in the past is never for them. Moreover, if that meaning were intended, the speech would have said "fa-laysa" (so it is not). Rather, it would say: "Your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses; they have no choice," so as to be a negation that it belongs to them both before and after.

The second reason: the Book of Allah is the clearest of expression and the most evident of speech, and it is impossible that anything in it be unintelligible in meaning. It is also not permissible in speech to begin by saying "ma kana li-fulan al-khiyara" (so-and-so had no choice) without a preceding statement that requires it. Likewise His words ﴿and chooses what they have no choice in﴾: nothing preceded it from Allah, the Exalted, reporting that anyone claimed that they had choice, so that it could be said to him, "you had no choice." Rather, what preceded it was a report about the destiny of one who repented of his polytheism, believed, and did righteous deeds, followed by the Exalted One's report about the cause of the faith of those among them who believed and did righteous deeds: that it is only because of His choosing them for faith, and because of His prior knowledge of them, through which they were guided. What we have said is further clarified by His words: ﴿And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they reveal﴾; so He informed that He knows the inner and outer states of His servants, and He chooses for Himself, and selects for His obedience, those whose sound inner state and pleasing outward conduct He knows.

The third reason: the meaning of "khiyara" in this place is "khiyara," which is that which is chosen from among beasts, livestock, men, and women. It is said of it: "u'tiya al-khiyara wa al-khayra" (he was given the choice and the best), like "al-tiyara" and "al-tayra" (omen). It is not the act of choosing. If "khiyara" is as we have described, it is well known that the better speech is to say: "Your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses whatever He wills; they had no good beast, no good food, no good man or woman."

If someone says: Is it permissible that it means the verbal noun (masdar)? It is said: No. For if it were a verbal noun, the meaning of the speech would be: Your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses the existence of choice for them. If that were its meaning, it would follow that there would be no bad beasts or livestock for them; and if they had no bad ones of those, it would follow that they would have no owner for them. The error of that is not hidden, because the good and bad of those have owners who possess them by Allah's granting them that possession. In this being so is the corruption of directing the word to the meaning of the verbal noun.

As for His words, glory be to Him and exalted is He, ﴿above what they associate﴾: His, the Exalted's, meaning is to declare Allah free and innocent, and exalted above what the polytheists attribute to Him of partnership, and what they fabricate of lies and falsehood against Him.

The sense of the speech is: Glory be to Allah and exalted is He above their polytheism. Some of the scholars of Arabic grammar used to construe it as meaning: "and exalted is He above that which they associate with Him."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 69–70:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they disclose (69). And He is Allah; there is no deity except Him. To Him belongs praise in the first [life] and the last, and to Him is the judgment, and to Him you will be returned (70).﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: "And your Lord, O Muhammad, knows what the breasts of His creatures conceal." It derives from "akantu al-shay' fi sadri" (I concealed the thing in my breast), when I hide it within it, and "kantu al-shay'" (I guarded the thing), when I protect it. ﴿And what they disclose﴾: he says, "and what they reveal with their tongues and their limbs." He only means by this that His choice of whom He chooses from among them for faith is made with knowledge of the hidden matters of their affairs and their outcomes, and that He chooses goodness for its people, so He grants them success in it, and He assigns evil to its people, and leaves them to it. His saying, ﴿And He is Allah; there is no deity except Him﴾: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "Your Lord, O Muhammad, is the one worshipped, to whom alone worship is fitting, and there is no deity whose worship is permissible other than Him." ﴿To Him belongs praise in the first﴾: meaning in this world ﴿and the last﴾. ﴿And to Him is the judgment﴾: he says, "and to Him belongs the decision between His creatures." ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾: he says, "and to Him you will be sent back after your deaths, and He will judge between you with truth."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 71:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered? If Allah should make for you the night perpetual until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you light? Then will you not hear?﴾

Allah, the Exalted, says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who associate others with Allah: "O people, have you considered: if Allah made the night perpetual for you, with no day following it, until the Day of Resurrection?" The Arabs say of anything that is continuous and unbroken, whether ease, affliction or blessing, that it is ﴿sarmad﴾ (perpetual).

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿sarmadan﴾: "Perpetual, without cessation."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Abi Juraij, from Mujahid, the same.

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abdullah told us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿If Allah should make for you the night perpetual﴾, he said: "Perpetual."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿what deity other than Allah could bring you light?﴾

It means: what worshipped being other than the One to whom every thing's worship belongs could bring you the light of day, so that you may see by it? ﴿Then will you not hear?﴾ means: will you not give heed with your hearing, reflect upon it and be admonished, and know that your Lord is the One who brings the night and takes away the day when He wills, and when He wills brings the day and takes away the night; so He bestows favour upon you through their alternation.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered? If Allah should make for you the day perpetual until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you a night in which you rest? Then will you not see?﴾

Allah, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your people: ﴿Have you considered﴾, O people, ﴿if Allah should make for you the day perpetual﴾, lasting forever with no night ever accompanying it ﴿until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah﴾, what worshipped being other than the One to whom every thing's worship belongs ﴿could bring you a night in which you rest﴾, so that you settle and become calm therein? ﴿Then will you not see?﴾ means: will you not see with your eyes the alternation of night and day upon you, a mercy from Allah to you and a proof from Him against you, so that you may know by this that worship is not fitting except for the One who bestowed this blessing upon you and not for any other, and for the One who has the power by which He alternates between them.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be thankful﴾ (73).

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And of His mercy﴾ toward you, O people, ﴿He made for you the night and the day﴾, differentiating between them: He made this night dark ﴿that you may rest therein﴾ and be still and settle, for the ease of your bodies from the toil of the activity you engage in by day for your livelihoods. Regarding the pronoun in His saying ﴿that you may rest therein﴾ there are two possibilities: first, that it refers to the night alone, with another pronoun implied for the day along with "seeking"; second, that it refers to both the night and the day, and the reason for using a singular pronoun for both is the same as the Arabs' reason in their saying: "Your coming forward and your turning back harm me," since "coming forward" and "turning back" are actions, and an action is expressed in the singular whether its instances are many or few. And He made this day a light in which you see, so that you move about with your eyes in it for your livelihoods, and to seek His provision, which He has apportioned among you by His bounty that He has bestowed upon you.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and perhaps you will be thankful﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: so that you may give thanks to Him for His favour upon you in that, He has done this for you so that you would single Him out for thanks and devote praise to Him alone, since no partner has shared with Him in His favour upon you in this, and therefore there should be no partner with Him in praise for it.
