He says: He said to them: produce your argument for your associating others with Allah, that which you used to associate, along with Allah's having given you warning through the messengers and establishing the proofs against you.

And according to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have said.

Mention of those who said that:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿Then We said: Produce your proof﴾ — meaning: your evidence.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Then We said: Produce your proof﴾ — he said: "Your argument for what you used to worship and say."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, ﴿Then We said: Produce your proof﴾ — he said: "Your argument for what you used to worship."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then they will know that the truth belongs to Allah﴾

He says: then they will know at that time that the conclusive proof belongs to Allah against them, and that the truth belongs to Allah, and His report is true; so they will be certain of a lasting punishment from Allah for them. ﴿And what they used to invent will have vanished from them﴾ — he says: that which they used to associate with Allah in the world has perished and disappeared, and what they used to fabricate and lie against Me concerning them, it did not benefit them there; rather it harmed them and burned them in the fire of Hell.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be thankful﴾ (73).

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And of His mercy﴾ toward you, O people, ﴿He made for you the night and the day﴾, differentiating between them: He made this night dark ﴿that you may rest therein﴾ and be still and settle, for the ease of your bodies from the toil of the activity you engage in by day for your livelihoods. Regarding the pronoun in His saying ﴿that you may rest therein﴾ there are two possibilities: first, that it refers to the night alone, with another pronoun implied for the day along with "seeking"; second, that it refers to both the night and the day, and the reason for using a singular pronoun for both is the same as the Arabs' reason in their saying: "Your coming forward and your turning back harm me," since "coming forward" and "turning back" are actions, and an action is expressed in the singular whether its instances are many or few. And He made this day a light in which you see, so that you move about with your eyes in it for your livelihoods, and to seek His provision, which He has apportioned among you by His bounty that He has bestowed upon you.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and perhaps you will be thankful﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: so that you may give thanks to Him for His favour upon you in that, He has done this for you so that you would single Him out for thanks and devote praise to Him alone, since no partner has shared with Him in His favour upon you in this, and therefore there should be no partner with Him in praise for it.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And on the day He calls to them and says: "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ (74) ﴿And We will extract from every nation a witness, and We will say: "Produce your proof." Then they will know that the truth belongs to Allah, and what they used to invent will have vanished from them﴾ (75).

He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: and on the day your Lord calls to these polytheists, O Muhammad, and says to them: ﴿Where are My partners whom you used to claim﴾, O people, in the world, that they were My partners?

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We will extract from every nation a witness﴾

And We will bring forth from every community its witness, who is its prophet, who testifies against it regarding what its people answered him concerning the message he brought them from Allah. It has been said: ﴿and We will extract﴾ derives from the saying: "So-and-so extracted (nazaʿa) with such-and-such a proof," meaning: he brought it forth and produced it.

And according to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And We will extract from every nation a witness﴾ — "its witness is its prophet, who testifies against it that he has conveyed the message of his Lord."

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿And We will extract from every nation a witness﴾ — he said: "A messenger."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, with similar.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then We will say: "Produce your proof"﴾

He says: We will say to the community of each prophet among them, the one that rejected his counsel and denied what came to it from their Lord, when their prophet testified against it that he had conveyed to them the message of Allah: ﴿Produce your proof﴾. He says: He said to them: produce your argument for your associating others with Allah, that which you used to associate, along with Allah's having given you warning through the messengers and establishing the proofs against you.

And according to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have said.

Mention of those who said that:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿Then We said: Produce your proof﴾ — meaning: your evidence.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Then We said: Produce your proof﴾ — he said: "Your argument for what you used to worship and say."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, ﴿Then We said: Produce your proof﴾ — he said: "Your argument for what you used to worship."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then they will know that the truth belongs to Allah﴾

He says: then they will know at that time that the conclusive proof belongs to Allah against them, and that the truth belongs to Allah, and His report is true; so they will be certain of a lasting punishment from Allah for them. ﴿And what they used to invent will have vanished from them﴾ — he says: that which they used to associate with Allah in the world has perished and disappeared, and what they used to fabricate and lie against Me concerning them, it did not benefit them there; rather it harmed them and burned them in the fire of Hell.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 76 (part 1 of 2):

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Musa, but he tyrannized over them. And We had given him of treasures so much that its keys would burden a group of strong men.﴾ When his people said to him, "Do not exult. Indeed, Allah does not love the exultant."

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿Indeed, Qarun﴾ — and he is Qarun son of Yashhar (Yasfar) son of Qahith son of Lawi son of Ya'qub — ﴿was from the people of Musa﴾ — meaning: he was from the clan of Musa son of Imran, the Prophet (ﷺ), and he was his paternal and maternal cousin, for Qarun is Qarun son of Yashhar son of Qahith, and Musa is Musa son of Imran son of Qahith. Thus Ibn Juraij traced his lineage.

It has been narrated to us by al-Qasim, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Musa﴾, that he said: "He was his cousin, the son of his father's brother. Qarun son of Yasfar" — so said al-Qasim — "but it is Yashhar son of Qahith, and Musa son of Imran son of Qahith, and Imran in Arabic is 'Umar."

As for Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Salamah related to us from him, that Yashhar son of Qahith married Sumayt [[In the book al-'Ara'is (Qisas al-Anbiya' of al-Tha'labi the exegete), it is Sumayt, daughter of Yatadim son of Barkiya son of Yash'an son of Ibrahim. And on page 213 of the Halabi edition: from Ibn Ishaq: Yashhar son of Qahith married "Sumayn daughter of Maryb son of Barkiya son of Yaqshan son of Ibrahim." And there is much disagreement among scholars regarding Hebrew names.]] daughter of Batawit son of Barkana son of Baqshan son of Ibrahim, and she bore him Imran son of Yashhar and Qarun son of Yashhar. Then Imran married Yakhibat daughter of Shamuwil son of Barkana son of Baqshan son of Barkana, and she bore him Harun son of Imran and Musa son of Imran, the chosen one of Allah and His prophet. So, according to what Ibn Ishaq mentioned, Musa was the son of Qarun's brother, and Qarun was his paternal uncle, brother of his father, through both father and mother. Most scholars hold, regarding this, what Ibn Juraij said.

Mention of those who said this:

It has been narrated to us by Abu Kurayb, who said: Jabir ibn Nuh related to us, who said: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid informed us, from Ibrahim, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Musa﴾, that he said: "He was the cousin of Musa."

It has been narrated to us by Ibn Bashshar, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, who said: Sufyan related to us, from Simak ibn Harb, who said: Sa'id related to us from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Musa﴾: "We used to narrate that he was the son of his father's brother, and he was called al-Munawwar because of the beauty of his voice with the Torah. But the enemy of Allah became a hypocrite, just as the Samiri did, and rebellion destroyed him."

It has been narrated to us by Ibn Wakic, who said: My father related to us, from Sufyan, from Simak, from Ibrahim, ﴿Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Musa﴾, he said: "He was his cousin, so he rebelled against him."

He said: Yahya al-Qattan related to us, from Sufyan, from Simak, from Ibrahim, who said: "Qarun was the cousin of Musa."

He said: Abu Mu'awiya related to us, from Ibn Abi Khalid, from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Musa﴾, who said: "He was his cousin."

It has been narrated to me by Bishr ibn Hilal al-Sawwaf, who said: Ja'far ibn Sulayman al-Dub'i related to us, from Malik ibn Dinar, who said: "It reached me that Musa son of Imran was the cousin of Qarun."

* *

And His saying: ﴿so he tyrannized over them﴾
He means: he transgressed his limit in arrogance and haughtiness toward them.

Some of them said: his tyranny over them was an increase of a span in the length of his garments.

Mention of those who said this:

It has been narrated to me by Ali ibn Sa'id al-Kindi, Abu al-Sa'ib and Ibn Wakic, who said: Hafs ibn Ghiyath related to us, from Layth, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, regarding ﴿Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Musa, so he tyrannized over them﴾, he said: "He exceeded them by a span in his garments."

Others said: his tyranny over them was by the abundance of his wealth.

Mention of those who said this:

It has been narrated to us by Bishr, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: "He only tyrannized over them by the abundance of his wealth."

* *

And His saying: ﴿And We had given him of treasures so much that its keys would burden a group of strong men﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: We gave Qarun of the treasures of wealth so much that its keys — and it is the plural of miftah (key), which is what is used to open doors.

Some of them said: by the keys in this place is meant the storehouses, so that they weigh down the group.

The interpreters of the Qur'an have said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said what we said about the meaning of "keys":

It has been narrated to us by Abu Kurayb, who said: Jabir ibn Nuh related to us, who said: al-A'mash informed us, from Khaythama, who said: "The keys of Qarun were carried by sixty mules, each key being for a treasure of known size, the size of a finger, made of hide."

It has been narrated to us by Ibn Wakic, who said: My father related to us, from al-A'mash, from Khaythama, who said: "The keys of Qarun's treasures were of hide; each key was the size of a finger, each key for a separate storehouse. When he rode, the keys were carried by sixty white-blazed mules."

It has been narrated to us by Ibn Humayd, who said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Khaythama, regarding His saying: ﴿so much that its keys would burden a group of strong men﴾, he said: "We find written in the Gospel: the keys of Qarun were a load for sixty white-blazed mules, and each key was no more than a finger in size, and for each key there was a treasure."

It has been narrated to us by Ibn Wakic, who said: Ibn 'Uyayna related to us, from Humayd, from Mujahid, who said: "The keys were of camel hide."

It has been narrated to us by al-Qasim, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿so much that its keys would burden a group of strong men﴾, who said: "Keys of hide like the keys of wooden sticks."

Others said: by the keys in this place is meant his storehouses.

Mention of those who said this:

It has been narrated to us by Abu Kurayb, who said: Hushaym related to us, who said: Isma'il ibn Salim informed us, from Abu Salih, regarding ﴿so much that its keys would burden a group of strong men﴾, who said: "His storehouses were carried by forty mules."

It has been narrated to us by Ibn Wakic, who said: My father related to us, from Abu Hujayr, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿so much that its keys﴾, who said: "Its containers."

Interpreters have said something similar to what we have said regarding the meaning of His saying: ﴿would burden a group﴾.

Mention of those who said this:

It has been narrated to us by Abu Kurayb, who said: Jabir ibn Nuh related to us, who said: Abu Rawq related to us, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿would burden a group﴾, who said: "It would weigh down the group."

It has been narrated to me by 'Ali, who said: Abu Salih related to us, who said: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿would burden a group﴾, who said: "It would weigh down." As for "group" (al-'usbah), it means a company of men.

The interpreters differed regarding the extent of its number intended in this place. As for the extent of the number of "'usbah" in the speech of the Arabs, we have mentioned it previously, with the differences of those who differed about it, the transmissions regarding it, and the evidence for the correct usage of it, in a way that suffices from repeating it in this place. Some of them said: his keys would weigh down a group whose number is forty men.

Mention of those who said this:

It has been narrated to us by al-Qasim, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hushaym related to us, from Isma'il ibn Salim, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying: ﴿would burden a group﴾, who said: "Forty men."

It has been narrated to us by Bishr, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿would burden a group﴾, who said: "It has been mentioned to us that the group is between ten and forty."

It was narrated from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿would burden a group of strong men﴾: "They claim that the group is forty men who carry his keys because of the number of them."

It has been narrated to me by Muhammad ibn Sa'd, who said: My father related to me, who said: My paternal uncle related to me, who said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And We had given him of treasures so much that its keys would burden a group of strong men﴾, who said: "Forty men."

Others said: sixty, and said: his keys were carried by sixty mules.

It has been narrated likewise to us by Ibn Wakic, who said: My father related to us, from al-A'mash, from Khaythama.

Others said: it was carried by between three and ten.

Mention of those who said this:

It has been narrated to us by Ibn Wakic, who said: Jabir ibn Nuh related to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿would burden a group﴾, who said: "The group: three."

It has been narrated to us by Abu Kurayb, who said: Jabir ibn Nuh related to us, who said: Abu Rawq related to us, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿would burden a group﴾, who said: "The group: between three and ten."

Others said: it would be carried by between ten and fifteen.

Mention of those who said this:

It has been narrated to me by Muhammad ibn 'Amr, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, who said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, who said: al-Hasan related to us, who said: Warqa' related to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿its keys would burden a group﴾, who said: "The group: between ten and fifteen."

It has been narrated to us by al-Qasim, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿would burden a group﴾, who said: "The group: fifteen men."

* *

And His saying: ﴿strong men﴾
He means: possessors of strength. Mujahid said regarding this:

It has been narrated to me by Muhammad ibn 'Amr, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, who said: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿strong men﴾, who said: "Fifteen."

If someone says: how is it said, "And We had given him of treasures so much that its keys would burden a group," and how can the keys burden the group, when it is rather the group that is burdened by them? It is said: scholars of the Arabic language differed regarding this. Some people of Basra said: the figurative sense is: the strong group would be burdened by the keys of his blessings. He said: it is said in speech: "Indeed, her buttocks are burdened by it," and the original is: "she is burdened by her buttocks, as a camel is burdened by its load." He said: the Arabs do this sort of thing. The poet said:

I ransom with his own self my self and my wealth, and I do not spare you except what I am able to.

And the meaning is: I ransom with my self and my wealth his self.

Another said:

And you ride horses between which there is no truce, and the spears are made to suffer by the red fat men.

And it is only the fat men who suffer by the spears. He said: "horses" here means men.

Another among them said regarding ﴿its keys﴾: He said: this is a place where "inna" is hardly begun, and He has said: ﴿Indeed, the death from which you flee — it will surely meet you﴾. And His saying: ﴿would burden a group﴾ — it is only the group that is burdened by them. And in poetry:

They are burdened by it, so its buttocks weigh it down.

I have not found this poetry. And the buttocks are not burdened by it, rather it is burdened by the buttocks. And al-A'sha said:

You were not in the 'awan war an inexperienced one, when its hot fuel kindled its roots.

Another among the grammarians of Kufa denied what this speaker said, the beginning of "inna" after "ma," and said: that is permissible with "ma" and "man," and with "ma" and "man" it is better than with "alladhi," because "alladhi" does not govern its relative clause, nor is its relative clause governed by it, so it was permitted, and the clause became the referent of "ma," since it does not govern "ma" and "ma" does not govern it. He said: it is good with "ma" and "man," because they may be taken as indefinite or definite as you wish, so you say: "I struck a man, indeed he will stand," and "I struck a man, indeed he is excellent," so "man" and "ma" are taken as such; but with "alladhi" it is worse, because it is not taken as indefinite.

Another among them said regarding His saying: ﴿would burden a group﴾: its burdening of the group is that it weighs them down. He said: the meaning is: "Indeed its keys would make the group lean from its weight," and when you insert the "ba'" you say: "it burdens them," as He said: ﴿Bring me, I will pour upon it molten copper﴾, and the meaning is: "Bring me copper that I may pour upon it." And when you remove the "ba'," you add an alif at the beginning of the verb, as in: ﴿So the pains of childbirth brought her﴾, meaning: "the pains brought her." And a man of the Arabic-speaking people said: "Indeed the group is burdened by its keys," transferring the verb to the keys, as the poet said:

Indeed a lamp, its glory is noble, by which the eye is adorned when it is seen.

Al-Farra' cited this as evidence, and it is the thing by which the eye is adorned. He said: if he heard this as a report, it is a valid reading; otherwise the man was ignorant of the meaning. And one of the Arabs recited to me:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 76 (part 2 of 2):

حتى إذَا ما الْتَأَمَتْ مَوَاصِلُهْ ... ونَاءَ في شقّ الشَّمالِ كَاهِلُهْ [[The two lines are among those recited by some Arabs. Al-Farra' (see his Ma'ani al-Qur'an, p. 242, and Lisan al-Arab, entry: ناء) said, after what we quoted from him regarding the previous piece of evidence: "Some Arabs recited to me: 'Until, when its joints came together, and its shoulder blade leaned toward the left side.' He means: the archer, when he took hold of the bow and drew it back, leaned over to his side, and that is his leaning (nawu') upon it. We think that the Arabs' saying 'ma sa'aka wa-naka' (what grieves you and burdens you) derives from this, and its meaning is: sa'aka wa-an'aka, except that the alif was dropped, because it follows sa'aka, just as the Arabs say: 'I ate food, so it made me pleased (fa-hana'ani) and wholesome (wa-mara'ani).' Its meaning when standing alone is wa-am'ara'ani, but the alif was dropped from it because it follows what has no alif in it."]]
He means: the archer, when he took hold of the bow and drew it back, leaned over it. He said: "We think that the Arabs' saying, 'ma sa'aka wa-naka min dhalika,' means: 'ma sa'aka wa-an'aka min dhalika,' except that the alif was dropped because it follows sa'aka, just as the Arabs say: 'I ate food, so it made me pleased (fa-hana'ani) and wholesome (wa-mara'ani),' whose meaning when standing alone is 'wa-am'ara'ani,' but the alif was dropped from it because it follows what has no alif in it."

This other view regarding the interpretation of His words, ﴿لَتَنُوءُ بِالْعُصْبَةِ﴾ (would weigh down a band of men), is more correct than the other views, for two reasons. The first is that it is an interpretation that agrees with the apparent sense of the revelation. The second is that the reports we have mentioned from the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) came with a meaning close to this, whereas the view of those who said that the meaning is: "Its keys would indeed weigh down a band of men" is merely a redirection by them toward the meaning: "Its keys would indeed be too much for a band of men to rise up with." When it is redirected in that way, it does not contain the indication, as this view does, that what is intended is a report about the great quantity of his treasures. For a band of men may rise up with a few keys or with many. What He, exalted is His praise, intended was a report about the abundance of that, and when the intended meaning is a report about its abundance, there is no doubt that what was said by those whose view we mentioned, that its meaning is "a band of men would be weighed down by its keys," is a view without meaning. This is in addition to its contradicting the interpretation of the early generations (al-salaf) on this matter.

* *

And His words: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ لَهُ قَوْمُهُ لا تَفْرَحْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الْفَرِحِينَ﴾ (When his people said to him: "Do not exult; indeed, Allah does not love those who exult.")

He means: when his people said: "Do not transgress and do not become insolent through exultation; indeed, Allah does not love, among His creatures, the arrogant and the insolent."

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

* Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الْفَرِحِينَ﴾ (indeed, Allah does not love those who exult), he said: "those who are exultant (al-marihin)."
* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasa, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿لا تَفْرَحْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الْفَرِحِينَ﴾ (Do not exult; indeed, Allah does not love those who exult), he said: "the haughty, the arrogant, the insolent, who do not thank Allah for what He has given them."
* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Jabir, who said: I heard Mujahid say regarding this verse, ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الْفَرِحِينَ﴾: "the arrogant, the insolent, the boastful (al-badhikhin)."
* Ya'qub related to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: al-Awwam informed us, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿لا تَفْرَحْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الْفَرِحِينَ﴾, he said: "He means by it transgression (al-baghy)."
* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿لا تَفْرَحْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الْفَرِحِينَ﴾, he said: "the boastful, the arrogant, who do not thank Allah for what He has given them."
* al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it; except that he said: "the boastful (al-mutabadhkhin)."
* Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Makhrami narrated to us, saying: Shababa related to me, saying: Warqa' related to me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿لا تَفْرَحْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الْفَرِحِينَ﴾, he said: "the arrogant, the insolent."
* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿إِذْ قَالَ لَهُ قَوْمُهُ لا تَفْرَحْ﴾ (when his people said to him, "Do not exult"): meaning "do not be exultant (la tamrah)"; ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الْفَرِحِينَ﴾: meaning "indeed, Allah does not love the exultant."
* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿لا تَفْرَحْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الْفَرِحِينَ﴾, he said: "the arrogant, the insolent, who do not thank Allah for what He has given them."
* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: al-Awwam informed us, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ لَهُ قَوْمُهُ لا تَفْرَحْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الْفَرِحِينَ﴾, he said: "it is the exultation of transgression (farah al-baghy)."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 77:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But seek, through that which Allah has given you, the Home of the Hereafter, and do not forget your share of the world. And do good as Allah has done good to you. And seek not corruption in the land. Indeed, Allah does not love corrupters.﴾ (77)

His saying, exalted is He His remembrance, reporting the words of Qarun's people to him: Do not transgress, O Qarun, against your people through the abundance of your wealth. Seek, through the wealth that Allah has given you, the good of the Hereafter, by acting in it in obedience to Allah in this world. As for His saying, ﴿and do not forget your share of the world﴾, it means: do not abandon your portion and your share of the world, such that you take in it only your share of the Hereafter, acting in it by that which will save you tomorrow from the punishment of Allah.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and do not forget your share of the world, and do good as Allah has done good to you﴾, that it means: do not abandon acting for Allah in this world.

- Ibn Wakie narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿and do not forget your share of the world﴾, he said: that you act in it for your Hereafter.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Qurrah ibn Khalid narrated to us, from Awn ibn Abdullah, ﴿and do not forget your share of the world﴾, he said: Indeed, some people place it other than in its proper place. "And do not forget your share of the world": act in it by obedience to Allah.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿and do not forget your share of the world﴾, he said: acting by His obedience.

- Ibn Wakie narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: act in your world for your Hereafter.

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding his saying: ﴿and do not forget your share of the world﴾, he said: acting in it by the obedience of Allah.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

- Ibn Wakie narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Isa al-Jurashi, from Mujahid: ﴿and do not forget your share of the world﴾, he said: that you act in your world for your Hereafter.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Mujahid, who said: acting by the obedience of Allah is his share of the world, for which he is rewarded in the Hereafter.

- Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿and do not forget your share of the world﴾, he said: Do not forget to send forward from your world for your Hereafter, for you will find in your Hereafter what you sent forward in this world, from what Allah has provided you.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: do not abandon seeking your portion of provision in it.

Mention of those who said that:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and do not forget your share of the world﴾: al-Hasan said: what Allah has made lawful for you from it, for you have in it sufficiency and provision.

- Ibn Wakie narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Humayd al-Mu'mari narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and do not forget your share of the world﴾, he said: seeking what is lawful.

- Ibn Wakie narrated to us, saying: Hafs narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿and do not forget your share of the world﴾, he said: send forward the surplus, and keep what suffices you.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: the lawful in it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and do good as Allah has done good to you﴾:

It means: and do good in this world by spending your wealth, which Allah has given you, in its proper channels and ways, just as Allah has done good to you, by widening His provision for you from it and extending it for you therein.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿and do good as Allah has done good to you﴾, he said: do good with what Allah has provided you.

﴿And seek not corruption in the land﴾: it means: do not seek what Allah has forbidden you of transgression against your people.

﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the corrupters﴾: it means: indeed, Allah does not love those who commit transgression and disobedience.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 28, verse 78:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿He said, "I have only been given it on account of knowledge I possess. Did he not know that Allah had already destroyed before him generations who were greater than him in strength and greater in accumulation? And the criminals will not be questioned about their sins."﴾

His, the Exalted's, words mean: Qarun said to his people who admonished him, "I was only given these treasures on account of a superior knowledge I possess, which Allah has taught me, so He was pleased with me and favoured me with this wealth over you, because of His knowledge of my merit over you."

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) have said similarly to what we have said.

Those who said that:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿He said, "I have only been given it on account of knowledge I possess"﴾: "On account of knowledge (khubr) I possess."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿I have only been given it on account of knowledge I possess﴾: "Had it not been for Allah's pleasure with me and His knowledge of my merit, He would not have given me this." And he recited: ﴿Did he not know that Allah had already destroyed before him generations who were greater than him in strength and greater in accumulation?﴾ ... the verse.

It has also been said that the meaning of His words ﴿I possess (ʿindī)﴾ is "in my opinion" (bi-maʿnā: arā), as if he had said: "I was only given it on account of my superior knowledge, in my view."

* *

As for His words: ﴿Did he not know that Allah had already destroyed before him generations who were greater than him in strength and greater in accumulation?﴾

His, the Exalted's, words mean: Did Qarun not know, when he claimed that he was given the treasures on account of a knowledge he possessed which I had taught him, and thereby deserved what he was given of treasures, that Allah had already destroyed, before him, nations that were greater than him in might (baṭsh) and greater in the accumulation of wealth? Had Allah given wealth to whoever He gives it to on account of merit in him and goodness in His sight, and His pleasure with him, He would not have destroyed the possessors of wealth who were greater in wealth than him. For whoever Allah is pleased with, it is impossible that Allah destroys him while He is pleased with him; He only destroys those with whom He is displeased.

As for His words: ﴿And the criminals will not be questioned about their sins﴾, it has been said that the meaning of this is that they will enter the Fire without reckoning.

Those who said that:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Umar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And the criminals will not be questioned about their sins﴾: "They will be made to enter the Fire without reckoning."

It has also been said that the meaning of this is: the angels will not question them, because they recognise them by their marks.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And the criminals will not be questioned about their sins﴾, like His words ﴿The criminals will be recognised by their marks﴾: "Blue-eyed, black-faced. The angels will not question them, for they have already recognised them."

It has also been said that the meaning is: and the criminals will not be questioned about the sins of those whom Allah destroyed from the past nations, as to why they were destroyed.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Ubaydah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, regarding ﴿And the criminals will not be questioned about their sins﴾: "About the sins of those who passed away, as to why they were destroyed?" So the pronoun in His words ﴿about their sins﴾ on this interpretation refers back to the ones in His words ﴿Did he not know that Allah had already destroyed before him generations who were greater than him in strength﴾. On the first interpretation, given by Mujahid and Qatadah, it refers to the criminals, and that is more appropriate to the mention of criminals, because the Exalted is not questioning about the sin of a sinner other than the one who committed it, whether believer or disbeliever. Given that this is so, it is clear that there is no point in restricting it to the criminals, if the pronoun in ﴿about their sins﴾ referred to those in ﴿greater than him in strength﴾, excluding the believers, meaning that neither believer nor disbeliever is questioned about that, except those who committed and acquired (those sins).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 79:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So he went out before his people in his adornment. Those who desired the worldly life said, "Oh, would that we had the like of what Qarun was given! Indeed, he is one of great fortune."﴾ (28:79)

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: "So Qarun went out before his people in his adornment," and it is said that this adornment was garments of crimson (arjuwan).

Those who said this:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Talhah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir: ﴿So he went out before his people in his adornment﴾ He said: "In crimson (al-qirmiz)."

- He said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Mujahid: ﴿So he went out before his people in his adornment﴾ He said: "In red garments."

- Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, from 'Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Mujahid: ﴿So he went out before his people in his adornment﴾ He said: "On white mules (baradhin bid), with saddles of crimson upon them, and they wore safflower-dyed garments (al-mu'asfarat)."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿So he went out before his people in his adornment﴾ He said: "He wore two safflower-dyed garments."

And Ibn Jurayj said: "On a grey-white mule with crimson upon it, and three hundred maidens on grey mules, wearing red garments."

- Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father and Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to me, from Mubarak, from al-Hasan: ﴿So he went out before his people in his adornment﴾ He said: "In red and yellow garments."

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak, that he heard Ibrahim al-Nakha'i say, regarding this verse: ﴿So he went out before his people in his adornment﴾ He said: "In red garments."

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak, from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, the like of it.

- Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ghundar narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak, from Ibrahim, the like of it.

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Ali al-Muqaddami narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Hakim narrated to us, saying: We entered upon Malik ibn Dinar in the evening, and he was mentioning Qarun. There was a man from among his neighbours wearing safflower-dyed garments. Malik said: ﴿So he went out before his people in his adornment﴾ He said: "In garments like the garments of this man."

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿So he went out before his people in his adornment﴾ He said: "It was mentioned to us that they went out on four thousand beasts, upon them and upon their beasts was crimson."

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿So he went out before his people in his adornment﴾ He said: "He went out with seventy thousand, wearing safflower-dyed garments, as my father used to mention to us."

﴿Those who said, "Oh, would that we had the like of what Qarun was given!"⁠﴾ His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: those among the people of Qarun who desired the adornment of the worldly life said: "Oh, would that we were given the like of what Qarun was given of its adornment," ﴿Indeed, he is one of great fortune﴾. He says: indeed Qarun is possessed of a great share of the world.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 28, verses 80–81:

The explanation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And those who had been given knowledge said, "Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for one who believes and does righteousness; and none is granted it except the patient."﴾

God, may He be remembered, says: And those who had been given knowledge of God said, when they saw Qarun going out before them in his adornment, to those who had said, "Oh, if only we had the like of what Qarun has been given": "Woe to you! Fear Allah and obey Him. The reward and recompense of Allah is for those who believe in Him and in His messengers, and act by the righteous deeds brought by His messengers, in the Hereafter, is better than what Qarun was given of his adornment and wealth."

* *

As for His words: ﴿and none is granted it except the patient﴾

He says: "None is granted it", meaning: none is given success in uttering this statement, which is His words: ﴿The reward of Allah is better for one who believes and does righteousness﴾. The pronoun "ha' and alif" refers to the statement. And His words ﴿except the patient﴾ mean: those who are patient in refraining from seeking the adornment of the worldly life, and who prefer what is with Allah of abundant reward for righteous deeds over the pleasures and desires of this world, so they strive diligently in obedience to Allah and renounce the worldly life.

* *

The explanation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. Then he had no company to support him against Allah, nor was he among those who could defend themselves.﴾

God, may He be remembered, says: We caused the earth to swallow Qarun and the people of his house. It has been said: "and his house" (wa-bidarihi), because it is mentioned that when Musa commanded the earth to seize him, it obeyed him and seized him and those among his companions who were in his house, and they were a group sitting with him, and they were on the same hypocrisy as he was and in supporting him in harming Musa.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash informed us, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When zakat was revealed, Qarun came to Musa and reached an agreement with him that for every thousand dinars he would give one dinar, and for every thousand of anything, one of it, or he said: and for every thousand sheep, one sheep [Al-Tabari is uncertain]. He said: Then he went to his house, reckoned it, and found it abundant. So he gathered the Children of Israel and said: "O Children of Israel, Musa has commanded you in everything and you have obeyed him, and now he wants to take from your wealth." They said: "You are our elder and our master, so command us as you wish." He said: "I command you to bring that prostitute So-and-so, and offer her a reward so that she will accuse him to his face." So they summoned her and offered her a reward on condition that she would accuse him to his face. Then he went to Musa and said to Musa: "The Children of Israel have gathered so that you may command them and forbid them." So he went out to them while they were in an open land, and said: "O Children of Israel, whoever steals, we will cut off his hand; whoever slanders, we will flog him; whoever commits fornication while not married, we will flog him a hundred times; whoever commits fornication while married, we will flog him until he dies, or stone him until he dies" [al-Tabari is uncertain]. Qarun said to him: "Even if you were the one?" He said: "Even if I were the one." He said: "The Children of Israel claim that you committed fornication with So-and-so." He said: "Call her. If she says so, then it is as she says." So when she came, Musa said to her: "O So-and-so," she said: "Here I am, at your service." He said: "Did I do to you what these people say?" She said: "No, and they lied; rather, they gave me a reward on condition that I accuse you to your face." So he leapt, prostrated, while among them, and Allah revealed to him: "Command the earth as you wish." He said: "O earth, seize them!" So it seized them to their feet. Then he said: "O earth, seize them!" So it seized them to their knees. Then he said: "O earth, seize them!" So it seized them to their waists [al-Haqw: the place where the waistband is tied; its plurals are ahuqq, ahqa', and huqy (with a doubled yaa), and huqa' (Lisan al-Arab: haqa)]. Then he said: "O earth, seize them!" So it seized them to their necks. He said: They began to say: "O Musa, O Musa," and to beseech him. He said: "O earth, seize them!" So it closed over them. Then Allah revealed to him: "O Musa, My servants are saying: 'O Musa, O Musa,' so you will not have mercy on them? Had they called upon Me, they would have found Me near and responsive." He said: That is the saying of Allah: ﴿So he went out before his people in his adornment﴾, and his adornment was that he went out on sorrel mounts with red saddles, wearing garments dyed with bahraman [al-Bahraman, with fatha on the ba' and ra': safflower or a kind of it (Lisan al-Arab: bahram)].

﴿Those who desired the worldly life said, "Oh, if only we had the like of what Qarun has been given..."﴾ until His words: ﴿Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed.﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿That home of the Hereafter We make for those who do not desire haughtiness upon the earth or corruption, and the [best] outcome is for the righteous.﴾

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn 'Isa narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from a man, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Allah commanded Musa concerning zakat, they accused him of fornication. He was distressed by that, so they sent to a woman to whom they had given a reward, on condition that she would accuse him herself. When she came, it weighed heavily upon her, and he (Musa) adjured her by the One who split the sea for the Children of Israel and sent down the Torah to Musa, to speak the truth. She said: "Since you have made me swear, I bear witness that you are innocent and that you are the Messenger of Allah." So he fell prostrate, weeping. Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed: "What makes you weep? We have empowered you over the earth, so command it as you wish." He said: "Seize them!" So it seized them as far as Allah willed. They said: "O Musa, O Musa," and he said: "Seize them!" So it seized them as far as Allah willed. They said: "O Musa, O Musa," and it swallowed them up. He said: Afterwards, the Children of Israel suffered hardship and severe hunger, so they came to Musa and said: "Pray to your Lord for us." He prayed for them, and Allah revealed to him: "O Musa, do you speak to Me about a people whose sins have darkened what is between Me and them? They called upon you and you did not answer them. As for Me, had they called upon Me, I would have answered them."

Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾: It was said to the earth: "Seize them!" So it seized them to their heels. Then it was said to it: "Seize them!" So it seized them to their knees. Then it was said to it: "Seize them!" So it seized them to their waists. Then it was said to it: "Seize them!" So it seized them to their necks. Then it was said to it: "Seize them!" So it swallowed them, and that is His saying: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Hashim ibn al-Barid narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿Indeed, Qarun was of the people of Musa﴾: He was his paternal cousin. Musa used to judge in one part of the Children of Israel, and Qarun in another part. He summoned a prostitute among the Children of Israel and offered her a reward on condition that she would throw herself at Musa. Then, when the day came when the Children of Israel gathered before Musa, Qarun came to him and said: "O Musa, what is the punishment for theft?" He said: "That his hand be cut off." He said: "Even if it is you?" He said: "Yes." He said: "What is the punishment for fornication?" He said: "That he be stoned." He said: "Even if it is you?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then you have done it." He said: "Woe to you, with whom?" He said: "With So-and-so." So Musa summoned her and said: "I adjure you by the One who sent down the Torah, did Qarun speak the truth?" She said: "O Allah, since you have adjured me, I bear witness that you are innocent, and that you are the Messenger of Allah, and that the enemy of Allah, Qarun, offered me a reward on condition that I accuse you to your face." He said: So Musa leapt up, and fell prostrate before Allah. Allah revealed to him: "Raise your head, for I have commanded the earth to obey you." Musa said: "O earth, seize them!" So it seized them until they reached the waistband. He said: "O Musa!" He said: "Seize them!" So it seized them until they reached the chests. He said: "O Musa!" He said: "Seize them!" He said: So they vanished. He said: Then Allah revealed to him: "O Musa, he sought your help and you did not help him. Had he sought My help, I would have answered him and helped him."

Bishr ibn Hilal al-Sawwaf narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman al-Dab'i narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith went out from the house, and entered the enclosure; when he came out from it, he sat down and leaned upon it, and we sat with him. He mentioned Sulayman ibn Dawud: ﴿He said, "O chiefs, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?"﴾ until His words: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Free of need and Generous.﴾ Then he fell silent about the mention of Sulayman and said: ﴿Indeed, Qarun was of the people of Musa, but he oppressed them﴾, and he had been given of the treasures what Allah mentioned in His Book: ﴿Indeed, its keys would burden a band of strong men﴾, ﴿He said, "I was only given it on knowledge I have"﴾. He said: He was hostile to Musa, and harmed him, and Musa used to overlook it and forgive him, out of kinship, until he built a house, and made its door of gold, and covered its walls with sheets of gold. The nobles of the Children of Israel would visit him morning and evening, and he would feed them, and they would talk with him and make him laugh. Then misfortune and calamity did not leave him, until he sent to a woman among the Children of Israel known for immorality and for abuse, and he sent for her and she came to him. He said to her: "Would you like me to make you wealthy and give you gifts, and join you with my women, on condition that you come to me while the nobles of the Children of Israel are with me, and say: 'O Qarun, do you not forbid Musa from me?'" She said: "Yes." When Qarun sat, and the nobles of the Children of Israel came, he sent for her, and she came and stood before him. Then Allah turned her heart and granted her repentance, and she said to herself: "Repenting today is better for me than harming the Messenger of Allah, ﷺ, and falsely accusing the enemy of Allah against him." So she said: "Qarun told me: 'Would you like me to make you wealthy and give you gifts, and join you with my women, on condition that you come to me while the nobles of the Children of Israel are with me, and say: O Qarun, do you not forbid Musa from me?' I found no repentance better than not harming the Messenger of Allah, ﷺ, and falsely accusing the enemy of Allah." When she spoke these words, Qarun was overcome with dismay, bowed his head, and the nobles fell silent, realizing he had fallen into ruin. Her words spread among the people until they reached Musa. When it reached Musa, his anger intensified, so he performed ablution with water, prayed, wept, and said: "O Lord, Your enemy harms me; he wanted to disgrace me and defame me. O Lord, empower me over him." So Allah revealed to him: "Command the earth as you wish, and it will obey you." Musa came to Qarun, and when he entered upon him, Qarun recognized the evil in Musa's face toward him, and said: "O Musa, have mercy on me." He said: "O earth, seize them!" He said: So his house shook, and it sank with Qarun and his companions up to the ankles, and he began to say: "O Musa!" So it seized them to their knees, while he beseeched Musa: "O Musa, have mercy on me." He said: "O earth, seize them!" He said: So his house shook and sank, and Qarun and his companions were swallowed up to their couches, while he beseeched Musa: "O Musa, have mercy on me." He said: "O earth, seize them!" So he was swallowed up with his house and his companions. He said: It was said to Musa, ﷺ: "O Musa, how harsh you are! By My might, had he called upon Me, I would have answered him."

Bishr ibn Hilal narrated to me, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Abu 'Imran al-Jawni, who said: It reached me that it was said to Musa: "I will never be worshipped by the earth after you, ever."

Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi and 'Abd al-Hamid al-Himmani narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Aghar ibn al-Sabbah, from Khalifa ibn Husayn; 'Abd al-Hamid added: from Abu Nasr, from Ibn 'Abbas, and Ibn Mahdi did not mention Abu Nasr, concerning ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾: "The seventh earth."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: It reached us that he is swallowed each day by a hundred cubits, and he will not reach the bottom of the earth until the Day of Resurrection; he will keep sinking therein until the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Habban narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Sulayman, who said: I heard Malik ibn Dinar say: It reached me that Qarun is swallowed each day by a hundred cubits.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾: It was mentioned that he is swallowed each day by a cubit, and that he keeps sinking therein, not reaching its bottom until the Day of Resurrection.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Then he had no company to support him against Allah﴾

He says: He had no army to turn to, nor a company to support him when the wrath of Allah descended upon him; rather, they disowned him.

﴿Nor was he among those who could defend themselves﴾: He says: Nor was he one who could defend himself against Allah when His vengeance befell him, so that his strength would protect him from it.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 28, verses 80–81:

The explanation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And those who had been given knowledge said, "Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for one who believes and does righteousness; and none is granted it except the patient."﴾

God, may He be remembered, says: And those who had been given knowledge of God said, when they saw Qarun going out before them in his adornment, to those who had said, "Oh, if only we had the like of what Qarun has been given": "Woe to you! Fear Allah and obey Him. The reward and recompense of Allah is for those who believe in Him and in His messengers, and act by the righteous deeds brought by His messengers, in the Hereafter, is better than what Qarun was given of his adornment and wealth."

* *

As for His words: ﴿and none is granted it except the patient﴾

He says: "None is granted it", meaning: none is given success in uttering this statement, which is His words: ﴿The reward of Allah is better for one who believes and does righteousness﴾. The pronoun "ha' and alif" refers to the statement. And His words ﴿except the patient﴾ mean: those who are patient in refraining from seeking the adornment of the worldly life, and who prefer what is with Allah of abundant reward for righteous deeds over the pleasures and desires of this world, so they strive diligently in obedience to Allah and renounce the worldly life.

* *

The explanation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. Then he had no company to support him against Allah, nor was he among those who could defend themselves.﴾

God, may He be remembered, says: We caused the earth to swallow Qarun and the people of his house. It has been said: "and his house" (wa-bidarihi), because it is mentioned that when Musa commanded the earth to seize him, it obeyed him and seized him and those among his companions who were in his house, and they were a group sitting with him, and they were on the same hypocrisy as he was and in supporting him in harming Musa.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash informed us, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When zakat was revealed, Qarun came to Musa and reached an agreement with him that for every thousand dinars he would give one dinar, and for every thousand of anything, one of it, or he said: and for every thousand sheep, one sheep [Al-Tabari is uncertain]. He said: Then he went to his house, reckoned it, and found it abundant. So he gathered the Children of Israel and said: "O Children of Israel, Musa has commanded you in everything and you have obeyed him, and now he wants to take from your wealth." They said: "You are our elder and our master, so command us as you wish." He said: "I command you to bring that prostitute So-and-so, and offer her a reward so that she will accuse him to his face." So they summoned her and offered her a reward on condition that she would accuse him to his face. Then he went to Musa and said to Musa: "The Children of Israel have gathered so that you may command them and forbid them." So he went out to them while they were in an open land, and said: "O Children of Israel, whoever steals, we will cut off his hand; whoever slanders, we will flog him; whoever commits fornication while not married, we will flog him a hundred times; whoever commits fornication while married, we will flog him until he dies, or stone him until he dies" [al-Tabari is uncertain]. Qarun said to him: "Even if you were the one?" He said: "Even if I were the one." He said: "The Children of Israel claim that you committed fornication with So-and-so." He said: "Call her. If she says so, then it is as she says." So when she came, Musa said to her: "O So-and-so," she said: "Here I am, at your service." He said: "Did I do to you what these people say?" She said: "No, and they lied; rather, they gave me a reward on condition that I accuse you to your face." So he leapt, prostrated, while among them, and Allah revealed to him: "Command the earth as you wish." He said: "O earth, seize them!" So it seized them to their feet. Then he said: "O earth, seize them!" So it seized them to their knees. Then he said: "O earth, seize them!" So it seized them to their waists [al-Haqw: the place where the waistband is tied; its plurals are ahuqq, ahqa', and huqy (with a doubled yaa), and huqa' (Lisan al-Arab: haqa)]. Then he said: "O earth, seize them!" So it seized them to their necks. He said: They began to say: "O Musa, O Musa," and to beseech him. He said: "O earth, seize them!" So it closed over them. Then Allah revealed to him: "O Musa, My servants are saying: 'O Musa, O Musa,' so you will not have mercy on them? Had they called upon Me, they would have found Me near and responsive." He said: That is the saying of Allah: ﴿So he went out before his people in his adornment﴾, and his adornment was that he went out on sorrel mounts with red saddles, wearing garments dyed with bahraman [al-Bahraman, with fatha on the ba' and ra': safflower or a kind of it (Lisan al-Arab: bahram)].

﴿Those who desired the worldly life said, "Oh, if only we had the like of what Qarun has been given..."﴾ until His words: ﴿Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed.﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿That home of the Hereafter We make for those who do not desire haughtiness upon the earth or corruption, and the [best] outcome is for the righteous.﴾

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn 'Isa narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from a man, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Allah commanded Musa concerning zakat, they accused him of fornication. He was distressed by that, so they sent to a woman to whom they had given a reward, on condition that she would accuse him herself. When she came, it weighed heavily upon her, and he (Musa) adjured her by the One who split the sea for the Children of Israel and sent down the Torah to Musa, to speak the truth. She said: "Since you have made me swear, I bear witness that you are innocent and that you are the Messenger of Allah." So he fell prostrate, weeping. Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed: "What makes you weep? We have empowered you over the earth, so command it as you wish." He said: "Seize them!" So it seized them as far as Allah willed. They said: "O Musa, O Musa," and he said: "Seize them!" So it seized them as far as Allah willed. They said: "O Musa, O Musa," and it swallowed them up. He said: Afterwards, the Children of Israel suffered hardship and severe hunger, so they came to Musa and said: "Pray to your Lord for us." He prayed for them, and Allah revealed to him: "O Musa, do you speak to Me about a people whose sins have darkened what is between Me and them? They called upon you and you did not answer them. As for Me, had they called upon Me, I would have answered them."

He said: "Even if it is you?" He said: "Yes." He said: "What is the punishment for fornication?" He said: "That he be stoned." He said: "Even if it is you?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then you have done it." He said: "Woe to you, with whom?" He said: "With So-and-so." So Musa summoned her and said: "I adjure you by the One who sent down the Torah, did Qarun speak the truth?" So it seized them until they reached the waistband. He said: "O Musa!" He said: "Seize them!" So it seized them until they reached the chests. He said: "O Musa!" He said: "Seize them!" He said: So they vanished. He said: Then Allah revealed to him: "O Musa, he sought your help and you did not help him. Had he sought My help, I would have answered him and helped him."

Bishr ibn Hilal al-Sawwaf narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman al-Dab'i narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith went out from the house, and entered the enclosure; when he came out from it, he sat down and leaned upon it, and we sat with him.
