The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 28, Verse 82:

Discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And those who had longed for his position the day before began to say, "Ah! It is as if Allah extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it. Had Allah not been gracious to us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us. Ah! It is as if the disbelievers will never prosper."﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying: "And those who had longed for his position the day before", meaning those who had longed for his worldly station, his wealth, and the abundance of his property, which had been granted to him the day before, before there came upon him what came of the wrath and punishment of Allah, "began to say: Ah! It is as if Allah..."

Scholars differed regarding the meaning of ﴿Wayka'anna Allah﴾ (Ah! It is as if Allah). As for Qatadah, two statements have been related from him on this matter. The first is:

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Uthmah related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Bashir related to us, from Qatadah, who said concerning His saying ﴿Wayka'annahu﴾: "Did you not see that..." (alam tara annahu).

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿Wayka'annahu﴾: "Do you not see that..." (awa la tara annahu).

* Isma'il ibn al-Mutawakkil al-Ashja'i related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Kathir related to us, saying: Ma'mar related to me, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿Wayka'annahu﴾: "Did you not see that..." (alam tara annahu).

The second statement is:

* al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Abu Sufyan related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿Wayka'anna Allaha yabsutu al-rizq﴾: "Or did he not know that Allah..." ﴿Wayka'annahu﴾: "Or does he not know that..." (aw la ya'lamu annahu).

Some scholars of the Arabic language from Basra also adopted this interpretation of Qatadah, and they cited as evidence for the soundness of this interpretation the verse of the poet:

"They asked me for divorce when they saw me, [saying]: 'My wealth has diminished, you have brought something repugnant.'
'Wayka'anna man yakun lahu nashbun yuhabb, wa man yaftaqir ya'ish 'aysha darr.'"

[[The two verses belong to Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl (Khizanat al-Adab al-Kubra of al-Baghdadi, 3:95-97), and before them there is a third verse, which is: "Those two wives of mine speak, over a long period until today, with false speech and slander."

The poet denies the condition of his two wives with him after he grew old and became poor. In the second verse: "That they saw my wealth as little..." etc. "Al-Ars" means the wife. "Al-Hatr" with a fatha on the ha is the verbal noun of hatara yahturuhu hatran (of the pattern nasara): when one tears his honour. With a kasra on the ha it means lying, a calamity, and a strange matter, a slip in speech, and an error in it. With a damma it means loss of reason due to old age, illness, or grief. "Al-Nukr" is an ugly, objectionable matter. "Al-Nashb" is original wealth, both movable and immovable. The evidence lies in the phrase "Wayka'annahu," regarding which the Basran and Kufan grammarians differed: is it one word or two? Sibawayh said: I asked al-Khalil about the saying of the Exalted, "Wayka'annahu la yuflihu al-kafirun" and about His saying "Wayka'anna Allah," and he claimed that they are: "Way" separated from "ka'anna." The meaning is that the people became alert and spoke according to their knowledge, or were admonished, and it was said to them: Does it not seem to you that this is so? Al-Farra' said in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (manuscript of the Jami'a, folio 243): "Wayka'anna..." in the speech of the Arabs is affirmation, like a man's saying: Do you not see the handiwork of Allah? And he recited to me: "Wayka'anna man yakun..." the verse. And a shaykh from Basra told me, saying: I heard a Bedouin woman say to her husband: "Where is your son, woe to you?" He said: "Wayka'annahu is behind the tent," meaning: "Do you not see him behind the tent?" ... to the end of what the author transmitted from him. I say: What Khalil and Sibawayh said in terms of the wording is closer to the truth, because the word is composed of three elements: wayy, the kaf, and anna. What al-Farra' said in terms of meaning is good and clear.]]

Some grammarians of Kufa said: "Wayka'anna" in the speech of the Arabs is affirmation, like a man's saying: Do you not see the handiwork and goodness of Allah? He mentioned that he was informed by one who heard a Bedouin woman say to her husband: "Where is our son?" He said: "Wayka'annahu is behind the tent." Its meaning: "Do you not see him behind the tent?" He said: Some grammarians take it that they are two words, meaning: wayka anna hu, as if he intended: "Woe to you" (waylaka), so the lam was dropped, and "anna" is then read with a fatha, governed by a concealed verb, as if he said: "Woe to you, know that he is behind the tent," with the verb "i'lam" (know) concealed.

He said: We have not found the Arabs making the verb of opinion or knowledge, or its like, operative on "anna" when it is concealed, for it is nullified when it is placed between the two words or at the end of the word. So when it is concealed, it takes the place of the one that comes later. Do you not see that it is not permissible at the beginning to say: "O you, that you are standing," or "O you, that you have stood," meaning "I know," or "I think"? As for dropping the lam from your saying "Woe to you" until it becomes "Wayk," the Arabs do say it, due to its frequency in speech. 'Antarah said:

"And indeed the saying of the horsemen has healed my soul and cured its sickness: 'Wayka, 'Antar, advance!'"

[[The verse belongs to 'Antarah ibn 'Amr ibn Shaddad al-'Absi, from his mu'allaqah (Mukhtar al-Shi'r al-Jahili by Mustafa al-Saqqa, p. 379). Its commentator said: He means that his companions' reliance upon him and their seeking refuge in him healed his soul and removed his grief. Wayy is a word uttered by one who is amazed at something; it is primary and biliteral in its formation, for it is among the onomatopoeic words, then it became a verb-name (ism fi'l), and the kaf of address may enter it, and they may add a lam to it, making it "wayl," or a ha, making it "wayh." The first is used in warning of evil, and the second in expressing compassion. So one says "waylaka," "waykha," "waysaka," and "waybaka," like "waylaka." His transmission of the verse here is like his transmission in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an (p. 243), for he transmitted it in his speech that the author quoted, and mentioned this evidence therein. In Mukhtar al-Shi'r it is said: al-Fawaris (the horsemen): in some versions "qawl al-fawaris," and both mean the same.]]

He said: Others said: the meaning of His saying "Wayka'anna" is: "Way" separated from "ka'anna," like your saying to a man: "Way! Do you not see what is before you?" Then he said "way," and then resumed: "as if Allah extends provision," and it is an expression of wonder, and "ka'anna" has the meaning of opinion and knowledge. This is a view that is sound. He said: The Arabs did not write them separately; if it were so, they would have written them separately. It may be that the speech with it became frequent, so it was joined to what is not part of it.

Another of them said: "Wayy" is an alert, and "ka'anna" is a different particle, meaning: "Perhaps the matter is such," "I think the matter is such," because "ka'anna" holds the position of "azunnu," "uhsibu," and "a'lamu."

The most correct of these interpretations is the statement related from Qatadah, that its meaning is: "Did you not see? Did you not know?" for the evidence we cited from the poet's verse and the transmission from the Arabs; and that "Wayka'anna" in the script of the Mushaf is one letter-group. If it were directed to other than the interpretation we related from Qatadah, it would become two words. For if it were directed to the view of one who interpreted it as "Woe to you, know that Allah..." it would be necessary to separate "wayka" from "anna," which contradicts the script of all the Mushafs, along with its incorrectness in Arabic for the reasons we mentioned. And if it were directed to the view of one who says "wayy" means alertness, then the speech resumed with "ka'anna," it would be necessary to separate "wayy" from "ka'anna," which is likewise contrary to the scripts of all the Mushafs [[I say: It is strange that the author, despite his imamate and the height of his standing in knowledge, makes the orthography of the Mushafs a proof of meaning, when the Mushafs' orthography differs clearly, and differences in meaning have no bearing on that orthography; it was due to other causes.]].

Since this is one word, the correct interpretation is what Qatadah said. Given that this is the correct view, the meaning of the speech is: And those who had longed for Qarun's place and position in the world the day before began to say, when they witnessed what Allah had brought upon him of His vengeance: "Did you not see that Allah extends provision to whom He wills of His servants, widening it for him, not for the excellence of his station with Him, nor for his honour before Him, just as He had extended such provision to Qarun, not for his excellence nor for his honour before Him." ﴿And restricts﴾ means: He narrows it upon whom He wills of His creation and constricts it for him, not out of his humiliation, nor out of His anger at his deeds.

* *

His saying: ﴿Had Allah not been gracious to us﴾

means: Had He not bestowed favour upon us, turning away from us what we had longed for the day before, ﴿He would have caused the earth to swallow us.﴾

The readers differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the readers of the cities, except Shaybah, recited it as "lakhusifa bina" with a damma on the kha and a kasra on the sin (lakhusifa bina, passive). It is related from Shaybah and al-Hasan: ﴿lakhasafa bina﴾ with a fatha on the kha and the sin, meaning: Allah would have caused the earth to swallow us.

* *

His saying: ﴿Ah! It is as if the disbelievers will never prosper﴾

means: Do you not know that the disbelievers do not prosper, so that their requests succeed?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 83:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is the Abode of the Hereafter. We assign it to those who do not desire haughtiness on earth or corruption. And the good outcome is for the righteous.﴾ (28:83)

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: That is the Abode of the Hereafter; We assign its bliss to those who do not desire arrogance against the truth on earth, or tyranny against it, nor corruption. He says: nor wronging people without right, nor acting in disobedience to God therein.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Abi Ziyad, who said: I heard ʿIkrimah say: ﴿do not desire haughtiness on earth or corruption﴾. He said: "Haughtiness" (al-ʿuluw): arrogance.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Muslim al-Batin: ﴿That is the Abode of the Hereafter; We assign it to those who do not desire haughtiness on earth or corruption﴾. He said: "Haughtiness": pride in what is not the truth; and "corruption": taking by other than right.

Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Muslim al-Batin: ﴿to those who do not desire haughtiness on earth﴾. He said: pride on earth without right. ﴿Nor corruption﴾: taking wealth without right.

He said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ashʿath, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr: ﴿to those who do not desire haughtiness on earth﴾. He said: transgression (al-baghy).

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying: ﴿to those who do not desire haughtiness on earth﴾. He said: magnifying oneself and tyranny. ﴿Nor corruption﴾: acting in acts of disobedience.

Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Ashʿath al-Samman, from Abu Salman al-Aʿraj, from ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: Indeed a man may be pleased that the strap of his sandal is finer than his companion's strap, and so he falls under His saying: ﴿That is the Abode of the Hereafter; We assign it to those who do not desire haughtiness on earth or corruption. And the good outcome is for the righteous.﴾

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the good outcome is for the righteous﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: "And the Garden is for the righteous," those who guard against disobedience to God and perform His obligations.

The people of interpretation have said similarly to what we have said regarding the meaning of "the outcome" (al-ʿaqibah).

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And the good outcome is for the righteous﴾, meaning the Garden is for the righteous.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 84:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it, and whoever comes with an evil deed—those who did evil deeds will not be recompensed except according to what they used to do.﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Whoever comes to God on the Day of Resurrection with sincere monotheism (ikhlas al-tawhid), for him is good, and that good is Paradise and lasting bliss. And whoever comes with an evil deed, which is associating partners with God (shirk).

As:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it﴾, meaning: he will have from it a share of good. The good deed is sincerity (al-ikhlas), and the evil deed is shirk.

We have already explained this with the differing views of those who differ, and we have indicated the correct position regarding it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Those who did evil deeds will not be recompensed﴾

He says: those who did evil deeds will not be rewarded for their evil deeds, ﴿except according to what they used to do﴾, meaning: except the recompense of what they used to do.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 28, verse 85:

The interpretation of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an will surely return you to a place of return. Say, "My Lord knows best who has come with guidance and who is in clear error."﴾ (28:85)

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Indeed, He who sent down to you, O Muhammad, the Qur'an.

As related:

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an﴾ he said: He who gave you the Qur'an.

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God: ﴿Indeed, He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an﴾ he said: He who gave it to you.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of His words: ﴿will surely return you to a place of return﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is: to your destination in Paradise.

Those who said that:

* Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Habib ibn al-Shahid narrated to me, saying: Attab ibn Bashir narrated to us, from Khusayf, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿will surely return you to a place of return﴾ he said: to your origin ("ma'dan") in Paradise.

* Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from a man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: To Paradise.

* Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, from Ibrahim ibn Hayyan, I heard Abu Ja'far, from Ibn Abbas, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: ﴿will surely return you to a place of return﴾ he said: its return is its afterlife, Paradise.

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, regarding ﴿Indeed, He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an will surely return you to a place of return﴾ he said: to Paradise, so that He may question you about the Qur'an.

* Abu Kurayb and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, who said: Paradise.

* Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Abu Salih: ﴿will surely return you to a place of return﴾ he said: to Paradise.

* Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, who said: He will return you to Paradise, then He will question you about the Qur'an.

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Ikrimah and Mujahid, both said: To Paradise.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumayla narrated to us, from Abu Hamza, from Jabir, from Ikrimah, Ata', Mujahid, Abu Qaza'a and al-Hasan, who said: The Day of Resurrection.

* He said: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿will surely return you to a place of return﴾ he said: He will bring you on the Day of Resurrection.

* He said: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan and al-Zuhri, who both said: its return is on the Day of Resurrection.

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding his saying: ﴿will surely return you to a place of return﴾ he said: He will bring you on the Day of Resurrection.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hawdha narrated to us, saying: Awn narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿will surely return you to a place of return﴾ he said: your return from the Hereafter.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿will surely return you to a place of return﴾ he said: al-Hasan used to say: Indeed, by God, He has indeed a return for him, which God will resurrect him to on the Day of Resurrection, and will admit him into Paradise.

Others said: the meaning of that is: will surely return you to death.

Those who said that:

* Ishaq ibn Wahb al-Wasiti narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Zubayri narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Sa'id al-Thawri narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿will surely return you to a place of return﴾ he said: Death.

* Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from a man, from Ibn Abbas, who said: To death.

* He said: my father narrated to us, from Israil, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, from Sa'id: ﴿will surely return you to a place of return﴾ he said: To death.

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from one who heard Ibn Abbas, who said: To death.

* Abu Kurayb and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: To death.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from a man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His saying: ﴿will surely return you to a place of return﴾ he said: Death.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumayla narrated to us, from Abu Hamza, from Jabir, from Adi ibn Thabit, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who both said: To death, or to Mecca.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: will surely return you to the place from which you departed, which is Mecca.

Those who said that:

* Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ya'la ibn Ubayd narrated to us, from Sufyan al-Usfuri, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿will surely return you to a place of return﴾ he said: To Mecca.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿will surely return you to a place of return﴾ he said: He says: will surely return you to Mecca, just as He brought you out of it.

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq informed us, from Mujahid, who said: his birthplace is Mecca.

* Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq, who said: I heard Mujahid say: ﴿will surely return you to a place of return﴾ he said: To your birthplace in Mecca.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Amr, that is Ibn Abi Ishaq, narrated to us, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an will surely return you to a place of return﴾ he said: To your birthplace in Mecca.

* al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Sada'i narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to us, from al-Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from Mujahid Abu al-Hajjaj, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an will surely return you to a place of return﴾ he said: To his birthplace in Mecca.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Isa ibn Yunus narrated to me, from his father, from Mujahid, who said: To your birthplace in Mecca.

The most correct statement on this matter, in my view, is the statement of those who said: will surely return you to your customary place of death, or to your customary place where you were born. This is because the word "ma'ad" in this context is a noun of place derived from "al-'ada" (custom), not from "al-'awd" (return). Unless one who interprets the words ﴿will surely return you﴾ as meaning "to your destination," in which case the words ﴿to a place of return﴾ would then carry the sense of return, and its interpretation would be: Indeed, He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an will surely bring you to your destination of returning to Mecca conquered for you.

If someone says: We have understood these meanings you have described, so what is the interpretation of those who explained it as meaning "will return you to Paradise"? It is said: its interpretation should be the same as this other aspect, namely, "to your destination of returning to Paradise."

If someone says: Was he expelled from Paradise, so that it is said to him: We will return you to it? It is said: For that there are two aspects. The first: if his father Adam, peace be upon them both, was expelled from it, then his descendants, by God's expulsion of him from it, were also expelled from it; so whoever enters it is, as it were, returned to it after the expulsion. The second: it is said that he ﷺ entered it on the night of the Isra' (Night Journey), as it is related from him that he said: "I entered Paradise and saw in it a palace, and I said: For whom is this? They said: For Umar ibn al-Khattab." And similar reports related from him to that effect. Then he was returned to the earth. So it is said to him: Indeed, He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an will surely return you to your destination, to the place from which you came out of Paradise, until you return to it. This, God willing, is the statement of those who said that.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Say, "My Lord knows best who has come with guidance"﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists: My Lord knows best who has come with the guidance, whoever follows it is saved, and who is in deviation from the right path, from us and from you.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿clear﴾

He means that it makes clear to the thinking person, when he contemplates and reflects upon it, that it is error and deviation from guidance.

The exegesis of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And you did not expect that the Book would be bestowed upon you, except as a mercy from your Lord. So never be a supporter of the disbelievers.﴾ (28:86)

Almighty God says: And you were not expecting, O Muhammad, that this Qur'an would be sent down to you, so that you would learn the news and reports about those who passed before you, and the events after you, of what had not yet occurred and what you had not witnessed and do not witness, and then recite that to your people from Quraysh. But your Lord showed you mercy and sent it down to you. So His words ﴿except as a mercy from your Lord﴾ are an exception that is disconnected (istithna' munqati', an exception not of the same kind as what precedes it).

* *

As for His words ﴿So never be a supporter of the disbelievers﴾:

He says: So praise your Lord for what He has bestowed upon you of His mercy toward you, by sending down this Book to you, and do not be a helper to those who disbelieve in your Lord in their disbelief in Him. It has also been said that this is one of the inverted expressions (al-mu'akhkhar alladhi ma'nahu al-taqdim), meaning that the letter lam (in the phrase) indicates: the One who imposed the Qur'an upon you sent it down to you, and you were not expecting that it would be sent down to you, so that you would be a prophet before that, returning you to a place of return (ma'ad).

* *

The exegesis of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And let them not turn you away from the signs of God after they have been sent down to you. And call to your Lord, and do not be among the polytheists.﴾ (28:87)

Almighty God says: And let them not divert you, O Muhammad, from conveying the signs and proofs of God after your Lord has sent them down to you, these polytheists, by their saying: ﴿Why was he not given the like of what was given to Moses?﴾ And call to your Lord, and convey His message to those to whom He sent you with it. ﴿And do not be among the polytheists﴾ means: do not abandon calling to your Lord and conveying His message to the polytheists, so that you would be among those who act as the polytheists act by disobeying their Lord and opposing His command.

The interpretation of His word, the Exalted: ﴿And do not invoke with Allah another god. There is no god but Him. Everything will perish except His Face. To Him belongs the judgment, and to Him you will be returned.﴾ (28:87–88)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And do not worship, O Muhammad, alongside your Lord, to whom all worship belongs, any other object of worship besides Him."

* *

And His word: ﴿There is no god but Him﴾

He says: there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, "Everything will perish except His Face."

Scholars differed over the meaning of His words ﴿except His Face﴾. Some said: its meaning is, "Everything will perish except Him."

Others said: the meaning is "except what is intended by His Face," and they cited in support of this interpretation the verse of the poet:

*"I seek forgiveness from Allah for a sin I cannot count,*
*The Lord of the servants, to Him are the face and the deed."* [[The verse is one of the fifty poetic lines cited by Sibawayh, whose composer is unknown. Grammarians cite it as evidence that the original form was "astaghfiru Allaha min dhanbin" ("I seek forgiveness from Allah for a sin"), after which the preposition was dropped, the genitive noun became attached to the verb, and it was put in the accusative as a direct object. The author cites it here following al-Farra' in his Ma'ani al-Qur'an (photographic copy held by the university, folio 244), where he said: "(Everything will perish except His Face): except Him." And he said regarding the poetry, "I seek forgiveness from Allah…" the verse, meaning: "I direct my deed."]]

* *

And His word: ﴿To Him belongs the judgment﴾

He says: judgment among His creatures belongs to Him alone, with no one other than Him sharing in judging them. ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾: He says, "To Him you will be returned after your deaths, and He will judge between you with justice, rewarding your believers with their recompense and requiting your disbelievers with what He has promised them."

Tafsir of Surah al-'Ankabut
